sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 3Poster Number:NSS-01-003] Development of a Monte Carlo Simulation-Based Analysis Technique for High-Pressure Ionization Chambers (HPIC) (#1858)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K.H. Sung (Autores: K.H. Sung , C.H. Min , J.-K. Shin)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Yonsei University, Department of Radiation Convergence Engineering, Wonju, Republic of Korea [2] NeosisKorea, Daejeon, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract High-pressure ionization chambers (HPICs) are widely used for radiation monitoring owing to their high sensitivity and mechanical robustness. However, under low-dose conditions, the inherently small signal results in a low signal-to-noise ratio, making accurate characterization of detector response challenging. Therefore, detailed analysis of radiation interaction and charge transport processes in the detector is required for accurate characterization and optimization of HPIC performance. In this study, a simulation framework was developed to investigate and optimize the signal response characteristics of HPICs. A coupled simulation framework integrating Geant4 and Garfield++ is used to model the full signal formation process, including radiation dose deposition and charge transport under applied electric fields. A Kyocera HPIC was used to measure the current response as a function of applied voltage under irradiation from a 95 μCi Cs-137 source. In the Geant4 simulation, the HPIC geometry was modeled to calculate the spatial distribution of dose deposition within the gas volume, which is subsequently converted into ion pair distributions using the W-value. The electric field is modeled in Garfield++ to simulate charge transport under applied voltages, enabling the calculation of the resulting current response. The collected charge in the anode shows a plateau behavior at approximately 64.2 pA, while the experimental results exhibit a saturation around 54.8 pA. It is predicted that the discrepancy is attributed to additional physical effects such as ion recombination, feedthrough effects, and leakage currents. These findings demonstrate that the proposed approach provides a reliable framework for accurate analysis and optimization of HPIC.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 5Poster Number:NSS-01-005] High Granularity Readout Time Projection Chamber R&D for Future Circular e+e- Colliders (#2530)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 H. Qi (Autores: H. Qi , M. Titov)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Institute of High Energy Physics, CAS, Beijing, China [2] Linear Collider Time Projection Chamber International Collaboration, Hamburg, Germany
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract A worldwide Lepton Collider Time Projection Chamber community of the physicists was working to realize an exceptional physics program of the energy-frontier, electron-positron collision, especially for Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee), Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC) and the International Linear Collier (ILC). In all proposed detector concepts, the Time Projection Chamber (TPC) serves as the main tracking detector, complemented by the silicon tracking detectors both inside and outside the TPC, all embedded within a 3 T solenoid field. Many extensive R&D program for the track detector has been developed within the collaboration of LCTPC. TPC performance is satisfactory in Higgs mode, but the high luminosity Z pole running poses substantial technical challenges. Based on MDI background simulation data to study ion-induced space charge effects, we have conducted a detailed assessment of TPC technical challenges and potential solutions, particularly under the high luminosity Z pole running conditions. In this talk, the feasibility and update progress of high precision TPC as the main track detector for e+ e− collider will be presented. TPC detection aims the good separation power with the cluster counting to be considered and the simulation results of the pad/pixelated TPC technology will be given. Compared with the pad readout using the simulation, the high granularity readout TPC options will obtain the better spatial resolution of single electrons, the very high detection efficiency in excellent tracking and good PID performance (less than 3σ). A large prototype TPC in a 1.0T magnetic field, which allow to accommodate up to seven identical Micro Pattern Gaseous Detector (MPGD) readout modules of the TPC being studied using the 5GeV electron beam at DESY, we will present the track reconstruction performance results and summarize the next steps of the pad/pixelated TPC technology for the future lepton colliders.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 7Poster Number:NSS-01-007] A Semi-Analytical Method for Sensitivity Estimation of Parallel-Plate Boron-Coated Ionization Chambers (#3076)
sub_talks.speaker: P. Tang
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] tsinghua university, Institute of Nuclear and New Energy Technology, beijing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a semi-analytical method for sensitivity estimation of multilayer parallel-plate boron-coated ionization chambers. The model combines: (1) an overlap-geometry calculation for the distribution of crossed boron layers under oblique incidence, and (2) a microscopic-simulation-based depth-response function for single-layer effective signal generation. By coupling geometric crossing statistics, boron attenuation, and depth response, detector sensitivity can be rapidly evaluated versus incidence angle, boron thickness, and plate spacing. Compared with Geant4, the method reproduces both trend and magnitude of angular sensitivity, with better agreement at large angles. The framework is suitable for fast parameter screening before high-fidelity simulation.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 9Poster Number:NSS-01-009] A New Efficient n-γ Pulse Shape Discrimination Technique for Fast Scintillation Detectors (#1149)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Riboldi (Autores: S. Riboldi , A. Giaz , S. Brambilla , C. Boiano)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Università degli Studi di Milano, Fisica, Milano, Italy [2] INFN, Milano, Milano, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Pulse shape discrimination (PSD) is an effective technique for identifying the interacting particle (e.g., gamma rays or neutrons) in scintillation detectors. In the simplest cases (e.g., the Cs 2 LiYCl 6 scintillator, showing a large difference between gamma and neutron signals), the PSD procedure can be performed using the "charge integration" (CI) method, based on rectangular weighting functions. However, for scintillators with smaller differences in signal shape (e.g., the LaCl 3 :Ce scintillator), different methods must be used. Moreover, when digital acquisition systems are used, sampling the photodetector's analog signal at a finite time step can significantly affect the PSD results. Indeed, apart from the effects of electronic and quantization noise, the main cause of overlapping of the PSD regions of interest (ROI) of fast scintillator signals processed in the time domain is the temporal variability (ΔT) of the sampling comb relative to the onset of the analog pulse. In the case of relatively high DAQ's acquisition frequency (e.g., 500 MHz), increasing it further to mitigate this issue is not practical, and alternative techniques must be used. One solution is to proceed via the absolute value of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) of the signal, which completely solves the temporal variability issue, though at the cost of significant computational burden. This paper presents a new analysis technique that solves the problem with a negligible computational overhead, making it especially suitable for online applications, by just linking the information on the time shift ΔT to the detector signal, and linearly filtering the whole dataset. The filter weighting function is determined with the DPLMS optimal filter synthesis algorithm, employed here for the first time for this purpose. The PSD results obtained with this technique, suitable as well for energy and time estimations, are here shown for experimentally acquired LaCl 3 :Ce scintillator signals.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 11Poster Number:NSS-01-011] Near infrared scintillation properties of rare earth doped fluorapatite transparent ceramics (#1184)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 T. Yanagida (Autores: T. Yanagida , K. Miyajima , K. Okazaki , T. Nakanishi , H. Furuse , T. Kato , D. Nakauchi , N. Kawaguchi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Nara Institute of Science and Technology, Ikoma, Japan [2] NIMS, Tsukuba, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Near infrared (NIR) emitting scintillators have attracted attentions recently for radiation monitoring at high dose fields. In this work, NIR scintillation properties of Yb3+ and Nd3+ doped fluorapatite (Ca10(PO4)6F2, FAP) transparent ceramics with different doping concentration were investigated. These materials have been originally developed for laser applications. The most famous laser material, Nd:YAG transparent ceramic, can show good scintillation performance both UV-VIS emission and NIR emission, and following such a study, good performance can be expected in FAP transparent ceramic. When X-rays were irradiated, they exhibited 1000 nm (Yb) and 1064 (band) emission bands, and their scintillation decay time resulted several micro hundreds s. The most important property for high dose field monitoring, the lower detection limit (LDL), was investigated by coupling with InGaAs photodiode. Yb and Nd-doped FAP showed 1.2 and 0.6 mGy/hr, respectively. In the conference, scintillation properties as well as photoluminescence properties will be presented, and compared with other NIR emitting scintillators.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 13Poster Number:NSS-01-013] Hydrophobic Solvent-Based Polishing for Performance Enhancement of Water-Sensitive Perovskite Scintillator Crystals (#1236)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Song (Autores: S. Song , J. Seo , D. Lee , C. Park , B. Park , J.-Y. Yeom)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea University, Department of Bioengineering, Seoul, Republic of Korea [2] Korea University, Interdisciplinary Program in Precision Public Health, Seoul, Republic of Korea [3] Korea Institute of Fusion Energy, Dajeon, Republic of Korea [4] Korea University, Global Health Technology Research Center, Seoul, Republic of Korea [5] Seoul National University, Research Institute for Future Technology and Policy, Seoul, Republic of Korea [6] Korea University, School of Bioengineering, Seoul, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Halide perovskites are promising scintillator materials for radiation detection and medical imaging because of their excellent optical and scintillation properties. Since the surface quality of single-crystal scintillators strongly affects light extraction and detector performance, polishing is an essential step in scintillator fabrication. However, conventional wet polishing processes are not suitable for water-sensitive crystals such as Cs 3 Cu 2 I 5 (CCI). In this work, hydrophobic solvents were investigated as polishing media for water-sensitive CCI single crystals. Three hydrophobic solvents-squalane, silicone oil, and mineral oil- were used as dispersion media for 1 μm alumina abrasives, followed by toluene rinsing after polishing. Among them, squalane showed the best polishing performance, yielding the lowest surface roughness (R q =17.29 nm), the highest transmittance of 78.21%, and the narrowest rocking-curve FWHM of 0.025°. In addition, sequential polishing in squalane using P2000 sandpaper, P4000 sandpaper, and 1 μm alumina enhanced the light yield and improved the energy resolution from 6.53% to 5.83%. These results identify squalane as a promising polishing medium for water-sensitive halide perovskite scintillators.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 15Poster Number:NSS-01-015] Combining cross-luminescent scintillators and μSiPMs for better timing in ToF-PET (#1249)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Herweg (Autores: K. Herweg , S. Bisi , C. Bruschini , E. Charbon , A. Gola , L. Parellada-Monreal , M. Penna , D. Schug , V. Schulz , S. Gundacker)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] RWTH Aachen University, University Hospital RWTH Aachen, Aachen, Germany [2] RWTH Aachen University, Institute of Imaging and Computer Vision, Aachen, Germany [3] Ecole polythechnique fédérale de Lausanne, Advanced Quantum Architecture Laboratory, Neuchatel, Switzerland [4] Fondazione Bruno Kessler, Trento, Italy [5] Austrian Academy of Sciences, Marietta Blau Institute for Particle Physics, Vienna, Austria
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Time-of-flight positron emission tomography (ToF-PET) has boosted PET image quality significantly in the last years. During its first inception it was built with cross-luminescent BaF 2 crystals, which have since been replaced by LYSO. Recently, cross-luminescence has regained popularity with new scintillators being developed. However, BaF 2 and the recently developed Cs 2 ZnCl 4 could not improve on the LYSO state-of-the-art coincidence time resolution (CTR) (56 ps for 2x2x3 mm³ and 95 ps for 3x3x19 mm³). As Cs 2 ZnCl 4 shows a significant Cherenkov production, we combined it with the DIGILOG approach to boost its timing performance. The DIGILOG approach segments the sensor into μSiPMs and has shown an improved timing performance for BGO due to its Cherenkov radiation and an improved SPTR. Here, we simulated a 3x3x3 mm³ and a 3x3x20 mm³ Cs 2 ZnCl 4 crystal coupled to seven different μSiPM arrays. The simulation included noise factors like dark counts, cross-talk, SPAD dead time and analog noise. It was designed with a PDE of 60 % and an SPTR of 25 ps. This resulted in an improved CTR of 34+/-4 ps for an array of 20x20 μSiPMs coupled to a 3x3x3 mm³ Cs 2 ZnCl 4 crystal compared to the non-segmented SiPM at 48+/-3 ps. Furthermore, for the 3x3x20 mm³ crystal, a CTR of 64+/-4 ps was reached with a 10x10 μSiPM array, while the non-segmented SiPM showed a CTR of 84+/-3 ps. The results of the segmented SiPMs improve on the LYSO state-of-the-art. Additionally, they demonstrate that the DIGILOG SiPM approach improves timing performance not just for BGO, but also for other scintillators with high Cherenkov yield, ultra-fast emission and low light yield. We also provide motivation to optimize sensors for Cs 2 ZnCl 4 , which could enable better timing performance than the LYSO state-of-the-art.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 17Poster Number:NSS-01-017] Temperature Dependence of Pulse Shape Discrimination in SiPM-Based EJ-276D Detectors (#1585)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Di Fulvio (Autores: J. W. Fritchie , A. Di Fulvio , G. Gariazzo , G. Roche)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering, Urbana, Illinois, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The temperature dependence of pulse shape discrimination performance was investigated for three commercial silicon photomultiplier technologies coupled to an EJ-276D organic scintillator. Measurements were conducted at 22 °C, 30 °C, 40 °C, and 50 °C using PuBe sources. Pulse shape discrimination was quantified using the tail-to-total ratio and figure of merit. For all devices, the figure of merit increased at 30 °C. The Broadcom device exhibited the highest performance, increasing from 1.12 at 22 °C to a maximum of 1.17 at 30 °C before decreasing to 0.76 at 50 °C. The Onsemi and Hamamatsu devices showed smaller improvements, with figure of merit values increasing from 0.86 to 0.89 and 0.84 to 0.90, respectively, between 22 °C and 30 °C. At 50 °C, all devices exhibited reduced performance due to increased silicon photomultiplier thermal noise. Temperature-dependent changes in pulse shape were observed, with increasing temperature producing faster decay and modifying the balance of prompt and delayed scintillation light, improving neutron-gamma separation at intermediate temperatures. Despite degradation at higher temperature, all devices maintained effective discrimination up to 50 °C. These results demonstrate that silicon photomultiplier-based detectors are capable of robust neutron-gamma discrimination at elevated temperatures relevant to safeguards applications.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 19Poster Number:NSS-01-019] Scintillation light quenching for energetic charged particles in GAGG:Ce (#1607)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 F. Liang (Autores: F. Liang , N. Floyd , H. Jayatissa , P. Adsley , A. Alvarez , R. Bartsch , S. Fritz , T. Hankins , B. Harvey , K. Pham , E. Schnorrenberg , D. Shelden , S. Yennello)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Los Alamos National Laboratory, ISR Division, Los Alamos, New Mexico, United States of America [2] Texas A&M University, Cyclotron Institute, College Station, Texas, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Cerium-doped gadolinium gallium aluminium garnet (GAGG:Ce) is a novel scintillator with excellent scintillation properties. It is suitable for use in various basic science research and applications. Because the scintillation light is quenched for charged particle detection, it is necessary to use beams from accelerators to calibrate the energy response. Measurements of energetic charged particles incident on three GAGG:Ce crystals were performed using accelerated protons, 4 He, and 12 C at 0 o C and 20 o C in consideration for detecting charged particles in the earth's radiation belts for space weather modeling and for deploying in dosimetry devices in ion therapy, respectively. The Birks factor which quantitatively describes the extent of quenching was deduced from the experimental data. For all three GAGG:Ce scintillators, the Birks factor decreases with the atomic number Z of the incident ions. Furthermore, less light quenching, a smaller Birks factor, was observed for GAGG:Ce at 0 o C. The quenching for the Mg-codoped GAGG:Ce which has a shorter decay time constant, was found to be less temperature dependent compared to the other two GAGG:Ce crystals.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 21Poster Number:NSS-01-021] Facile, scalable and high-yield synthesis of zero-dimensional copper halide Cs 3 Cu 2 Cl 5 scintillator with near-unity quantum yield for high-resolution X-ray imaging applications (#1659)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Shin (Autores: Y.S. Choi , J. Im , K. Heo , S.O. Cho , B.K. Cha , B. Shin)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] KAIST, Materials Science and Engineering, Daejeon, Republic of Korea [2] KAIST, Nuclear and Quantum Engineering, Daejeon, Republic of Korea [3] Viewworks, Anyang, Republic of Korea [4] KERI, Ansan, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Metal halide perovskites, particularly copper halide variants, have emerged as promising scintillators owing to their large Stokes shift, high photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), and efficient radioluminescence. Here, we demonstrate a dioxolane-mediated reaction synthesis as a simple, scalable, and high-yield strategy for producing Cs 3 Cu 2 Cl 5 powders with near-complete conversion. By employing low-polarity yet water-miscible dioxolane as the reaction medium together with an aqueous H 3 PO 2 additive, the solubility imbalance between the precursors inherent to low-polarity solvents is effectively addressed. This approach enables stoichiometry-controlled dissolution-precipitation under a low-polarity reaction environment and the formation of phase-pure Cs 3 Cu 2 Cl 5 powders with near-unity PLQY. The powders show bright green emission at ~530 nm and retain over 80% of their initial efficiency after 300 days of ambient storage without encapsulation, demonstrating remarkable intrinsic stability. Cs 3 Cu 2 Cl 5 -based composite films deliver an ultrahigh light yield of ~98,000 photons MeV -1 , greatly surpassing that of commercial scintillators such as Gd 2 O 2 S and CsI:Tl, and exhibiting excellent dose linearity and long-term irradiation stability. When integrated into commercial flat-panel detectors, the Cs 3 Cu 2 Cl 5 -based composite films successfully enabled high-quality 2D radiographic and 3D computed tomography imaging, directly verifying their compatibility with existing X-ray detection systems. This facile and efficient synthesis, together with the demonstrated device-level imaging performance, highlights Cs 3 Cu 2 Cl 5 as a scalable and practical candidate for next-generation X-ray scintillators.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 23Poster Number:NSS-01-023] Spectral-feature-based radionuclide and radiation-type discrimination using a plastic scintillation fiber detector for in-situ pipe measurements (#1767)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 T. Abe (Autores: T. Abe , T. Nakasone , T. Yamada , M. Kanno , Y. Morishita)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Japan Atomic Energy Agency, Collaborative Laboratories for Advanced Decommissioning Science, Minamisomashi, Japan [2] Japan Radiation Engineering Co.,Ltd., Hitachishi, Japan [3] PESCO Co., Ltd., Minatoku, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract A capillary-type plastic scintillation fiber (PSF) detector combined with a multi-channel analyzer (MCA) was investigated for radionuclide and radiation-type discrimination in in-situ pipe measurements. Plastic scintillators generally exhibit poor energy resolution, resulting in broadened spectra that complicate conventional peak-based identification. In this study, spectral features including the Compton edge (CE), endpoint, and centroid were extracted from β- and γ-ray spectra obtained using Sr-90/Y-90 and Cs-137 sources. The positional dependence of these features along the fiber was evaluated, and significantly reduced variation compared with previous studies was achieved by introducing a reflective structure at the fiber end. In addition, radiation-type discrimination under mixed β/γ conditions was investigated using a stainless-steel (SUS) cover to suppress β-ray components. The results demonstrated that the extracted spectral features remained stable against source position and that condition switching using the SUS cover enabled practical discrimination of β and γ components. These findings indicate that the proposed method is applicable to contamination assessment in confined environments such as piping systems.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 25Poster Number:NSS-01-025] Investigation of Coincidence Time Resolution in BaF 2 :Y Scintillators for TOF PET Applications (#1798)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 C.-M. Kao (Autores: H. Kim , J. Chen , J. Zhang , J. Xu , S. Sundramoorthy , Y. Wang , C.-T. Chen , C.-M. Kao)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Chicago, Department of Radiology, Chicago, Illinois, United States of America [2] University of Chicago, Department of Radiation and Cellular Oncology, Chicago, Illinois, United States of America [3] Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Shanghai, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We are investigating BaF₂:Y scintillators for TOF‑PET applications. BaF₂ exhibits an ultra‑fast scintillation component with a 0.6 ns decay time produced through cross‑luminescence, making it an attractive material for achieving coincidence time resolutions below 100 ps. Recent advances in Vacuum‑Ultraviolet (VUV) SiPMs, which provide high photon‑detection efficiency in the deep‑UV range, have made it increasingly feasible to reliably detect this fast component. In addition to the fast emission, BaF₂ also contains a slow scintillation component with a decay time of approximately 600 ns. This slow component can be substantially suppressed through doping-for example, BaF₂:Y, produced via yttrium doping. Effective suppression of the slow component is essential for applications requiring high count‑rate capability, excellent timing performance, and minimal pulse pile‑up, such as TOF‑PET. In this work, we investigated the coincidence time resolution (CTR) of BaF₂:Y scintillators. The BaF₂ and BaF₂:Y crystals used in this study were grown and polished by the Shanghai Institute of Ceramics (SIC), China. For the BaF₂:Y samples, the yttrium concentration was set to 2 at%, which suppressed the slow component by approximately a factor of four while leaving the fast‑component light yield unaffected. Hamamatsu S13370 VUV‑MPPCs were used to detect the fast scintillation component. Pairs of BaF₂ and BaF₂:Y crystals with dimensions 2 × 2 × 3 mm³ were optically coupled to S13370 VUV‑MPPCs and irradiated with a ²²Na source placed between them in a coincidence setup. We measured CTR values of 86 ps for BaF₂ and 96 ps for BaF₂:Y. These initial results are highly promising, and we anticipate further improvements in CTR with a more optimized experimental setup. Here, we report our preliminary findings.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 27Poster Number:NSS-01-027] Experimental Study of DOI Effects on the Timing Response of a 1"×2" LaBr3 Detector (#1996)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Gaitan Dominguez (Autores: S. Gaitan Dominguez , V. M. Nouvilas , M. Caballero Rodríguez , J. A. Briz , L. M. Fraile , J. Udias)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Complutense University of Madrid, Group of Nuclear Physics, EMFTEL and IPARCOS, Madrid, United Kingdom [2] Cern, ISOLDE, EP Department, Geneva, Genève, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Depth of interaction (DOI) effects can affect the timing response of scintillation detectors due to variations in optical photon transport inside the crystal volume. In this work, DOI-dependent timing measurements were performed using a 1"×2" LaBr 3 ​ scintillation detector coupled to a photomultiplier tube (PMT) within the framework of the HiSTARs project. A 22 Na source was positioned at different locations along the crystal axis in coincidence with a fast SiPM-based reference detector, and signals were acquired using a DRS digitizer operating at 5 GS/s. The present study focuses on the comparison between interactions occurring close to the PMT side of the crystal and interactions occurring close to the opposite side. Coincidence timing distributions show a systematic shift of approximately 300 ps in the centroid position between both irradiation configurations. Coincidence timing resolutions of 287 ps and 268 ps FWHM were obtained for the two positions, respectively. The observed behavior is consistent with differences in optical photon propagation paths and light collection timing inside the scintillator. Although DOI effects introduce measurable timing shifts, the overall degradation of the timing resolution remains moderate for the studied configurations. Additional irradiation geometries and analysis conditions are currently under study in order to obtain a more complete characterization of DOI effects in long LaBr 3 ​ scintillation detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 29Poster Number:NSS-01-029] Development of Mo-Doped Cs 2 HfCl 6 for Dosimetry in High Dose-Rate Environment (#2267)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Kondo (Autores: S. Kondo , C. F. Fujiwara , A. Yamaji , S. Kurosawa)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Nagoya University, School of Engineering, Nagoya, Japan [2] Tohoku University, Department of Materials Science, Graduate School of Engineering,, Sendai, Japan [3] Nagoya University, Graduate School of Engineering, Nagoya, Japan [4] Osaka University, Institute of Laser Engineering, Osaka, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In order to accomplish rapid and safe decommissioning of Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant, the remote and real-time dosimeter was required. To address this issue, detector systems comprising a scintillator coupled to an optical fiber have been proposed.　 In this system, emission wavelength of the scintillator itself should be in the near-infrared (NIR) band, to spectrally discriminate the scintillation signal from the Cherenkov component generated within the optical fiber itself. Therefore, in this study, we focus on Mo doped Cs 2 HfCl 6 as the scintillator with NIR emission wavelength and high atmospheric stability. The Mo doped Cs 2 HfCl 6 scintillators were grown via melt solidification method. The result of powder X-ray diffraction pattern suggested that the single phase of Mo: Cs 2 HfCl 6 were successfully obtained. Furthermore, the emission wavelength of Mo doped Cs 2 HfCl 6 was shifted to 900nm from 420 nm of host emission of C 2 HfCl 6 . These results indicate Mo: CHC is the promising scintillator for the real time remote monitoring system with optical fiber.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 31Poster Number:NSS-01-031] From LaBr 3 :Ce to Cs 2 LiLa(Br,Cl) 6 :Ce Mixed-Halide Elpasolites: Tailoring Scintillation Response for High-Precision Gamma-Ray and Neutron Detection (#2321)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Z. Cai (Autores: Z. Cai , Z. Yin , X. Zhang , Z. Kang , J. Liu , Q. Zhao , T. Wang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Northwestern Polytechnical University, State Key Laboratory of Solidification Processing, Xi'an, China [2] Crystalab Corporation Ltd, Xi'an, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Halide scintillators provide a flexible material platform for detectors requiring high gamma-ray energy resolution, fast response, and, in lithium-containing compounds, intrinsic neutron sensitivity. This work presents CrystaLab Co., Ltd.'s compositional-engineering route from LaBr 3 :Ce gamma-ray scintillators to Cs 2 LiLa(Br,Cl) 6 :Ce (CLLBC) mixed-halide Elpasolites for combined gamma-ray and neutron detection. Packaged LaBr 3 :Ce detector modules demonstrate high-resolution gamma-ray spectroscopy, with a representative energy resolution of 2.37% at 662 keV and product specifications below 3% at 662 keV. CeBr 3 detectors provide a low-background lanthanide-halide option with energy resolution below 4.5% at 662 keV. By introducing Li and tuning the Br/Cl halide sublattice, Cs 2 LiLaBr 6 (CLLB) and CLLBC extend the platform to neutron-sensitive dual-mode detection with neutron-gamma pulse-shape discrimination (PSD). CLLB products provide gamma-ray energy resolution below 4.5% at 662 keV and room-temperature neutron-gamma figure of merit (FOM) values >1.2, while optimized 1-inch CLLBC crystals achieved 3.09% energy resolution at 662 keV and FOM = 2.1. These results show how halide composition, crystal growth, and detector integration can tailor scintillation response from high-precision gamma-ray spectroscopy toward compact mixed-field radiation detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 33Poster Number:NSS-01-033] Application of neutron sensitising layers to plastic scintillator (#2414)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. P. Taggart (Autores: J. R. Hitchens , C. Allwork , S. L. Chauhan , T. Crane , T. Heather , M. P. Taggart)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] AWE Nuclear Security Technologies, Reading, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Eljen plastic scintillator disks have been coated with layers of neutron sensitiser in a systematic study on the thickness of neutron detection layers. Here we discuss the impact of enhancing standard plastic scintillator (PVT) with coatings containing both lithium and boron isotopes. The application of these layers enhances the material to provide a mechanism for detecting neutron radiation. A systematic study was performed to assess the impact of sensitiser thickness on neutron detection efficiency and neutron-gamma pulse shape discrimination (PSD) performance. Samples were exposed to the mixed radiation fields of a 252 Cf source, and a sample of plutonium. The results demonstrate clear neutron-gamma discrimination in sensitised samples, with measured figures of merit in excess of 3 recorded for optimised lithium-rich coatings. This is comparable performance to established dual-mode detectors. These findings show that thin, externally applied neutron-sensitising layers provide an effective route to enhancing the performance of conventional plastic scintillators. This approach may offer a low-cost means of upgrading existing detector systems in nuclear security applications.

The samples showed sharp emission peaks at around 700 nm, which matched the sensitivity of typical Si-photodetectors. When the samples were combined with a Si-photodetector and irradiated with X-, α-, and β-rays, currents ranging from picoamperes to nanoamperes were detected. sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 37Poster Number:NSS-01-037] Single-ended Multiplexed Readout Scintillation Detector With Depth of Interaction Capability: Architecture and Optical Simulation (#2505)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 G. Jazvac (Autores: G. Jazvac , A. M. Kožuljević , L. Lotina , L. Pavelić)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Institute for Medical Research and Occupational Health, Division of Radiation Protection, Zagreb, Croatia [2] Nucleometrix d.o.o., Zagreb, Croatia
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract An accurate and precise determination of the depth of interaction (DOI) of incident photons in scintillation detectors is paramount to increasing the spatial resolution of positron annihilation tomography (PET) systems. The high number of readout channels is a major source of cost and complexity of such systems, while light sharing multiplexed readouts suffer from edge effects. We have developed a pixelized scintillator detector with DOI capability and 4-to-1 multiplexing utilizing only single-ended readout and light-sharing light guides which can improve signal-to-noise ratio and mitigate edge effects present in other solutions. The scintillator matrix is coupled to a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) array on one end and light guides on the other. Adjacent crystals are connected in pairs via light guides to enable light sharing. The scintillation light of these crystal pairs is shared between exactly two SiPM pixels. DOI is determined using the ratio of signals on the two SiPM pixels. Pairing distant crystals on matrix edges avoids edge effects. We present the detector architecture and the results of optical simulations evaluating its DOI capability. The interaction position was swept along the central axis of one crystal and the number of incident photons was recorded in the interaction crystal and in the optically connected crystal. The number of rays incident on the sensor coupled to the interaction crystal is always higher than that of the connected crystal. This enables unambiguous determination of the interaction crystal. The ratio of the number of rays incident on the sensors spans three orders of magnitude and approaches unity as the source gets closer to the light guide. These properties demonstrate a favorable DOI capability of the presented detector configuration.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 39Poster Number:NSS-01-039] Performance evaluation of GaGG(Ce) scintillators with different photosensors (#2850)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Caballero Rodríguez (Autores: M. Caballero Rodríguez , N. Bernier , V. M. Nouvilas , L. Fraile , O. Alonso-Sañudo , J. A. Briz , S. Gaitan , G. G. de Lorenzo , P. Gonzalez-Tarrio , A. Illana , J. Udias)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Universidad Complutense de Madrid, Facultad de Ciencias Físicas / Departamento de Estructura de la Materia, Física Térmica y Electrónica, Madrid, Spain [2] CERN, ISOLDE, EP Department, Geneva, Spain [3] CSIC, Instituto de Estructura de la Materia, Madrid, Spain
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The HIE-ISOLDE Timing Array for Reaction Studies (HISTARS) project at CERN is developing a specialized detector system designed to measure the lifetimes of excited nuclear states. For efficient particle detection, thin square GaGG(Ce) are utilized alongside YSO due to their high density and fast scintillation properties. This work evaluates the performance of GAGG(Ce) crystals coupled with two distinct photosensors: a Hamamatsu R9779 photomultiplier tube (PMT) and an array of four silicon photomultipliers (SiPM) using a custom-designed circuit. These configurations were tested in combination with a LaBr 3 (Ce) detector to facilitate coincidence measurements. Data acquisition was performed using high-speed digitizer to extract timing and energy information. This article reports on the comparative performance of both readout methods, specifically characterizing pulse shape discrimination capabilities, energy resolution, and the coincidence time resolution for alpha-gamma events. Although the energy resolution is acceptable and it has a good pulse shape discrimination capability, the measured timing limitations show that the current configuration is not ideal for the HISTARS array. These results will guide the selection of better-suited materials for high-precision timing at HIE-ISOLDE.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 41Poster Number:NSS-01-041] Cosmic-Ray Muon Position Reconstruction via Dual-End Readout of Triangular Plastic Scintillators (#2888)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Zhang (Autores: Z. Yin , Y. Zhang , J. Zhang , L. Wang , Y. Huang , X. Zhao , J. Cheng , Y. Liu)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Beijing Normal University, School of Physics and Astronomy, Beijing, China [2] Beijing Normal University, Joint Laboratory of Jinping Ultra-low Radiation Background Measurement of Ministry of Ecology and Environment, Beijing, China [3] Jinping Deep Underground Frontier Science and Dark Matter Key Laboratory of Sichuan Province, Liangshan, China [4] Beijing Normal University, Key Laboratory of Beam Technology of Ministry of Education, Beijing, China [5] Chengdu University of Technology, College of Nuclear Technology and Automation Engineering, Chengdu, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract By measuring the time difference and amplitude ratio of the signals at both longitudinal ends of a triangular prism plastic scintillator through dual-end readout, it is theoretically possible to reconstruct the longitudinal position of an incident muon. This paper presents a cosmic-ray muon collimation device that determines the incident region via triple coincidence and features an adjustable incident area. Using natural cosmic-ray muons obtained with this device, dual-end positioning experiments were carried out on a triangular prism plastic scintillator. The threshold-crossing time and amplitude information were extracted from the complete waveforms and fitted, yielding well-fitted relationship functions of the threshold-crossing time difference and the logarithm of the amplitude ratio with respect to the hit position. Experimental results show that the longitudinal position resolution achieved by this method is 3 cm, confirming the effectiveness of the dual-end readout positioning method in triangular prism plastic scintillator array muon detectors and laying a foundation for future research on lightweight and efficient plastic scintillator array detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 43Poster Number:NSS-01-043] Scintillation Properties of 6 Li-doped CsI:Tl Crystals for Thermal Neutron Detection (#2928)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. K. Gourishetty (Autores: D. Sharma , A. K. Gourishetty , M. Tyagi , M. Sonawane)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] India Institute of Technology Roorkee, Department of Physics, Roorkee, India [2] Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Technical Physics Division, Mumbai, India
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Alkali halide scintillators have emerged as promising low-cost alternatives to conventional thermal neutron detectors such as 3 He counters, through the incorporation of neutron sensitive isotopes such as 6 Li or 10 B, owing to their ease of growth and scalability. In this work, single crystals of CsI:Tl incorporating 2% 6 Li and varying concentration of Sr as dopants were grown using the Bridgman melt growth method and evaluated for their scintillation and neutron-gamma discrimination characteristics. The radioluminescence spectra are dominated by yellow-green emission from Tl activator sites. Under 137 Cs excitation, the light output of the crystals was observed to decrease with Sr incorporation compared to the 6 Li-only doped crystal, while the crystal doped with 2% Sr exhibit the best energy resolution of 6.8% at 662keV. The pulse shape discrimination (PSD) studies of the grown crystals demonstrate effective neutron-gamma discrimination, highlighting the potential of these crystals for use in mixed radiation fields and compact radiation system.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. K. Gourishetty (Autores: T. Kumar , V. Anand , A. K. Gourishetty)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract A series of polyvinyl toluene (PVT)-based scintillators was prepared via thermal polymerization to investigate the effect of the thermal initiator 2,2-Azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN) on light output. Samples were synthesized both with varying weight percentages (wt%) of AIBN and without AIBN. All samples contained 2% 2,2-diphenyloxazole (PPO) and 0.05% 1,4-bis(5-phenyl-2-oxazolyl) benzene (POPOP), while the concentrations of vinyl toluene and AIBN were varied. The light output of the developed plastic scintillators (PS) was compared to the commercially available PS EJ-267D using the gamma spectrum from a Cs-137 radiation source. The results indicated that samples containing 0.1% AIBN without argon purging, 1% AIBN without purging, and 0% AIBN with argon purging yielded 24.40%, 28.23%, and 40.88% of the light output of EJ-267D, respectively.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 47Poster Number:NSS-01-047] Comparative Analysis of Scintillators for TOF-DXA Detectors in the Low-Energy X-ray Region (#3149)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Nam (Autores: J. Nam , J. Jung , S.-H. Chun , S. Kwon , J.H. Jung , Y. Choi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Sogang University, Department of Electronic Engineering, Intelligent Signal Processing System (ISPS) Laboratory, Seoul, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract TOF-DXA requires simultaneous energy and timing measurement in the low-energy X-ray region (<60 keV). However, the low X-ray energies result in reduced scintillation light output and small detector signals, making timing measurement challenging. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the performance of different scintillators for energy and timing measurement in low-energy TOF-DXA detectors. An analog front-end circuit was developed for energy and timing measurement in low-energy TOF-DXA detectors. Detector signals in the energy path were amplified transmitted differentially to reduce common-mode noise and signal degradation. For timing path, a high slew-rate amplifier and comparator were used to generate LVDS preserving the rising-edge integrity of detector pulses. Three 3 × 3 × 3 mm³ scintillators (LYSO, GFAG, and YAP) coupled with a NUV-MT SiPM were evaluated for simultaneous energy and timing measurement. Output pulses were measured using an Am-241 point source to evaluate energy resolution and pulse characteristics. In addition, X-ray spectra were acquired using an X-ray generator operated at 83 kVp and 0.2 mA with a Ce filter to evaluate detector performance in the DXA. The energy resolutions measured with LYSO, GFAG, and YAP were 25.7%, 24.4%, and 30.9%, respectively. In the timing path, LYSO exhibited the highest slew rate (364.8 MV/s), followed by GFAG (354.9 MV/s) and YAP (220.8 MV/s). LYSO showed the highest peak-to-valley ratios for both the low- and high-energy peaks (3.96 and 1.62, respectively). For the low-energy peak, GFAG and YAP showed PVRs of 3.32 and 2.45, respectively, whereas YAP showed a slightly higher high-energy PVR (1.13) than GFAG (1.02).This overall performance may be attributed to the balanced characteristics of LYSO, which exhibited higher light output than YAP and faster decay time than GFAG. These results indicated that LYSO was superior to GFAG and YAP for TOF-DXA applications requiring both energy and timing measurement.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 49Poster Number:NSS-01-049] Improved Low‑Energy Threshold Performance of a Vacuum‑Compatible Hybrid Pixel Detector for Soft X‑ray Applications (#1007)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Nakaye (Autores: Y. Nakaye , T. Inoue , M. Oka , T. Sakumura , Y. Sakuma , S. Mikusu)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Rigaku Corporation, Detector Development Grp., Akishima, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We report characterization results of a vacuum‑compatible, pre‑production hybrid pixel array X‑ray detector incorporating a silicon sensor and a low‑noise photon‑counting readout ASIC, with emphasis on extending the practical low‑energy discriminator threshold. Calibration pulse measurements combined with refined noise characterization enabled evaluation of discriminator threshold settings down to approximately 450 eV. Considering measured RMS noise levels on the order of 70-80 e - RMS, such threshold operation implies practical detectability of soft X‑ray photons with energies around 500 eV, although uniform full‑field operation at this threshold is not yet expected. Low‑threshold operation was found to be temporally stable, showing negligible threshold drift and no observable degradation of pixel operability during continuous operation over extended periods. Soft X‑ray beam validation experiments are planned at the SPring‑8 BL17SU beamline. Additional measurements at higher X‑ray energies will be conducted at BL32‑B2 and BL29XU to support fundamental characterization of detector and ASIC behavior. The present study focuses on system‑level noise correction and threshold optimization using a conventional silicon sensor. Evaluation with alternative sensor technologies, including iLGAD, is foreseen in future work.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 53Poster Number:NSS-01-053] Development and Testing of the Strip Pairing Algorithm for the COSI Data Pipeline (#1263)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Gerber (Autores: J. Gerber , A. Zoglauer , S. E. Boggs , F. Hagemann , C. Kierans , S. N. Pike , J. M. Roberts , F. R. Rogers , J. A. Tomsick)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of California, San Diego, Astronomy & Astrophysics, San Diego, California, United States of America [2] University of California, Berkeley, Space Sciences Laboratory, Berkeley, California, United States of America [3] NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Greenbelt, Maryland, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) is a NASA Small Explorer satellite mission scheduled for launch in August 2027. COSI's imaging capabilities are achieved by reconstructing Compton scattering events within a 2 x 2 x 4 stack of germanium detectors (GeDs). Each GeD contains orthogonal electrode strips on opposite faces of the detector, forming an x-y grid. An incident gamma ray interacts with the GeD by depositing energy in one or more strips on each face that are then read out simultaneously. The "strip pairing" algorithm reconstructs the 2D position of each scatter by comparing the measured energies on pairs of orthogonal strips through a reduced chi square statistic. While simple for a single-site event, the matching becomes more complex when considering multiple scatters within a detector, multiple scatters on a single strip, or charge sharing between neighboring strips. Here, we describe the strip pairing algorithm and how it is implemented into the COSI pipeline. We then test the algorithm's efficacy and use it to demonstrate the imaging and spectral performance of a COSI GeD. Using a 137 Cs calibration source and a single test detector, we find that the pipeline reconstructs the source's position and yields an energy resolution of less than 1% full width at half maximum at 662 keV.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 55Poster Number:NSS-01-055] Temperature-Dependent Charge Transport in Diamond Radiation Detectors (#1377)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 O. A. Johnson (Autores: O. A. Johnson , R. Fitzhugh , E. Lukosi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Tennessee Knoxville, Nuclear Engineering, Knoxville, Tennessee, United States of America [2] Y-12 National Security Complex, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Semiconductor radiation detectors are often limited due to thermal degradation of their electrical properties: as temperature increases, thermally activated carrier generation and other effects lead to elevated leakage currents and reduced signal to noise ratios. For more extreme environments such as advanced reactors and molten salt environments, detectors which operate at high temperatures are needed. Diamond, with its wide 5.47 eV bandgap, high carrier mobility, and radiation hardness is a promising material. Previous work in literature reported charge collection efficiency degradation in diamond at 230 °C, followed by recovery and stability of operation to 450 °C. However, this result has not been widely validated. This study evaluates three diamond samples of varying thickness at elevated temperatures, reevaluating carrier mobility and charge collection efficiency. Alpha traces at each temperature are analyzed to study the current transients, gaining insight into how thermal variations impact detector performance and mechanisms driving charge transport variation.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 57Poster Number:NSS-01-057] Monitoring neutron exposure in hyper-pure germanium detectors with in-situ capture reactions (#1736)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 T. Round (Autores: T. Round , B. Green , S. Croft , J. Moore , A. Metcalfe , M. J. Joyce)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Lancaster University, Engineering Department, Lancaster, United Kingdom [2] NSG Environmental, Chorley, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The potential to monitor neutron exposure in hyper-pure germanium detectors via capture-g reactions in the germanium crystal is explored. The short-lived reactions on 70 Ge and 74 Ge resulting in g rays in the 130 to 200 keV energy region have been studied in terms of their response to thermalization of neutrons incident on portable, mechanically cooled, reverse-electrode hyper-pure germanium detectors (REGe TM ). The relative sensitivity in terms of y rays emitted per unit neutron flux is estimated and a comparison is made with the inelastic response observed at higher energies, the latter often considered as cause of damage in such detectors. We report the potential for these short-lived reactions to serve as a built-in neutron-sensitive diagnostic for germanium detector use in hot cells and realistic, mixed-field environments.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 59Poster Number:NSS-01-059] Pixel Architecture Effects on Neutron-Induced White Spot Generation in CMOS Image Sensors (#1811)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Jeong (Autores: J. Jeong , S. Kim , J. Lim , S. Lee , I. Kwon)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Yonsei University, Radiation Convergence Engineering, Wonju, Republic of Korea [2] Samsung Electronics, Whaseong, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper quantifies how pixel structural parameters, specifically pitch, photodiode type, and transfer gate design, independently influence neutron-induced white spot generation in CMOS image sensors. Six sensor families with pixel pitches of 0.64, 0.70, 1.00, 1.12, and 1.20 μm, covering single and dual photodiode configurations and single and dual transfer gate designs, were irradiated with neutrons at the TRIUMF facility across seven cumulative fluence steps up to approximately 7×10⁸ n/cm². Ten samples per family were used, with dark-frame measurements performed at each step using eight-frame averaged images. White spot fractions were extracted using a baseline-subtracted delta counting method with Arrhenius-based temperature correction applied to the radiation-induced component. All six families exhibit a clear power-law dependence of white spot fraction on fluence. Spatial analysis reveals a monotonic increase in the 3×3 cluster ratio, defined as the ratio of the summed dark signal increase in neighboring pixels to that of the center hot pixel, from 0.14 at 1.20 μm to 0.24 at 0.64 μm, and this metric remains independent of fluence. A two-stage meta-regression model shows that increasing pitch from 0.64 to 1.20 μm raises the power-law amplitude by 2.12 times, adopting dual photodiode sharing raises it by 2.35 times, and employing a dual transfer gate reduces it by 0.49 times. Furthermore, the model is extended to predict white spot fractions for unmeasured pixel configurations, with potential for radiation-tolerant CIS design.

Herzen , D. John , F. L. Klaus , C. Mogler , L. Pancheri , J. Parnell , M. Persson , E. Posteraro , M. Sjolin , M. Y. Tamm , S. Wirtensohn)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Monolithic silicon CMOS Sensors represent a considerable step forward in charged particle and photon sensing, and emerge as a promising embodiment for the design of novel deep-silicon photon-counting X-ray Computed Tomography scanners . This work presents the first characterization of the ARCADIA MD3 Fully-Depleted CMOS sensors, which technology is currently the baseline for the development of innovative sensors under the framework of the EIC Pathfinder Open 1MICRON project. We report on the characterisation results using an edge-on geometry and a focused synchrotron X-ray beam at the DESY test facility. The x-rays impinge on the edge of the sensor, increasing the active sensor depth seen by the photons, which consequently improves the quantum efficiency with respect to a face-on configuration. A 37 keV focused beam incident parallel to the sensor surface allowed scans along the two directions of the sensor edge, enabling the extraction of the active sensor thickness and mechanical tilt via pixel intensity profiles. Lateral scans across pixel boundaries revealed a periodicity of the spatial modulation of mean cluster size compatible with the pixel pitch of the matrix. Taking the cluster size as the main figure of merit, the performance of the sensor was evaluated at different thresholds and multiple bias voltages in order to assess the variation in the Coulomb cone and collection dynamic. The measurements are supported by Allpix Squared Monte Carlo framework, demonstrating good consistency between the simulated and the real domain.

With increasing deposited charge, the gain was observed to decrease. This gain suppression effect originates from the electrostatic field screening produced by the avalanche multiplication charge. This work investigates the resilience of the LGADs to the gain suppression by characterizing a set of detectors with different gain layer designs and thicknesses, using Transient Current Techniques.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 65Poster Number:NSS-01-065] Pulse-Shape-Based Slow-Rising Pulse Rejection for Reliable Charge-Carrier Transport Characterization in a Semiconductor Radiation Detector (#2231)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Boo (Autores: J. Boo , B. Park , G. Kim)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Seoul National University, Department of Energy Systems Engineering, Seoul, Republic of Korea [2] Seoul National University, Nuclear Research Institute for Future Technology and Policy (NIFTEP), Seoul, Republic of Korea [3] Seoul National University, Nuclear Engineering Department, Seoul, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Mobility (μ), lifetime (τ), and mobility-lifetime product (μτ) are key metrics for semiconductor radiation detectors. Highly concentrated trapping centers or defects can distort the internal electric-field distribution, producing reduced-amplitude slow-rising charge-sensitive preamplifier pulses that degrade carrier-transit and charge-collection analyses. Although slow-rising-pulse rejection is commonly used to sharpen pulse-amplitude peaks and suppress low-amplitude tails, this work extends its use to charge-carrier transport characterization. A CdZnTeSe detector [1, 2] was characterized at room temperature under electron- and hole-transit-dominant conditions using ²⁴¹Am alpha irradiation. Pulse-shape analysis rejected slow-rising pulses for key metrics extraction. In electron-transit-dominant measurements, the fast-rising pulse events preserved the bias-dependent peak-centroid trend and yielded (μτ) e = 5.7 × 10⁻⁴ cm²/V, μ e = 576 cm²/V·s, and τ e = 1.0 μs, consistent with reported values [3,4]. For hole-transit-dominant measurements, all-pulse events obscured the pulse-amplitude peak and hindered Hecht fitting. After rejection, we obtained (μτ) h = 2.1 × 10⁻⁴ cm²/V, τ h = 0.7 μs, comparable to reported values [5], with μ h = 318 cm²/V·s. Using the rise-time peak as the representative transit time, both all-pulse and fast-rising-pulse events yielded similar μh values. However, when the median rise time of all-pulse events was used instead, drift velocity did not show a clear linear dependence on electric field, whereas fast-rising-pulse events retained linearity. This reflects the need for careful consideration of slow-rising components and the transit-time definition. These results show that slow-rising-pulse rejection enables reliable transport characterization beyond spectral improvement.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 67Poster Number:NSS-01-067] The Sensor, Packaging and INtegration (SPIN) group at Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK): capabilities, facilities and expertise (#2415)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 P. Tosato (Autores: D. Novel , T. Facchinelli , E. Demenev , A. Lega , P. Tosato , S. Ferrari)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Fondazione Bruno Kessler, Trento, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This contribution presents the capabilities, infrastructure, and technical expertise of the Sensor, Packaging and Integration (SPIN) group at Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK). The SPIN unit has established experience in the miniaturisation and integration of electronic systems for radiation detectors, with demonstrated results in space instrumentation (e.g. THESEUS for ESA), high-energy physics (e.g. R&D for ALICE3), and medical applications (e.g. the BOA project within INFN). These domains impose stringent constraints on material budget, geometrical footprint, and signal integrity, motivating the development of dedicated integration strategies. The group core expertise lies in the co-design of sensors and front-end electronics for operation in highly constrained volumes, where standard packaging solutions are not applicable. This includes the optimisation of interconnect technologies (wire bonding, TAB, flip-chip), layout strategies and the implementation of low-noise architectures. Emphasis is placed on preserving signal integrity in high-density environments typical of modern detector systems. SPIN offers end-to-end capabilities covering system design, prototyping, assembly, and characterisation, supported by dedicated infrastructure for precision packaging and electrical testing. A key enabling technology is the use of flexible and hybrid electronics, allowing the development of low-mass, conformable interconnects and non-planar integration schemes. In particular, the group has developed dedicated processes for the fabrication and integration of ultra-thin Kapton-aluminium flexible circuits, optimised for low material budget and high mechanical compliance. These structures enable the realisation of fine-pitch routing on lightweight substrates, with controlled thickness and reduced radiation length, making them especially suitable for tracking detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 69Poster Number:NSS-01-069] High-voltage stress test and thermal recovery of an amorphous-silicon-passivated planar HPGe detector (#2646)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Han (Autores: L. Han , Y. Li , L. He , S. Yu , X. Li , M. Yang , Y. Li , Y. Tian)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Tsinghua University, Department of Engineering Physics, Beijing, China [2] Ministry of Education, Key Laboratory of Particle & Radiation Imaging (Tsinghua University), Beijing, China [3] Greater Bay Area National Center of Technology Innovation, Guangzhou, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract High-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors are widely used in low-background and rare-event measurements because of their excellent energy resolution and relatively high detection efficiency. Compared with a-Ge, sputtered a-Si provides a higher electron-injection barrier, which is attractive for planar detectors under high electric fields. However, the high-voltage (HV) stability of a-Si contacts and the recovery from HV-induced large leakage-current and resolution degradation remain insufficiently understood. The detector was fabricated using a planar p-type HPGe crystal (φ24 mm × 10 mm). A Li-diffused n+ contact was used as the high-voltage electrode, while the opposite face was coated with an a-Si layer deposited by magnetron sputtering. A central Al pad was formed on the a-Si layer by thermal evaporation and used as the signal readout electrode. I-V curves were measured with a picoammeter up to 2500 V, and 57Co spectra were acquired at 500-2000 V using a DSPEC-50 digital spectrometer. The stress test consisted of repeated biasing up to 2000 V, followed by 9 hours of room-temperature storage and 9 hours of thermal treatment with the crystal holder maintained below 70 degrees. After the high-voltage stress test, the leakage current at 1000 V increased to approximately 1.1 nA, more than two orders of magnitude higher than the initial level. After thermal treatment below 70 degrees, the leakage current at 1000 V decreased to less than 2 pA, close to the as-fabricated level. At 1000 V, the resolution broadened to 1.53 keV FWHM, suggesting larger noise and contact-related instability under a higher electric field. After thermal treatment, the resolution at 500 V recovered to 0.67 keV FWHM, comparable to the initial value. In the future, we will repeat stress-recovery cycles, and investigate the dependence on treatment temperature and duration. The possible underlying recovery mechanism related to the a-Si fermi level will also be studied.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 71Poster Number:NSS-01-071] Development of a SiC-Based Muon Beam Monitor for the COMET Experiment (#2912)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Okabe (Autores: K. Okabe , Y. Fukao , Y. Igarashi , Y. Fujita , E. Hamada , T. Kishishita , K. Kojima , R. Kosugi , S. Mihara , H. Nishiguchi , M. Shoji , Y. Tanaka , Y. Yamaguchi , Y. Yamada)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] The Graduate University for Advanced Studies, Particle and Nuclear Physics Program, Tsukuba, Japan [2] High Energy Accelerator Research Organization, Institute of Particle and Nuclear Studies, Tsukuba, Japan [3] Universität Bonn, Physikalisches Institut, Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [4] National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology, Advanced Power Electronics Research Center, Tsukuba, Japan [5] University of Tsukuba, Faculty of Engineering, Information and Systems, Tsukuba, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The COMET Experiment at J-PARC aims to search for the muon-to-electron conversion process with a sensitivity of 10−17. In COMET Phase-I, the muon beam monitor (MBM) will be installed downstream of the primary detector system for background suppression and precise beam control. Since the MBM directly measures the high-intensity muon beam, silicon carbide (SiC), one of the wide-bandgap semiconductors with higher radiation tolerance, is employed as the detector material. The SiC sensor was jointly developed by KEK and AIST, and a beam test performed at J-PARC MLF in 2024 showed successful muon detection and sufficient linearity for operation in the COMET Experiment. In addition, a radiation-tolerant ASIC currently under development at KEK is planned for the SiC detector readout. While the initial prototype MBM board utilised a two-layer polyimide PCB to minimise the material budget, it suffered from external noise and inter-channel crosstalk, obscuring low-amplitude beta-ray signals. To address this and optimise the final MBM board design, we developed a test board equipped with seven SiC detectors. This study showed that noise can be reduced by implementing appropriate noise mitigation techniques, such as a ground plane in a standard PCB structure, enabling stable waveform acquisition of low-amplitude beta-ray signals. In addition, inter-channel crosstalk was effectively suppressed to a negligible level by introducing low-pass filters on the bias supply lines close to each detector. Based on these findings, a prototype MBM board for the final system is currently being developed. This presentation also reports on its design and initial performance evaluation.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 73Poster Number:NSS-01-073] Argon Ion-Assisted Polycrystalline PbO Layers for Direct-Conversion X-ray Imaging Detectors (#3080)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Vostokov (Autores: M. Vostokov , J. Rado , G. Nagicheva , A. Stieh , A. Alexandrov , A. Reznik)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Lakehead University, Physics Department, Thunder Bay, Ontario, Canada
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Lead oxide (PbO) is a high-atomic-number photoconductor for direct-conversion X-ray imaging. This work compares PbO layers produced by three deposition regimes: conventional physical vapor deposition from molten PbO powder, oxygen ion-assisted PVD, and argon ion-assisted PVD. All layers were deposited on indium tin oxide coated glass substrates with a polyimide blocking layer to reduce dark current and were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, profilometry, density measurements, and X-ray photoconductivity. Deposition without ion assistance produced low-density polycrystalline PbO with noticeable lag in the X-ray response after irradiation. Oxygen ion-assisted growth yielded dense amorphous PbO with essentially lag-free temporal response. In contrast, argon ion-assisted deposition preserved the polycrystalline structure while producing a more uniform layer with intermediate density and needle-like surface crystallites. X-ray photocurrent measurements showed that the argon-assisted films had an electron-hole pair creation energy, W±, of approximately 6 eV/ehp at 10 V/µm, close to the fundamental limit. Under 30 Hz modulated X-ray irradiation, these films showed stable photocurrent during exposure and rapid signal decay after irradiation stopped, indicating negligible lag.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 75Poster Number:NSS-01-075] Quantum Dots-Based Short-Wave Infrared Avalanche Photodetectors (#1295)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 X. Wei (Autores: S. Fang , X. Wei)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Chongqing, China [2] Chongqing Institute of Green and Intelligent Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chongqing, China [3] Chongqing School, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chongqing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Short-wave infrared photodetectors based on colloidal quantum dots (QDs) have attracted substantial attention owing to their solution processability, tunable bandgaps, and natural compatibility with silicon-based readout integrated circuits. However, the performance of QDs photodetectors is fundamentally limited by the low intrinsic carrier mobility of colloidal QDs, which significantly hinders charge transport. In addition, conventional detector architectures typically provide insufficient internal gain, thereby restricting detection sensitivity, particularly under weak infrared illumination. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid avalanche photodetector that integrates a halogen-passivated PbS QDs absorption layer with a silicon multiplication region. After absorbing incident infrared photons in the QDs layer, photoexcited electrons are efficiently injected into the silicon multiplication region. The accelerated carriers then induce impact ionization, which enables strong avalanche multiplication and yields high internal gain for efficient carrier collection. Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations indicate that the proposed device delivers a responsivity of 29.5 A/W at a wavelength of 1550 nm, accompanied by fast rise and fall times of 305 ps and 306 ps, respectively. By integrating the spectral tunability of PbS QDs with the robust avalanche gain offered by mature silicon platforms, this architecture provides a highly promising, CMOS-compatible route toward next-generation, high-sensitivity infrared photodetection.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 77Poster Number:NSS-01-077] Characterization and Radiation Damage Mitigation of Silicon Photomultipliers for Low Earth Orbit Applications (#1902)
sub_talks.speaker: S. Davarpanah
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Université de Genève, Département de physique nucléaire et corpusculaire, Genève, Genève, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) are attractive photosensors for space applications because of their compact size, low cost, low operating voltage, high photon detection efficiency (PDE), and single-photon sensitivity. Their use in space applications, however, is limited by radiation-induced increases in dark count rate (DCR). This work presents the characterization and radiation tolerance study of FBK NUV-HD-MT SiPMs for the focal plane of the Terzina Cherenkov telescope onboard the NUSES mission, which will operate in a Sun-synchronous low Earth orbit (LEO) at an altitude of approximately 550 km. Devices with micro-cell sizes ranging from 25 to 50 μm were evaluated through a comprehensive characterization campaign comprising static (current-voltage), dynamic (noise and pulse-shape), and optical (photon detection efficiency) measurements to identify the sensor configuration best suited for this application. The 30 μm bare sensors were selected as the optimal solution, achieving a PDE greater than 50% at 400 nm, optical cross-talk below 2%, and a DCR below 60 kHz/mm 2 at 10 V overvoltage. The radiation environment was modeled using SPENVIS, and dose deposition in the focal plane was evaluated with Geant4 simulations. In parallel, radiation effects were investigated experimentally through two irradiation campaigns: a 50 MeV proton beam test and electron exposure using a Sr-90 source. Proton-induced damage produced a significant increase in leakage current and DCR, while electron-induced degradation was substantially smaller. Temperature-dependent measurements were used to extrapolate in-orbit performance and to evaluate recovery through thermal annealing. The results indicate that performing periodic annealing cycles at temperatures above 50°C can reduce the radiation-induced current by up to 40% after approximately 84 hours, helping preserve detector performance over the three-year mission.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 79Poster Number:NSS-01-079] Toward SiPM Single-Photon Detection Matrix using Ultrafast, Low Power RF Readout (#1939)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. F. Yvon (Autores: R. Belkacem , D. F. Yvon , D. Baudin , D. Breton)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CEA Saclay / Univ. Paris-Saclay, IRFU/DPhP, Gif sur Yvette, France [2] CEA Saclay / Univ. Paris-Saclay, IRFU/DEDIP, Gif sur Yvette, France [3] CNRS-IN2P3/ Univ. Paris-Saclay, IJCLab, Orsay, France [4] UMR BioMaps/ Univ. Paris-Saclay, Orsay, France
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract To enable the readout of fast signals from SiPM arrays, we have developed a SiPM chip readout based on a compact, low-power radio-frequency preamplifier, thus avoiding the use of ASICs. On a 16 mm² SiPM operating in single photoelectron mode, we measure a rise time of 450 ps and a timing resolution (SPTR) of 84 ps (FWHM), while amplifying the fast component of the SiPM pulses. Furthermore, the active output impedance of the preamplifier is on the order of kΩ, allowing these chips to be mounted along a transmission line without significantly affecting signal propagation. This enables the implementation of dense SiPM lines or arrays, reducing the number of digitization channels required for readout. Finally, an optimized passive pole-zero compensation network, placed at the ends of the line, suppresses the slow component of the SiPM pulses and achieves critical damping of the fast pulse shapes. Thus, pulse pile-up, expected during multiplexing of SiPM photodetectors, can be controlled even at high counting rates. We are currently working on the assembly of such SiPM arrays. We measured a Coincidence Time Resolution of 69 ps (FWHM) using a 9 mm 3 LYSO crystal + SiPM spectrometers with our readout electronics.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 81Poster Number:NSS-01-081] FPGA-Based Real-Time SiPM Emulator with Sub-Nanosecond Temporal Quantization (#1987)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Carsi (Autores: A. Abba , S. Carsi , F. Caponio , E. Proserpio , V. Arosio)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Nuclear Instruments SRL, Lambrugo, Italy [2] Università dell'Insubria, Como, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This work presents a real-time FPGA-based Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) detector emulator capable of reproducing physically accurate detector waveforms at 16-bit resolution and 2.5 GS/s analog output rate. The proposed architecture combines microscopic event simulation with a temporally quantized event-streaming model, enabling real-time waveform synthesis directly inside FPGA logic while drastically reducing bandwidth requirements compared to traditional waveform streaming approaches. The emulator separates event generation from signal shaping: software layers generate timestamped photon-hit sequences derived either from analytical distributions, Geant4 simulations, or SimSiPM microscopic detector models, while the FPGA reconstructs the analog waveform through parallel Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) filter banks implementing the SiPM transfer function; a look-ahead recursive transformation enables II = 1 operation across all banks at 156.25 MHz, consuming approximately 235 DSP48E2 slices. A multi-phase temporal quantization architecture provides 0.8 ns effective timing precision using a 156.25 MHz fabric clock and eight temporal sub-phases. Experimental validation demonstrates excellent agreement between hardware-generated waveforms and analytical as well as SimSiPM-generated references, including pile-up scenarios with overlapping scintillation events reproduced through linear superposition. The prototype operates with an end-to-end latency of approximately 83 ns.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 83Poster Number:NSS-01-083] Design and Single-Cell Verification of an Integrated Temperature-Compensation Architecture for Digital SiPMs in Extreme Environments (#2580)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 O. Jinseok (Autores: O. Jinseok , H. Seop , K. Seo-Ryong , K. Inyong)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea University of Science and Technology (UST), Daejeon, Republic of Korea [2] Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute (KAERI), Daejeon, Republic of Korea [3] Yonsei University, Wonju, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the single-cell design and verification of a digital SiPM building block with an integrated temperature-compensation architecture that eliminates external sensors by exploiting SPAD output-amplitude tracking as an intrinsic thermal indicator. A low-power SPAD with a P+/N-well junction and P-well guard ring was fabricated in a 180 nm CMOS process, exhibiting a 10.3 V breakdown voltage, while the digital-cell employs a high-speed comparator to suppress pulse-width variation and premature edge breakdown. The extracted amplitude trend drives an integrated PMIC in a closed loop to dynamically adjust the SPAD bias, maintaining a constant overvoltage and providing instantaneous compensation for thermal drifts.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 85Poster Number:NSS-01-085] Graphene Photodetectors for Vacuum-UV Through Visible Wavelengths (#3124)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Lindman (Autores: A. Lindman , M. Turqueti , L. Schlueter , G. R. Araujo)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, United States of America [2] University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Many experiments rely on measuring vacuum-ultraviolet light, which is emitted in situations as diverse as scintillation in cryogenic liquid noble gases (126.8 nm in argon) and laser spectroscopy of atomic hydrogen isotopes (121.6 nm). Graphene-monolayer photodetectors offer several attractive traits: they are naturally thin, sensitive to a broad range of wavelengths, relatively simple to fabricate (including with integrated readout circuitry with the same process), and can be made on flexible substrates. We present measurements with visible and UV light down to 115 nm, including at low intensity and with fast pulses, of graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) of various sizes up to 2 mm square fabricated on silicon. These detectors show promise for experiments from neutrinoless double beta decay searches to absolute neutrino mass measurements, as well as dark-matter searches or other VUV-detection applications.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 87Poster Number:NSS-01-087] Development of a PLL-less 6.25Gbps Serializer and CML Transmitter for the LCLS-II Upgrade (#1129)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Gupta (Autores: G. Liu , H. Sandberg , A. Pena Perez , B. Markovic , A. Gupta , H. Kim , L. Rota , D. Doering , L. Ruckman)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Stanford University, SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, California, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Linac Coherent Light Source (LCLS) at SLAC National Laboratory has been going through a major upgrade, called LCLS-II, where the repetition rates are increasing from 120Hz to almost a MegaHertz. Custom ASICs that support x-ray data measurements at these rates are in development for both full frame and sparse data readout. For these ASIC designs we are departing from conventional internal PLL architectures, and instead implementing a 6.25 Gbps serializer with high-speed current-mode logic (CML) receivers (for clock) and transmitters (for data). This approach simplifies the whole chip design, reduces the power consumption and minimizes the noise sensitivity between the high-speed data path and the low-noise front-end blocks. This paper presents detailed performance measurements in a prototype ASIC, followed by the description of their circuit design and implementation.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 89Poster Number:NSS-01-089] Performance Evaluation of Differential Amplifiers for Fast Scintillating Fiber Readout in Proton Therapy (#1449)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Deniz (Autores: B. Deniz , A. Eksim)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] TUBITAK BILGEM, KOCAELI, Turkey [2] Gebze Technical University, KOCAELI, Turkey
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Real time range verification in proton therapy requires analog front end electronics that can process fast, low amplitude signals from scintillating fibers with sub nanosecond precision. This work compares two COTS differential amplifiers (ADA4930 vs. ADA4938) for the NOVO project's detector. Using actual scintillator derived PWL pulses (0.3 V peak, 18 ns rise time) and a 5th order 250 MHz Butterworth filter, we show that small signal bandwidth governs transient performance. The ADA4930 achieved 660 V/µs pre filter and 350.56 V/µs post filter slew rate, versus 550 and 289.44 V/µs for the ADA4938. Noise analysis reveals the ADA4930 is "resistor noise limited" (61.4% passive resistors), while the ADA4938 is "IC noise limited" (71.6% internal noise). The ADA4930 yields SNR = 65 dB and ENOB = 10.6 bits, outperforming the ADA4938 (62 dB, 10.0 bits). The ADA4930 is therefore the optimal driver for maximizing slope to noise ratio and minimizing timing jitter.
