sub_talks.title: [NSS-07-05] Enhanced Light Outputs in Cs 2 ZnCl 4 Single Crystals via Hydrothermal Purification and Cd Doping (#2781)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Deng (Autores: Y. Wu , M. Deng , S. Wang , J. Ma , T. Wu , J. Chen)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, State Key Laboratory of Functional Crystals and Devices, Shanghai, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Cs 2 ZnCl 4 single crystals exhibit ultrafast cross-luminescence and show great potential for high-repetition-rate and fast timing radiation detection areas. However, their light output is severely limited by synthesis-induced impurities and intrinsic defects. To address this bottleneck, this work systematically investigates two parallel strategies: hydrothermal purification and Cd doping. High optical-quality single crystals were grown via the vertical Bridgman method using hydrothermally purified method, followed by systematic optical transmittance, luminescence, and absolute light output characterizations. The results demonstrate that hydrothermal purification effectively eliminates heavy metal impurities in the precursors, significantly enhancing the light output (LO) from 680 ph/MeV to 1078 ph/MeV (a 58.5% increase) while fully preserving the crystal's ultrafast decay constant of 1.76 ns. Furthermore, Cd doping increases the light output to 3689 ph/MeV, representing an enhancement of 126.6%. This study provides two effective strategies for enhancing the light output of ultrafast halide light-emitting materials.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-07-06] Scintillation Properties of Ce 3+ -, Pr 3+ -, and Eu 2+ -Doped LiCl, LiBr, and LiI Single Crystals (#2238)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Glodo (Autores: J. Glodo , E. van Loef , L. Soundara Pandian)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Radiation Monitoring Devices, Inc., Watertown, Massachusetts, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Lithium-rich scintillators are widely used to detect thermal neutrons, with Eu-doped lithium iodide (LiI:Eu) serving as the long-standing benchmark. LiI:Eu, however, has high gamma sensitivity, slow scintillation decay, and limited ability to distinguish neutrons from gamma rays. As a result, we have shifted our focus towards the lighter binary lithium halides, such as lithium chloride (LiCl) and lithium bromide (LiBr), which offer intrinsically lower gamma sensitivity. We also investigated Ce 3+ and Pr 3+ with the goal of evaluating their ability for fast d-f type emission and neutron-gamma discrimination. Single crystals were grown by the vertical Bridgman method and characterized by X-ray luminescence, light yield, decay time, and neutron response using a moderated Am/Be source. Initial results show that LiBr:Ce delivers a clear thermal-neutron peak at 3.1 MeVee with a light yield of 7,300 ph/n (comparable to GS20) and pulse-shape discrimination capability. Full data and comparison across all dopant-host combinations will be presented.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-07-07] Characterising ZnSe(Al,O) for Real-Time Sr-90 Beta Spectroscopy (#2965)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Kolnikaj (Autores: A. Kolnikaj , K. A.A. Gamage , O. Popoola)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Glasgow, James Watt School of Engineering, Glasgow, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract ZnSe(Al,O) is a promising scintillator for compact beta spectroscopy, but its detector-relevant properties are poorly documented and strongly dependent on dopant composition, growth quality, and optical transport. This work experimentally characterises a commercially supplied ZnSe(Al,O) crystal intended for use in a silicon photomultiplier-coupled beta detector for strontium-90 monitoring. The crystal measured 42 mm in diameter and 2.1 mm in thickness. Scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirmed a zinc selenide composition with aluminium and oxygen impurities, giving measured atomic abundances of 49.2% zinc, 46.1% selenium, 3.50% oxygen, and 1.2% aluminium. The measured density was 5.31 g cm^−3, and the refractive index determined using a Brewster-angle method was 2.475. Scintillation waveforms were recorded under strontium-90/yttrium-90 beta irradiation using silicon photomultiplier readout and analysed to extract charge spectra and decay behaviour. The light yield was estimated to be approximately 7.8 × 10$^4$ photons MeV^−1, while the decay constant was measured as 9.41 us, with a waveform-to-waveform standard deviation of 1.1 us. These values are broadly consistent with the range reported for zinc-selenide-based scintillators, while providing a single experimentally derived parameter set for this specific ZnSe(Al,O) sample. The results support the suitability of ZnSe(Al,O) for silicon photomultiplier-based beta spectroscopy and provide material inputs required for improved detector modelling, optical design, and future development of compact detectors for environmental strontium-90 monitoring.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-07-08] Exploring wavelength-shifting properties of nanocrystal layers and nanocomposites (#3052)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 V. Zabloudil (Autores: V. Zabloudil , J. Kral , V. Masek , J. Delenne , J.-L. Faure , S. Rojas , E. Auffray)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CERN, Geneva, Switzerland [2] Czech Technical University in Prague, Prague, Czech Republic [3] Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic [4] Université de Strasbourg, UMR7178, CNRS, IPHC, Strasbourg, France [5] CEA Saclay, Paris, France
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Efficient detection of fast ultraviolet scintillation is essential for the next generation of high-speed radiation detectors. We investigate CsPbX 3 nanocrystals as a versatile wavelength-shifting platform, leveraging their sub-nanosecond response times and tunable bandgaps to match the peak sensitivity of standard photodetectors. As a proof-of-concept, using radioluminescence measurements, we characterize the conversion of scintillation light from a LYSO:Ce reference crystal by CsPbBr 3 nanocrystal layers and polymer-based nanocomposites. It has been observed that concentrated drop-cast layers perform better than nanocomposites and achieve total extinction of the broad scintillation peak of LYSO:Ce at 430 nm, shifting it to 535 nm, corresponding to the nanocrystal emission. Rigorous validation tests confirm that the observed green emission is a product of wavelength-shifting rather than a result of direct nanocrystal excitation or spectral attenuation of the primary light. This performance establishes a foundation for modular wavelength-shifting interfaces that can be tailored to various scintillators and radiators, including BaF 2 (cross-luminescence), CeF 3 , and PbF 2 (Cherenkov light).

sub_talks.title: [JS-01-01] Uniformity, Stability and High-Flux X-ray Detection Performance of FAPbBr 3 , CsPbBr 3 and CZT (#2658)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 I. Braddock (Autores: I. Braddock , W. Brown , S. Cardiff , V. Dhamgaye , O. Fox , J. Jayarathne , S. Joshi , D. McAleer , G. Tumen-Ulzii , T. Nicholls , K. Sawhney , P. Sellin , S. Stranks , M. Veale)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Science and Technology Facilities Council, Rutherford Appleton Laboratory, Harwell, United Kingdom [2] University of Cambridge, Department of Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology, Cambridge, United Kingdom [3] University of Surrey, School of Mathematics and Physics, Guildford, United Kingdom [4] Diamond Light Source, Harwell, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Pixel detectors for X-ray science typically require pixel pitches of less than 1 mm and operation at photon fluxes greater than 10 9 ph s −1 mm 2 . For lead halide perovskite detectors to be viable in these applications, they must demonstrate good spatial uniformity, as well as operational stability over a period of hours or days. Here, we present results of synchrotron experiments in which the detection performance of melt-grown CsPbBr 3 devices, solution-grown FAPbBr 3 devices and CZT were each measured at 20 keV X-ray fluxes up to 10 9 ph/s/mm 2 , demonstrating the linear response of the material to changing X-ray fluxes. Microbeam maps of device response to single-photon fluxes of 50 keV X-rays were used to quantify spatial variations in the charge collection efficiency and rise time of events.

sub_talks.title: [JS-01-02] Estimating requirements for scintillator-based photon counting detectors in CT (#1502)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Hsieh (Autores: S. Hsieh , S. Lee , B. Wilson , P. Mondal , D. Schaart)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Mayo Clinic, Radiology, Rochester, Minnesota, United States of America [2] TU Delft, Radiation Sciences & Technology, Delft, Netherlands
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Scintillator-based photon counting detectors (PCDs) couple a fast scintillator with a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) and associated readout electronics. The characteristics of the scintillator and SiPM that are required for competitive performance are not yet clear, and it is sometimes felt that bright scintillators and high photodetection efficiency are needed. We use numerical modeling to study this question, using a cascaded system model with multiple stages to quantify the effects of light yield, SiPM sensitivity, and energy binning. Effects such as SiPM saturation, Swank noise, and K-escape are also included as optional stages. We find that using relatively dim components (5x dimmer than that assumed in previous modeling studies) introduces little harm into spectral imaging tasks, but the penalty of K-escape is large. Future prototype detectors should emphasize K-escape, stopping power, and speed rather than light yield or photodetection efficiency.

sub_talks.title: [JS-01-03] A four side buttable system in package for medical and industrial Photon-Counting CT (#1574)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 T. Solf (Autores: T. Solf , T. Froehlich , E. Hostalet , R. Kanan)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] AMS Osram, Garching, Germany, Germany [2] AMS Osram, Jona, Switzerland [3] AMS Osram, Valencia, Spain
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We present the second generation of a four-side buttable module solution (AS592xM) for spectral CT detectors with a pixel matrix of 72x24 covering an area of 24.5 mm x 8.57 mm with a pitch of 365 µm x 340 µm. In combination with a suitable direct detection material like CdTe or CZT it detects individual X-ray photons with five programmable thresholds. Improvements have been made to reduce power consumption down to 0.35mW/pixel while maintaining low noise performance (380 e rms). Count rate stability is based on two different methods: a static leakage compensation (SLC) as well as a base line restorer circuit (BLR). The new SLC in combination with an auto-zero scheme in the frontend suppresses the effect of potential 1/f and Random Telegraph Noise (RTN) noise from the amplifiers. The adjustable BLR compensates for static and dynamic baseline shifts up to 700nA of leakage current per pixel. Measurements with and without CZT will be shown to quantify the energy resolution and count rate stability over input flux for different operation modes to quantify S/N for the different energy bins. Additionally, the MTF is characterized to project spatial resolution on system level.

sub_talks.title: [JS-01-04] A Vibrational-Scanning Single-Photon Emission Microscope (SPEM) for In Vivo 3-D Autoradiography of Targeted Alpha Therapy (#3062)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 W. Zhang (Autores: W. Zhang , Y. Jin , S. Mandot , S. Shu , E. Zannoni , L. Meng)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Department of Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering, Champaign, Illinois, United States of America [2] University of Texas at Austin, Walker Department of Mechanical Engineering, Austin, Texas, United States of America [3] University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Department of Bioengineering, Champaign, Illinois, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In this presentation, we will report the design and imaging performance of our third-generation Alpha-SPECT-mini system (the Alpha-SPECT-mini-ZM, where ZM stands for Zoom-in Microscope), which combines ultra-narrow micro-ring collimators and a vibrational aperture-scanning scheme to provide ultrahigh spatial resolution for in vivo 3-D autoradiography of α-RPT in small lab animals. The system uses a cylindrical ring of 10 detector panels, each comprising 2×6 HEXITEC/CZT detector modules. Each CZT module has a 2×2 cm 2 active area with 80×80 pixel array at 250 μm pitch and offers 1.5 keV FWHM energy resolution at 122 keV. The Alpha-SPECT-mini-ZM system uses a two-section collimator ring that combines pinhole apertures for whole-body imaging and ultra-narrow micro-ring apertures for zoomed-in ultrahigh-resolution imaging of a focal area with a 5-mm-diameter FOV, switched via a motorized stage. To offer an ultrahigh imaging resolution that overcomes the limited detector pixel size, the system employs a vibrational scanning strategy with MUCRB-guided acquisition optimization. Preliminary simulations with micro-hot-rod phantoms show the micro-ring collimator achieving better than 160 μm resolution at practical sensitivity. Further phantom studies will be carried out to characterize the performance of the system.

sub_talks.title: [JS-01-05] Multi-Agent Pipeline with Local Large Language Models for Automated MCNP Script Review (#1447)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Jeon (Autores: B. Jeon , S. Lim)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, Artificial Intelligence Section, Daejeon, Republic of Korea [2] Quamtum Beam Solution, Daejeon, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Although large language models (LLMs) perform well on general-purpose programming tasks, their accuracy drops sharply when applied to domain-specific simulation codes such as Monte Carlo N-Particle (MCNP). Within the nuclear sector, security policies and export-control rules typically forbid uploading inputs to cloud-hosted LLM services, so review tools must instead run on-premise atop openly released models. This study introduces a coordinated multi-agent framework that automatically inspects and repairs MCNP input decks. Three role-specific agents-a Supervisor, a Fixer, and a Validator-drive the workflow, supported by 16 auxiliary tools and an optional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module that consults the MCNP user manual. To measure performance, we assembled a 360-case benchmark covering six representative nuclear-engineering scenarios. Our pipeline reaches a 75.8% success rate, exceeding a single-agent reference by 15.5 percentage points and confirming that role-based orchestration is an effective strategy for trustworthy MCNP code repair in fully local deployments.

sub_talks.title: [JS-01-06] A Compact Educational Platform for Demonstrating TDAQ Concepts in Particle Detector Systems (#1734)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 R. Giordano (Autores: R. Giordano , M. Cuciuc)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Naples "Federico II", Naples, Italy [2] INFN, Naples, Italy, Naples, Italy [3] Extreme Light Infrastructure - Nuclear Physics, IFIN-HH, Magurele, Romania [4] Pomelo Instrumentation SRL, Bucarest, Romania
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Particle physics experiments rely on complex detectors, where trigger and data acquisition (TDAQ) systems play a key role. These systems are typically expensive, large-scale, and accessible only in specialized laboratories, limiting students' early exposure to the fundamentals of TDAQ. To address this gap, we developed a compact, low-cost educational platform that reproduces the main elements of a particle-detector readout chain in a form suitable for university laboratories. The platform is based on an Arduino UNO R4 Wi-Fi, a custom piggy-back board, and a detector module consisting of a CsI(Tl) scintillator coupled to a silicon photomultiplier. The system integrates bias-voltage generation and temperature monitoring, programmable pulse amplitude discrimination, peak detection, digitization, and USB or Wi-Fi data transfer to a personal computer. The platform enables students to explore the main TDAQ concepts, including trigger formation, latency, dead time, buffering, and threshold setting. By progressively implementing different firmware strategies, from simple trigger polling to interrupt-driven and hardware-assisted acquisition, students gain direct insight into the relation between system design and detector performance. Educational activities on slow control, such as bias-voltage calibration, detector monitoring, and gain stabilization, are also possible. After firmware development, students can perform gamma-spectroscopy measurements using low-activity radioactive materials. Examples include potassium chloride salt substitutes, where the 1460.8 keV photopeak from 40 K can be observed, and thoriated tungsten welding electrodes, which exhibit several gamma lines from thorium decay products. In this contribution, we discuss the platform, the TDAQ topics addressed, and student experiments that demonstrate its educational potential.

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-02] Systematic Defect and Crystal-Field Engineering of LYSO-U Scintillators for Photon-Counting CT (#2274)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. Ding (Autores: C. Li , Z. Xue , P. Qiu , S. Zhao , B. Zhao , B. Liu , D. Ding)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Chinese Academy of Sciences, State Key Laboratory of Functional Crystals and Devices, Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Shanghai, China [2] Center of Materials Science and Optoelectronics Engineering, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China [3] Nuctech Company Limited, Beijing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) requires scintillators with ultrafast decay times, ultralow afterglow, and high light yields (LY) to prevent pulse pile-up and image ghosting under continuous high-flux X-rays. While cerium-doped lutetium yttrium oxyorthosilicate (LYSO:Ce) is a benchmark material, its intrinsic ~40 ns decay time and deep-trap-induced afterglow constrain its PCCT applications. This work demonstrates systematic defect and crystal-field engineering to modify LYSO:Ce crystals, establishing a highly customizable material platform. Four distinct codoping strategies are evaluated to overcome the speed-efficiency-afterglow trade-offs. First, multi-site co-doping was employed to convert Ce 3+ in ultrafast LYSO (LYSO-U) scintillation crystals into fast-emitting Ce 4+ , introducing a non-radiative path within the crystal. This breaks the intrinsic lifetime barrier, achieving a 7.3 ns decay component and suppressing afterglow to 0.02% at 40 ms, while preserving an LY of 25,000 photons/MeV. Second, multivalent Al/Mn codoping utilizes bidirectional energy transfer to deliver a 9.6 ns decay, 446 ppm afterglow at 40 ms, and an LY of 31,300 photons/MeV. Third, isovalent Ge substitution (LYSGO:Ce) increases local crystal-field splitting to thermodynamically deepen emitting states for enhanced carrier capture, elevating the LY to 38,700 photons/MeV and supporting a 25.6 lp/mm spatial resolution. Finally, trace Co 2+ doping (~330 ppm) passivates oxygen-vacancy traps without severe lattice distortion, boosting the LY to 37,800 photons/MeV. By elucidating these physical mechanisms, these tailored, charge-sharing-free scintillator platforms address the diverse architectural demands of advanced PCCT detectors.

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-03] Energy resolved imaging with a fine-pitch YAGG-SiPM based indirect photon counting detector (#2087)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Shimazoe (Autores: K. Shimazoe , Y. Kobayashi , K. Kamada , Y. Shoji , M. Yoshino , K. Sakamoto , F. Acerbi , A. Gola)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Scintillation based photon counting detectors (PCDs) attracts great interest because of its fast time response, crystal separation to suppress the charge sharing and wider choices of sophisticated scintillation crytals. We have designed and fabricated a custom fine-pitch (250 μ m) 10 × 10 Ce:YAGG- SiPM array whose size is comparable to the current commercial compound semiconductor based PCD. The performance was characterized in terms of energy resolution, spatial resolution, count rate capability and imaging capability. The measured results shows 28% @ 122 keV moderate energy resolution, 2.9 LP/mm spatial resolution comparable to the existing CT, 20 Mcps/mm2 at 20 % loss count rate capability. The comparison between YAGG and GFAG shows the significant supression of K-α escape cross-talk in the energy spectrum. The investigation with other scintillation crystals, such as LYSO will be shown. The different concentration of Optiray contrast agent (Iodine) with 10 m-50 mg/mL was clearly identified with 4 thresholds photon counting system.

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-04] Latest update on the glass-less TSV FBK SiPM for 2.5D integrated ToF-PET modules (#2474)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Penna (Autores: M. Penna , C. Trippl , F. Acerbi , I. Hany , F. Caso , J. Dalmasson , R. Dolenec , D. O.E. Elgewaily , A. Ficorella , P. Kachru , D. Mazzanti , L. Parellada-Monreal , G. Paternoster , M. Ruzzarin , A. Sanuy , O. A.M. Villarreal , N. Zorzi , R. Ballabriga , J.M. Benlloch , G. El Fakhri , D. Gascon , S. Majewski , R. Pestotnik , A. Gola)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Fondazione Bruno Kessler, Povo, Italy [2] CERN, Meyrin, Switzerland [3] Jozef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana, Slovenia [4] ICCUB, University of Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain [5] UPV, Instituto de Instrumentacion Para Imagen Molecular, Velencia, Spain [6] Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, United States of America [7] University of California Davis, Davis, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In this work, the latest developments in glass-less Through-Silicon Via (TSV) integration of FBK NUV-HD-MT Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs), targeting next-generation Time-of-Flight Positron Emission Tomography (ToF-PET) detectors in the framework of the PetVision project, are presented. The NUV-HD-MT technology platform provides an outstanding baseline for TSV integration, featuring Photon Detection Efficiency (PDE) exceeding $65\%$ at $420\ \text{nm}$, optical crosstalk below $5\%$ at $15\ \text{V}$ excess bias, and a Single-Photon Time Resolution (SPTR) as low as $\simeq 18\ \text{ps}$ FWHM for a single SPAD. The glass-less TSV architecture eliminates any permanent intermediate layer at the scintillator interface by removing the temporary glass carrier after backside thinning to $150\ \mu\text{m}$, enabling optimal optical coupling and preserving the fast-timing performance of the underlying technology. The TSV development follows a structured, learning-cycle-based R\&D approach. Preliminary characterization of the Learning Cycle 1 (LC1) front-side production confirms that timing performance remains at state-of-the-art levels, with a Coincidence Time Resolution (CTR) of $\simeq 75\ \text{ps}$ FWHM achieved using a $3\times3\ \text{mm}^2$ SiPM coupled to a $2.8\times2.8\times3\ \text{mm}^3$ L(Y)SO:Ce:Ca scintillator, and an SPTR of $\simeq 25\ \text{ps}$ FWHM obtained for a single $50\ \mu\text{m}$ SPAD. Back-side processing of the LC1 wafers has been completed and full electrical and functional characterization is now underway. The Learning Cycle 2 (LC2) design, featuring an optimized $4\times2$ SiPM array with a $3\ \text{mm}$ channel pitch for direct crystal matrix coupling and a reduced TSV count of one per channel for improved yield, represents a significant step toward a robust, production-ready solution.

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-05] The DIGILOG Project: µSiPM Sensor and Sub-20 ps Readout Electronics for ToF-PET (#2623)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Bisi (Autores: S. Bisi , K. Herweg , A. Muntean , D. Schug , V. Schulz , L. Parellada-Monreal , M. Penna , A. Gola , S. Gundacker , M. Motoyoshi , C. Bruschini , E. Charbon)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Advanced Quantum Architecture Lab, Neuchatel, Neuchâtel, Switzerland [2] RWTH Aachen University, University Hospital RWTH Aachen, Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [3] RWTH Aachen University, Institute of Imaging and Computer Vision, Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [4] NovoViz S.A., Neuchatel, Neuchâtel, Neuchâtel, Switzerland [5] Hyperion Hybrid Imaging Systems GmbH, Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [6] Fondazione Bruno Kessler, Trento, Italy [7] Marietta Blau Institute for Particle Physics, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna, Wien, Austria [8] Tohoku-MicroTec Co., Ltd., Sendai, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In time-of-flight PET, coincidence time resolution (CTR) is essential, with the ultimate aim of reaching 10 ps CTR [1]. Cherenkov radiation in BGO crystals, offers a path toward this target, but its low photon yield demands detectors combining high photon detection efficiency, low dark count rate, and fast single-photon time resolution (SPTR) [2]. In DIGILOG, we segment state-of-the-art analog SiPMs into smaller clusters called µSiPMs [3]. With fewer SPADs per cell, µSiPMs have lower capacitive loading, enabling simpler, faster electronic interfaces and higher-resolution timestamping via time-to-digital converters (TDCs) in proximity through 3D stacking. Optical and system-level simulations identify a granularity of 6×6 SPADs per µSiPM (100 µSiPMs in 3×3 mm²) as optimal for Cherenkov-based BGO timing [4]. The µSiPM top tier, fabricated by FBK in NUV-HD-MT technology [5], uses Single-Cell TSVs for independent microcell cathode access without fill-factor loss. We present two 110 nm CMOS readout architectures, both based on a current-mirror front-end, a Vernier ring-oscillator TDC [6], and a serial interface. Two ring oscillators run at slightly different frequencies setting the LSB; the sequences are compared as in a Vernier line until pulses align, and T is computed from the counts n1 and n2. The first implementation, an 8×8 TDC array with 20 ps target LSB, has been fabricated; a Vernier LSB of 19 ps and 4.4 ps RMS jitter have been measured [7]. The second upscales to a 9×9 array with three TDCs per µSiPM on independent threshold levels of a multi-level comparator, enabling MD-SiPM-like operation [8] and order-statistics-based timing [9]. It targets a 6 ps LSB at 2.0 mW per channel, with an on-chip PLL (<5 ps FWHM jitter) stabilizing the oscillators against PVT. Post-layout simulations yield SPTR <20 ps (FWHM) and INL ±1.1 LSB. Die-to-die 3D bonding of the two tiers is ongoing at T-Micro.

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-06] Real-Time DOI Layer Prediction in TOF-PET Detectors via FPGA Neural Network (#2254)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Xin (Autores: S. Xin , Z. Han , X. Zhang , X. Lv , S. Chu)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] united imaging, MI, Shanghai, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Depth-of-interaction (DOI) information is critical for improving time-of-flight (TOF) precision in positron emission tomography (PET) detectors. Traditional DOI estimation methods, such as dual-ended readout and layered crystal arrays, require complex fabrication or additional photodetector channels, increasing system cost and degrading timing performance. This paper presents a machine learning framework for real-time DOI layer prediction in single-ended readout LYSO crystal arrays (5×6 structure coupled to a 2×2 SiPM array). A neural network takes normalized SiPM energy ratios and crystal position as inputs and outputs DOI classification into 2, 3, or 6 depth layers. A symmetry-based training strategy is introduced to enhance model generalization across crystal positions, effectively quadrupling the training data through rotational coordinate transformations. Experiments with a collimated ²²Na source demonstrate classification accuracy of 40-80% across six depth layers. Validation using top radiation data confirms the model's generalization from lateral irradiation (training) to normal incidence (clinical deployment). DOI-corrected coincidence time resolution (CTR) evaluated on 4320 crystals shows improvements of 2.25 ps (2-layer), 3.41 ps (3-layer), and 5.18 ps (6-layer). The two-layer neural network has been implemented on FPGA with fixed-point arithmetic, achieving a processing rate for real-time inference. Ongoing work focuses on system-level integration and image quality evaluation.

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-07] Physics-Informed Deep Learning on FPGA for Inter-Crystal Scattering Correction in ToF-CT (#1776)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Jdid (Autores: L. Jdid , R. Fontaine , A. C. Therrien)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Université de Sherbrooke, Interdisciplinary Institute for Technological Innovation, Sherbrooke, Québec, Canada
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Time-of-Flight Computed Tomography (ToF-CT) enhances contrast-to-noise ratio by suppressing patient-scattered photons. However, the fine pixel pitch required for sub-millimeter spatial resolution intensifies inter-crystal scattering (ICS), a confounder that conventional energy-based discrimination cannot resolve under polychromatic X-ray sources, ultimately compromising spatial resolution. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the first real-time, physics-informed ICS correction framework deployed at the FPGA-based detector readout of ToF-CT systems. Built on Physics-Informed Knowledge Distillation (PI-KD), the framework compresses a high-capacity teacher (AUPRC = 0.99) into a compact student architecture suitable for embedded deployment. Specifically, the distillation objective constrains the student to remain consistent with Klein-Nishina scattering kinematics and Monte Carlo-derived interaction priors, thereby preserving the physical structure of its spatiotemporal and energetic representations under aggressive compression. Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) further enables hardware-native INT8 inference, reducing the parameter footprint to ∼2.3 kB with negligible performance loss. Post-synthesis on a Xilinx ZCU104 at a 200 MHz target clock confirms real-time operation beyond the 1 MHz acquisition target, sustaining 1.32 MHz per inference instance with 0.83 µs latency, while INT8 LUT-based arithmetic leaves all DSP blocks free (28% LUT, 38% BRAM, 0% DSP).

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-08] Cherenkov Photon Counting, Labeling, and Multi-Photon Timing Estimation for sub-100 ps CTR BGO TOF-PET Detectors (#2761)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. W. Cates (Autores: J. W. Cates , S. Lee , R. Heller , W.-S. Choong)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Applied Nuclear Physics, Berkeley, California, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We have developed a bismuth germanate (BGO) Cherenkov and Scintillation photon counting time-of-flight positron emission tomography (TOF-PET) detector which can count and provide unique timestamps for detected optical photons. This allows 511 keV photon time of interaction estimators to be derived from the prompt Cherenkov light without influence from scintillation light, which has a much higher variance from time of detection. This detector concept is also capable of three-dimensional positioning of 511 keV photon interactions, allowing for position and depth-of-interaction dependent optical transit time skew corrections to be applied to the prompt estimators. Information from this detector concept can be used to classify each detected optical photon as Cherenkov or scintillation. In this work, we show how labeling each detected photon as Cherenkov/scintillation and only incorporating prompt information into a timing estimator that averages timestamps for events with more than one detected Cherenkov photon significantly improves both achievable coincidence time resolution with BGO and also the TOF kernel shape by significantly reducing the long tails from time pickoff on scintillation light. We constructed a 16x16x15 mm 3 BGO photon counting detector prototype and evaluated its performance in coincidence with a fast reference detector. Incorporating the information from multiple labeled Cherenkov photons improved CTR from 159 ps to 137 ps FWHM, and the long scintillation tail was reduced to a small fraction of the total coincidence distribution. When considering all events with at least one Cherenkov photon detected, CTR was 122 ps FWHM with a Gaussian kernel shape. CTR improved to ≤100 ps for events containing 2 or more detected Cherenkov photons. We present these methods, along with a new detector concept with high Cherenkov photon detection efficiency to enable ≤100 ps CTR in a BGO TOF-PET detectors that also have high 511 keV photon detection efficiency.

sub_talks.title: [JS-02-09] 3D-cylindrical microdetector arrays for microdosimetryin proton therapy (#2475)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 C. Guardiola (Autores: C. Riera-Llobet , C. Fleta , P. Ibáñez , I. López , C. Guardiola)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] National Center of Microelectronics (IMB-CNM, CSIC), Radiation Detectors Group, Barcelona, Spain [2] Univ. Complutense de Madrid (UCM), Nuclear Physics Group, Madrid, Spain
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Proton therapy provides high dose conformity, improving protection of organs at risk, especially for radioresistant tumours, sensitive locations, and paediatric cases. However, reported toxicities may be linked to high linear energy transfer (LET) effects. To address this issue, IMB-CNM has developed a new radiation detector architecture [1]: 3D-cylindrical silicon microdetectors, with micrometre-scale sensitivity to quantify LET. Starting from this kernel, different configurations have been designed and fabricated to cover a wide range of resolutions and radiation sensitive areas from a 11 × 11 array (2 mm × 2 mm) [2] to a linear array of 200 of those microdetectors covering 0.4 mm × 12 cm [3, 4], among others. To the best of our knowledge, these are the largest radiation sensitive surfaces covered with microdosimeters so far. Each of these multi‒arrays are integrated in customized electronics readouts by using multichannel ASICs to DAQ. The ASIC enables the beam trigger and an analogue output for 128 microdetectors. Additionally, special pitch‒adapters have been manufactured for each configuration to connect the signal channels with the ASIC readouts properly. In this work we present the first measurements in proton therapy centres under clinical fluence rates (10^8 p/cm2s) across different regions of the beam. Additionally, Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations were performed to crosscheck the experimental results. Representative microdosimetry energy spectra were obtained for some clinical depths as well as the comparison with the patient simulated LET values obtained by a treatment planning software. The results show the feasibility of quantifying distributions of microdosimetry lineal energy values under clinical conditions, which are compared with clinically simulated for the first time.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 350Poster Number:RTSD-04-350] Characterization of Bremsstrahlung Photon Contamination in Clinical Electron Beams via CdZnTe Detectors (#1036)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 C. Park (Autores: C. Park , S. Kim , H. Kim , W.-Y. Jeong , H. Park , J.-Y. Yeom , S. Cho)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea University, Global Health Technology Research Center, Seongbuk-gu, Republic of Korea [2] Chonnam National University Medical School, Department of Radiation Oncology, Gwangju, Republic of Korea [3] Korea University, School of Biomedical Engineering, Seongbuk-gu, Republic of Korea [4] Korea University, Department of Bioengineering, Seongbuk-gu, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Accurate dosimetry of high-energy (≥ 15 MeV) clinical electron beams is challenged by bremsstrahlung-induced photon contamination (X-ray tail), which leads to unintended dose deposition in deep tissues. In this study, high-resistivity CdZnTe (CZT) detectors were investigated for sensitive characterization of this contamination. Two planar CZT detectors (5-mm and 8-mm thick) exhibited high bulk resistivity (~2.0 × 10 10 Ω‧cm) and competitive energy resolution (3.9-4.1% at 662 keV). Measurements were performed using clinical LINAC electron beams (6-18 MeV) at an SSD of 100 cm. To circumvent pulse pile-up under intense photon flux, the detector response was evaluated via time-integrated current in a mixed radiation field. The integrated charge increased markedly at 15 and 18 MeV, indicating enhanced bremsstrahlung production. The 8-mm detector showed higher sensitivity to penetrating photon components than the 5-mm detector, highlighting the importance of detector thickness. These results demonstrate that CZT detectors enable high-sensitivity characterization of photon contamination and are promising for real-time dosimetry and radiotherapy quality assurance.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 351Poster Number:RTSD-04-351] Engineering Low-Reverse-Current CsPbBr 3 Sensor Structures through Surface Passivation and Deposition of Different Contacts (#1094)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 V. Gnatyuk (Autores: V. Gnatyuk , X. Wang , J. Kalliopuska , D. Nalyvaiko , N. Masuda , S. Vähänen , S. Wang , G. Meng)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Advafab Oy, Helsinki, Finland [2] University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China [3] Anhui Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics, Hefei Insititutes of Physical Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Hefei, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract CsPbBr 3 single crystals (CPB SCs) were grown by a modified inverse temperature crystallization method and processed to fabricate metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) sensor structures. A 5 nm Al 2 O 3 layer was deposited by atomic layer deposition to passivate the crystal surface, suppress surface leakage, and provide environmental protection. Pt, Ti, Au, and Al contacts were subsequently deposited to form asymmetric barrier structures with different electrode combinations. X-ray diffraction measurements confirmed high crystalline quality of the as-grown CPB crystals. The rocking curve of the (004) plane exhibited a full width at half maximum of 0.19°. I-V measurements demonstrated pronounced rectification in all investigated MIS structures. The Pt/Al 2 O 3 /CPB/Al 2 O 3 /Al sample exhibited the lowest reverse current (~ 25 nA at 1000 V) and the strongest blocking behavior. These results confirm that Al 2 O 3 passivation combined with optimized asymmetric contacts is an effective approach for engineering low-leakage, polarization-resistant perovskite X/γ-ray sensors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 352Poster Number:RTSD-04-352] Additive Engineering of Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 Double Perovskite Single Crystals: Growth Optimization, Structural Characterization, and Radiation Detector Evaluation (#1418)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 N. S. Sahsuvar (Autores: N. S. Sahsuvar , M. Fiederle , Z. Cihan , M. Daub)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, Freiburg Materials Research Center (FMF), Freiburg im Breisgau, Baden-Württemberg, Germany [2] Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, Institute of Inorganic and Analytical Chemistry, Freiburg im Breisgau, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This study presents a systematic investigation of additive engineering strategies for the solution-based growth of all-inorganic Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 double perovskite single crystals and their evaluation as radiation detectors. Various chemical additives including toluene, ethyl acetate, thiourea, sodium acetate (NaOAc), and potassium acetate (KOAc) were systematically introduced into the precursor solution to influence nucleation dynamics, crystal size, and structural quality. The combination of NaOAc and KOAc was identified as the most effective additive strategy, consistently producing large (up to 2.2 cm), well-faceted, phase-pure single crystals with high reproducibility. The optimized crystals were characterized using X-ray diffraction(XRD), high-resolution XRD(HR-XRD) with rocking curve analysis, scanning electron microscopy(SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy(EDX), laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS), and Raman spectroscopy. HR-XRD rocking curves revealed exceptionally narrow full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) values as low as 0.0144°, confirming outstanding crystalline perfection. Electrical characterization, including current-voltage (I-V) profiling, space-charge-limited current (SCLC) analysis, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) evaluation, was performed to assess the detector potential of the optimized crystals. While the crystals exhibited high bulk resistivity (∼10 9 -10 10 Ω·cm), excellent phase purity, and radiation sensitivity, detector-level investigations revealed trap-limited charge transport and self-trapped exciton formation as intrinsic limitations. This work establishes dual-acetate additive engineering as a robust strategy for growing high-quality Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 single crystals and provides critical insights into the gap between crystal quality and detector-scale performance.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 353Poster Number:RTSD-04-353] Solution Growth and Material Characterization of Cs₂AgBiBr₆ Double Perovskite Crystals for X-Ray Detection: Crystal Quality, Electrical Transport Properties, and Structural Defects (#1556)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Z. Z.-F. Cihan (Autores: Z. Z.-F. Cihan , M. Fiederle)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Albert Ludwigs Üniversity of Freiburg / Freiburger Material Forschungszentrum (FMF), Fakultät für Umwelt und Natürliche Ressourcen Institut für Geo- und Umweltnaturwissenschaften Kristallographie, Freiburg, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This work builds upon our characterization of lead-free double perovskite Cs₂AgBiBr₆ single crystals for radiation detection applications, where high-quality, centimeter-scale crystals (up to ~2.2 cm) were synthesized via a low-cost standard solution-cooling growth method. Structural analysis confirmed a phase-pure cubic Fm3̅m structure with a dominant {111} orientation and narrow FWHM values, indicating high crystalline quality. Morphological and compositional studies revealed smooth surfaces, uniform morphology, and near-stoichiometric composition, while electrical measurements showed low leakage current, ohmic behavior, and high resistivity (10⁹-10¹⁰ Ω·cm)[4]. Despite these favorable properties, device performance remained limited due to defect-related charge transport.To address this, a constant-temperature, feed-controlled growth approach is introduced, where supersaturation is regulated via continuous precursor feeding under stable thermal conditions. This steady-state method suppresses uncontrolled nucleation and promotes the growth of larger, higher-quality crystals. The approach is expected to reduce defect densities and improve material performance, providing a pathway toward high-performance, environmentally friendly radiation detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 354Poster Number:RTSD-04-354] A new approach for studying phase equilibria in the CdTe-MnTe system (#1669)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Bolotnikov (Autores: O. Kopach , V. Kopach , P. Fochuk , M. Solodkyi , M. Kukurudziak , A. Bolotnikov , R. B. James)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Yuriy Fedkovych Chernivtsi National University, Chernivtsi, Ukraine [2] Brookhaven National Laboratory, Upton, New York, United States of America [3] Savannah River National Laboratory, Aiken, South Carolina, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In this work we determined the peculiarities of high-temperature phase equilibria in the CdTe-MnTe system using a differential thermal analysis method in a thermocycling mode. Temperature dependences of the volume fractions of the liquid and solid phases in Cd 1-x Mn x Te (x=0÷0.5) alloys, as well as the minimum and maximum melting temperatures of the solid phase were obtained. These dependences allowed us to establish critical temperatures of equilibria between the solid phase and the melt and to construct the solidus and liquidus lines of the CdTe-MnTe phase diagram. It was shown that with an increase in the molar fraction of MnTe in alloys ranging from 0.1 to 0.5, the decreases in the temperatures for both the solidus and the liquidus did not exceed 20 °C. Plus, the temperature interval between them remains practically constant at 15-18°C. Also, we determined the temperature intervals of the pre-melting region and found that with an increase in the MnTe fraction, the region of pre-melting states of the alloys expands. The results described in this work provide more reliable data on the equilibrium between phases, since the method reduces the influence of kinetic limitations of classical thermography.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 355Poster Number:RTSD-04-355] First Clinical Evaluation of a Gallium Nitride Diode Array for Proton Pencil Beam Scanning (#1828)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Parschat (Autores: L. Parschat , N. F. Brosda , J.-Y. Duboz , E. Frayssinet , S. Higueret , M. Hugues , M. Siviero , C. Bäumer)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] TU Dortmund University, Department of Physics, Dortmund, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [2] West German Proton Therapy Centre Essen, Essen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [3] Ruhr-University Bochum, Department of Physics, Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [4] Université Côte d'Azur, Nice, France [5] CNRS, CRHEA, Valbonne, France [6] Université de Strasbourg, IPHC, CNRS, UMR7178, Strasbourg, France
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract To fully exploit the high-precision of proton therapy, advanced beam monitoring and quality assurance devices capable of reliable real-time dose verification are essential. This study presents the first performance evaluation of a Gallium Nitride (GaN) pin-diode array at a clinical proton therapy facility using Pencil Beam Scanning. The detector array is comprised of 11x11 diodes with a 500 μm pitch coupled to a low-noise multi-channel readout system, and the response of all 121 pixels was evaluated individually. The experimental characterization was carried out at a cyclotron-based proton therapy center using clinical proton energies of 100 MeV and 226.7 MeV. We investigated the detector response for different single proton spots ranging from 0.02 to 100 monitor units (MU), corresponding to 10 6 - 10 10 protons. The results demonstrate excellent linearity between diode response and machine output. Regarding the time response characteristics, a bi-exponential decay model expresses the observed signal fall-off after irradiation. The afterglow contribution was less than 5% of the integrated signal per measured spot. These initial results of a pixelated GaN pin-diode array under clinical pencil beam scanning conditions identify the proposed detector as a promising candidate for both real-time beam monitoring and high-precision quality assurance in clinical proton therapy environments.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 356Poster Number:RTSD-04-356] An Integrated Purification-Growth Strategy for High-Performance Perovskite CsPbBr 3 Crystals (#2068)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Chen (Autores: J. Wang , J. Ma , S. Wang , C. Zhong , Y. Zhu , Y. Lu , R. Xu , J. Chen)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, State Key Laboratory of Functional Crystals and Devices, Shanghai, China [2] Shanghai University, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Shanghai, China [3] University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Center of Materials Science and Optoelectronics Engineering, Beijing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract All-inorganic perovskite CsPbBr 3 single crystals are promising candidates for room-temperature radiation detection; however, the conventional vertical Bridgman (VB) growth rates (<1 mm/h) severely constrain efficient growth and wide applications. In this study, we report a novel strategy for preparing high-performance single crystals via zone refining, which integrates the traditionally separate purification and crystal growth processes into a unified in-situ purification and growth process. This strategy accelerates the growth rate to 25 mm/h - approximately 25-fold faster than conventional vertical Bridgman (VB) growth methods - while preserving an X-ray rocking-curve FWHM of just 0.02°. The resulting crystals exhibit exceptional carrier transport properties, with a hole mobility-lifetime product (μₕτₕ) of 1.2 × 10 -3 cm 2 V -1 and a dark current of only 26 nA at 300 V for a 6-mm-diameter circular device. Asymmetric planar detectors fabricated from these crystals demonstrate outstanding room-temperature energy resolutions (ERs) of 7.3%, 5.8%, 5.0%, and 3.3% for 241 Am (59.5 keV), 57 Co (122 keV), 22 Na (511 keV), and 137 Cs (662 keV) γ-rays, respectively. This work breaks the crystal growth rate bottleneck and provides a practical pathway toward the scalable in-situ growth of high-performance perovskite CsPbBr 3 radiation detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 357Poster Number:RTSD-04-357] Spectral Performance of GaAs:Cr Photon-Counting Detectors with Various Thicknesses (#2228)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Wang (Autores: B. Wang , T. Zhong , H. Li , J. Kalliopuska , D. Nalyvaiko , V. Gnatyuk , X. Lai)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Shanghaitech University, School of Biomedical Engineering, ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, Pudong, China [2] Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare Advanced Technology Research Institute Co., Ltd., Pudong, China [3] Advafab OY, Helsinki, Finland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Photon-counting detectors (PCDs) enable high spatial resolution, zero electronic noise, and multi-material decomposition. Chromium-compensated gallium arsenide (GaAs:Cr) is an outstanding candidate material for these applications. To address single-crystal inhomogeneities and ASIC-induced variations, we implemented a single-pixel energy calibration scheme based on K-edge absorption for high-resistivity GaAs:Cr detectors [1]. S-curve scans were performed for 0.6 mm, 1.0 mm, and 1.4 mm sensor thicknesses using 0.5 mm metallic filters (Ta, W, Pb). Calculating the differential intensity ratio between filtered and air spectra allowed accurate K-edge energy extraction, yielding highly linear fits (R 2 > 0.99) between energy (keV) and Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) thresholds. Crucially, incorporating electron mobility-lifetime ( µτ e ) products elucidates the physical mechanisms driving thickness-dependent gain variations and spectral shifts. Subsequent evaluations confirmed the calibration accuracy. This calibration and physical analysis validate the spectral imaging capabilities of thick GaAs:Cr detectors, advancing their clinical applications.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 358Poster Number:RTSD-04-358] Optical manipulation of space charge in rectifying CdZnTe/CdTe radiation detectors (#2589)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Kačenga (Autores: S. Kačenga , M. Betušiak , E. Belas , R. Grill , P. Praus)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Charles University, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Institute of Physics, Prague, Czech Republic
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This work investigates the polarization and depolarization processes in CdZnTe and CdTe radiation detectors with rectifying contacts. The electrical properties of the contacts were characterized by I-V measurements, while the evolution of space charge was studied using the Laser-induced Transient Current Technique (L-TCT) combined with Monte Carlo simulations of charge transport to determine electric field profiles. In both CdZnTe and CdTe detectors, the gradual formation of negative space charge within the detector volume after applying bias was observed due to the hole blocking anode. Depolarization methods based on optical irradiation were subsequently investigated. In the CdTe detector, continuous above-bandgap irradiation of the anode by a 565 nm diode resulted in a stable, nearly flat electric field profile, demonstrating effective suppression of polarization for at least 1000 s. Similar results were observed for above-bandgap anode irradiation of CdZnTe as well. In both CdZnTe and CdTe detectors, continuous side irradiation by a below-bandgap 904 nm diode decreased the space charge and improved stability as well. However, compared with the above-bandgap anode irradiation, polarization was only partially suppressed for the CdTe detector, and the internal electric field still evolved over time, albeit more slowly than in the dark. For the CdZnTe detector, the side irradiation completely stopped the polarization. The results confirm that controlled optical irradiation can significantly improve the stability of CdTe/CdZnTe detectors operated under bias.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 359Poster Number:RTSD-04-359] High-Voltage Tolerant Ni/YSZ/4H-SiC MOS Detectors for Thick Active Layers (#2697)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Talacko (Autores: M. Talacko , B. Zaťko , Š. Chromik , M. Španková , E. Kováčová , Z. Zápražný , I. Píš , V. Ukrainets , L. Hrubčín , A. Šagátová)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Slovak Academy of Sciences, Institute of Electrical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia [2] Slovak University of Technology, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, Bratislava, Slovakia
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Conventional 4H-SiC Schottky barrier detectors (SBDs) with thick active layers (>50 µm) are often limited by high leakage currents and premature breakdown under high bias voltages. This work introduces an innovative approach using an ultrathin yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) high- κ dielectric interlayer to form a metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) structure. While YSZ is a known ionic conductor at elevated temperatures, its ionic mobility is effectively frozen at room temperature, allowing it to function as a robust electrical insulator that suppresses carrier injection. Ni/YSZ/n-4H-SiC MOS structures, fabricated via pulsed laser deposition demonstrated stable operation up to 1 kV. The high-voltage stability enabled a depletion width of approximately 70 µm at 1000 V, establishing favorable conditions for efficient charge collection in thick epitaxial layers. Spectrometric evaluation with a triple-alpha source (²³⁸Pu-²³⁹Pu-²⁴⁴Cm) confirmed enhanced performance, with stable energy resolution maintained across a broad bias range (100-1000 V) and optimal results observed between 200 V and 600 V. This architecture significantly improves high-voltage resilience while maintaining competitive spectroscopic qualities, paving the way for next-generation deep-depletion radiation detectors in nuclear and space applications.

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract TlBr Polycrystalline Based Semiconductors (PBS) are investigated as promising ceramic materials for low-cost, high-energy x-ray detection. Ceramic samples were prepared through hot pressing followed by the fabrication of planar detectors for characterization and x-ray response measurements. Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics were evaluated for all devices, which exhibited high resistivity (≥10 9 Ω cm) and stable performance under applied bias. The samples demonstrated excellent sensitivity to 70 kVp x-rays, as well as outstanding response to 6 MeV and 9 MeV x-ray pulses from the Linatron M9A linear accelerator (linac) at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK). This work provides a general overview of the ceramic preparation process and detector characterization and summarizes low and high-energy x-ray responses measured at RMD and UTK.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 361Poster Number:RTSD-04-361] Lateral Expansion of the Active Region in Semi-Insulating GaAs Radiation Detectors with Different Schottky Contact Sizes (#3001)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 N. Kurucova (Autores: N. Kurucova , A. Sagatova , B. Zatko , E. Kovacova)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Slovak University of Technology, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, Institute of of Nuclear and Physical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia [2] Slovak Academy of Sciences, Institute of Electrical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This work investigates the influence of Schottky contact size on the charge collection efficiency (CCE) and lateral expansion of the active region in 350 µm thick semi-insulating GaAs detectors using alpha particle spectrometry. Measurements were performed for detectors with Schottky contact diameters ranging from 0.10 mm to 2.00 mm under reverse bias voltages up to 500 V. The results show that detectors with smaller contacts achieve higher CCE values and simultaneously higher counting rates, indicating spreading of the electric collection field beyond the geometrical contact area. The lateral extension of the active region was evaluated from the effective active diameter derived from alpha peak count analysis. The obtained results demonstrate an approximately linear increase of the lateral extension with increasing reverse bias voltage, reaching average values of about 80 µm at 200 V and 120 µm at 300 V. These findings are particularly relevant for pixelated detector systems with small pixel pitch, such as Timepix3-based detectors employing thick GaAs sensors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 362Poster Number:RTSD-04-362] Depth‑Resolved Measurement of Charge‑Cloud Formation and Transport in a 2.0 mm CdTe‑Timepix3 Detector (#3046)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. S. Rodrigues (Autores: D. S. Rodrigues , A. M. Trindade , J. M. Maia , R. M. Curado da Silva , P. G. Carmo , J. F. Sousa , M. Letra)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] LIP-Laboratory of Instrumentation and Experimental Particle Physics, Coimbra, Portugal [2] University of Beira Interior (UBI), Department of Physics, Covilhã, Portugal [3] University of Coimbra, Department of Physics, Coimbra, Portugal
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Understanding charge cloud formation and transport in CdTe detectors is essential for precision spectroscopy, imaging, and Compton polarimetry in the sub-MeV gamma-ray band. We report a detailed experimental study of electron diffusion and electron-dispersion mechanisms in a 2.0 mm-thick CdTe-Timepix3 detector (256×256 pixels, 55 µm pitch), operated at a bias voltage of −300 V and temperature of ≈28 °C. Monochromatic 200 keV and 300 keV gamma-ray beams, collimated to 10 µm×10 µm, were provided by the ESRF ID15A beamline and directed along the detector's Y-axis. A depth-resolved scan was performed in 200 µm steps along the Z-axis, probing the evolution of the transverse charge cloud inside the CdTe volume. For each Z-position, thousands of photoelectric events were selected, and the 1D transverse distribution of the total collected charge was reconstructed along the X-axis. Gaussian fits to these distributions yielded depth-dependent width values. Fitting the squared width values with a function that models all contributions to the transverse charge distribution at the pixelated plane enabled the extraction of key charge-transport parameters: the initial radius of the primary photoelectron cloud and the electron transverse diffusion coefficient. Independent measurements of the electron drift velocity using throughgoing muon tracks were used to constrain this parameter. The measured evolution of sigma values is well described by a model that combines thermal diffusion, the finite initial radius of the primary photoelectron cloud, and Coulomb-driven charge-cloud expansion. This work provides the first depth-resolved experimental quantification of these combined effects in CdTe-Timepix3 detectors, improving charge-transport inputs for simulations of Compton imaging and polarimetry in the 0.1-1 MeV energy band.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 363Poster Number:RTSD-04-363] When 0 V Is Not Really 0 V: Remnant Fields in MAPbBr₃ X-Ray Detectors (#1290)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J.-M. Verilhac (Autores: E. Gros-Daillon , O. Baussens , F. Lédée , J.-M. Verilhac)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CEA, Leti, Grenoble, France [2] CEA, Liten, Grenoble, France
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Methylammonium lead tribromide (MAPbBr 3 ) single crystals are intensively studied emerging materials for use in X-ray radiography and gamma-ray spectrometry [1] and their quality such as shape control, dislocation and point defect densities are improving but some of their properties remain elusive. In particular, transient X-ray-induced photocurrent can be measured in MAPbBr3 single crystals detectors after the bias is switched off. This response then slowly decays over time. In this study, we investigate the internal electrical field that builds up when a bias is applied2 4 by measuring the residual sensitivity of millimeter-thick Cr/MAPbBr 3 /Cr-based detectors after switching off the bias from 10V to 0V. By fitting a numerical model, we compute the value of this internal field and infer the ionic charge density close to the electrodes. This model is also used to approximate the charge carrier mobility lifetime product.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 364Poster Number:RTSD-04-364] Vibration‑suppressed solution growth of perovskite single crystals for high‑resolution gamma‑ray detection (#1577)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 H. Wu (Autores: B. Song , Y. Chen , S. Xiao , Z. Li , Y. Ge , H. Wu)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Chinese Academy of Sciences, Research Center for Advanced Detection Materials and Medical Imaging Devices, Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Shenzhen, China [2] Shenzhen Polytechnic University, School of Electronic and Communication Engineering, Shenzhen, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract High‑performance γ‑ray spectroscopy with solution‑grown metal halide perovskites has been persistently limited by uncontrolled defect formation during crystal growth. Here, we identify ambient mechanical vibration as a critical yet overlooked factor that destabilizes the concentration boundary layer and perturbs lattice ordering in hybrid perovskite single crystals. The resulting crystals exhibit an increased carrier mobility-lifetime product of 8.36×10 -2 cm -2 V -1 , which contributes to a more efficient charge collection process. Detectors achieved an energy resolution of 9.5% at 59.5 keV and 5.2% at 122 keV. These results establish vibration control as a key principle for high‑quality single‑crystal growth and scalable perovskite radiation detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 365Poster Number:RTSD-04-365] Investigation of the anisotropy of the electronic properties of CsPbBr 3 (#1667)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Bolotnikov (Autores: V. Skliarchuk , P. Fochuk , A. Bolotnikov , R. B. James)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Chernivtsi National University, Chernivtsi, Ukraine [2] Brookhaven National Laboratory, Upton, New York, United States of America [3] Savannah River National Laboratory, Aiken, North Carolina, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The study of the electrical properties of perovskite CsPbBr 3 crystals, grown by the Bridgman method in our laboratory, showed that the stability of the dark current of the In/CsPbBr 3 /In structure critically depends on the polarity of the applied voltage. The CsPbBr 3 crystal was cut perpendicular to the growth plane. Indium was deposited on both surfaces after treatment in an argon plasma. The contact area was 4x4 mm 2 , and the thickness of the plates was 1-2 mm. The study was carried out at a temperature of T≈300 K and a voltage of 100 V. The surface of the sample, which was closer to the beginning of the ingot growth and crystallized first, will be designated as "cold". When on the "cold" side was the "minus", the current remained stable over time for 8 hours of continuous operation, while with reverse polarity, a degradation of the blocking properties wais observed with an increase in the dark current by 2-3 orders of magnitude. A similar phenomenon (non-equivalence of opposite crystal surfaces) was observed in CdTe crystals, oriented in the (111) plane. Therefore, it can be assumed that when cutting a plate perpendicular to the growth axis, with there is a very high probability that one side will be enriched with a layer of Cs and Br atoms, and the opposite side, which is more chemically active, will be enriched with Pb and Br atoms. This may be the reason for the non-equivalence of their behavior in the electrical measurements.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 367Poster Number:RTSD-04-367] Improved Stability of Perovskite Single Crystal Semiconductor X-ray Detector via 2D Layer Formation (#2555)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. Lee (Autores: D. Lee , B. Park , S. Song , J. Seo , C. Park , J.-Y. Yeom)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea University, Department of Bioengineering, Seoul, Republic of Korea [2] Korea University, Interdisciplinary Program in Precision Public Health, Seoul, Republic of Korea [3] Seoul National University, Nuclear Research Institute for Future Technology and Policy (NIFTEP), Seoul, Republic of Korea [4] Korea University, Global Health Technology Research Center, Seoul, Republic of Korea [5] Korea Institute of Fusion Energy (KFE), Daejeon, Republic of Korea [6] Korea University, School of Bioengineering, Seoul, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Methylammonium lead tribromide (MAPbBr 3 , MPB) single crystals are promising candidates for direct-conversion X-ray detection, but their practical use is hindered by ion migration that causes photocurrent drift and baseline instability under continuous X-ray exposure. In this work, a two-dimensional (2D) organic-inorganic hybrid layer is formed on MPB single crystals through a simple solution-dipping process using 4-fluorophenethylammonium iodide (4F-PEAI), and the impact on detector stability is systematically investigated. The 2D-layer formation, controlled through precursor concentration and dipping time, is confirmed by the emergence of a new low-angle XRD peak assigned to a (4F-PEA) 2 PbX 4 2D layered phase, and by a blue shift of the band-edge photoluminescence consistent with surface modification. Surface 2D-layer passivation reduces the dark-current hysteresis, suppresses the photocurrent drift under continuous X-ray exposure, and lowers the in-pulse relative standard deviation, while maintaining linear dose response across the measured dose-rate range. These results demonstrate that surface 2D-layer formation is a practical strategy for suppressing ion migration and improving the operational stability of perovskite single-crystal X-ray detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 368Poster Number:RTSD-04-368] Highly Radiation-Hard Flexible Perovskite Imaging Arrays for Real-Time Proton Beam Monitoring (#2700)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Zhang (Autores: Y. Zhang , G. Niu)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan National Laboratory for Optoelectronics and School of Optical and Electronic Information, WuHan, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Real-time proton beam monitoring is crucial for pencil beam scanning in proton therapy, but conventional solid-state detectors suffer from radiation-induced damage and structural rigidity, limiting their in-vivo applications. Building upon the lattice-anchoring dynamic repair mechanism in hybrid perovskites, we developed a highly stable, flexible perovskite thin-film transistor array for real-time proton beam profiling. The detector adopts a p-i-n architecture on a flexible substrate, protected by robust Parylene encapsulation to ensure long-term operational stability. Under 160 megaelectron-volt high-energy proton irradiation, the arrays demonstrated exceptional radiation hardness, maintaining robust operational stability even after accumulating a high fluence of 1.23*10 10 p cm -2 . Spatial resolution remained uncompromised post-irradiation, with the spatial frequency at a modulation transfer function of 0.2 showing negligible degradation from about 3.03 line pairs per millimeter.. When deployed in a clinical setup, the TFT array achieved real-time proton beam imaging at a frame rate of 15 frames per second. At a 16-centimeter solid water depth, the measured beam full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) was 8.47 millimeters, perfectly matching the 8.27 millimeters theoretical value predicted by Monte Carlo simulations using FLUKA and Allpix, and it has achieved real-time tracking and prediction of the center of the proton beam. These results validate the immense potential of flexible perovskite TFT arrays for the real-time tracking of the Bragg peak and conformal dose monitoring, offering a transformative dosimetric tool for advanced precision radiotherapy and expanding the practical applications of room-temperature semiconductor detectors.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Cardiff (Autores: S. Cardiff , G. Tumen-Ulzii , S. D. Stranks)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Formamidinium lead bromide (FAPbBr3) single crystal perovskites have recently emerged as a key candidate for commercially viable radiation detectors for their high per formance and solution processability at low temperatures. An under-explored consequence of crystal growth from solution is the ability to crystallise around pre-placed structures, enabling detectors with an embedded electrode architecture. This work presents the growth of FAPbBr3 single crystals around a 2×2 array of gold wire electrodes, showing the first demonstration of this device architecture in a FAPbBr3 single crystal radiation detector as a proof of concept. By collecting charge carriers laterally, the charge carrier transit time and trap probability is reduced compared to the planar configuration. Initial charac terisation demonstrated a linear I-V response and sensitivity to X-rays. Future work will scale to a larger array with an increased area targeting γ-ray spectroscopic performance with fast signal pulse rise times.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 371Poster Number:RTSD-04-371] Evaluation of carrier transport properties of TlBr semiconductor detectors (#1686)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Watanabe (Autores: K. Watanabe , Y. Sugai , S. Tanaka , Y. Kawai , M. Nogami , K. Hitomi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Kyushu University, Department of Applied Quantum Physics and Nuclear Engineering, Fukuoka, Japan [2] Tohoku University, Department of Quantum Science and Energy Engineering, Sendai, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Thallium bromide (TlBr) is a highly promising material for next-generation gamma-ray detectors due to its wide band gap and high stopping power. To realize large-volume and high-performance detectors, it is essential to establish an efficient evaluation method for detector performance. This study aims to investigate the correlation between crystalline structural quality and carrier dynamics in TlBr single crystals. We developed a scanning time-of-flight (TOF) measurement system to evaluate the two-dimensional distribution of electron mobility and trapping characteristics. A 3-mm-thick TlBr wafer was characterized using both EBSD mapping and laser-induced TOF measurements. The results revealed a clear correlation between structural grain boundaries and localized degradations in electron mobility. Furthermore, spatial mapping of the residual charge ratio identified specific regions characterized by high trap densities. Subsequent evaluations of detectors fabricated from these regions showed significantly poor long-term stability. This study provides essential feedback for improving crystal growth processes and establishes a methodology for the quality assurance of compound semiconductor radiation detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 372Poster Number:RTSD-04-372] Fabrication of Flexible Nanostructured Polymer for Nanomaterial-based Detectors (#1099)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 I.-H. Han (Autores: I.-H. Han , J. Boo , G. Kim)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Seoul National University, Department of Energy System Engineering, Gwanak-gu, Republic of Korea [2] Seoul National University, Department of Nuclear Engineering, Gwanak-gu, Republic of Korea [3] Seoul National University, Institute of Engineering Research, Gwanak-gu, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This study describes the fabrication of the aramid nanofiber (ANF) to produce flexible detectors based on nanomaterials, with short preparation and low surface leakage current. Flexible detectors offer the advantage of achieving improved detection efficiency and efficient use of space with curved surfaces. In previous studies, ANF was used as a porous nanostructured polymer for the fabrication of nanomaterial-based semiconductor detectors. However, it had the issues of a long preparation time and brittleness after drying. To address these issues, we used DMSO containing an aqueous KOH solution in the preparation of the ANF solution. with This reduced the preparation time from one week to two days. Furthermore, we compared the results of ANF coagulation in different soloutions-ethanol (EtOH), acetic acid (AcOH), and a mixed AcOH-EtOH (volume ratio was 7:3) solution-to alleviating the pore collapse of the nanostructure, with the conventional H 2 O-based method. The synthesis solution containing PbS quantum dots (about dia. 5 nm) and Te nanorods (130 nm in length), as confirmed by TEM and XRD, was loaded into ANF samples using various coagulation solutions. We confirmed that uniform loading in dpeth occurred in the order of H 2 O, EtOH, AcOH, and the AcOH-EtOH mixture. Furthermore, according to the I-V curves, the surface leakage current also tended to decrease in the same order of uniform loading, with a maximum 10,000-fold difference observed between the ANF samples prepared with H 2 O (about 100 μA at 10 V) and the AcOH-EtOH mixed solution (about 2 nA at 10 V). Therefore, it was shown that ANF coagulated with the AcOH-EtOH mixed solution remained flexible even after drying, and the uniform embedding of nanomaterials according to depth reduced the surface leakage current.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 X. Pang (Autores: X. Pang , Z. Li , M. Sui , Y. Lu , Y. Ge , H. Wu)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Perovskite materials are promising for low-cost direct X-ray detection, but their integration with thin‑film transistor backplanes is limited by porosity, cracking, and poor imaging uniformity. Here, we report a combined strategy of uniform particle dispersion and solution-assisted hot pressing for fabricating uniform MAPbI 3 thick films on TFT substrates, where uniform particle dispersion stabilizes slurry dispersion and solution-assisted hot pressing promotes film densification, grain growth, and pore filling. The average particle size of the fabricated devices decreased from 32.07 μm to 15.14 μm, and the standard deviation reduced from 7.3 μm to 4.9 μm. At an electric field strength of 100 V·mm -1 , the sensitivity reached 3514 μC·Gy air -1 cm -2 . A prototype MAPbI 3 -based X-ray flat-panel detector further achieves a spatial resolution of 3.75 lp mm -1 at an modulation transfer function of 0.2, together with significantly improved imaging uniformity. This work provides a practical route toward scalable, thin‑film transistor compatible perovskite X-ray flat‑panel detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 374Poster Number:RTSD-04-374] Investigation of Metal Oxides as Contact Materials for CdTe X-Ray, Gamma-Ray Detectors (#1816)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Niraula (Autores: M. Niraula , M. Tanimoto , Y. Ohi , R. Fukuda)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Nagoya Institute of Technology, Graduate School of Engineering, Nagoya, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract CdTe is a well-established semiconductor for high-resolution X-ray, gamma-ray detector. However, its widespread application is limited by high dark current and long-term performance instability. The metal-semiconductor interface plays a critical role in governing these issues, as it strongly influenced by contact metal indiffusion and interfacial reactions. In this work, indium tin oxide (ITO) is investigated as a potential contact material for CdTe detectors to mitigate these limitations. ITO electrodes were deposited on one face of a high-resistivity p-like CdTe crystal by RF sputtering, while a gold electrode was formed on the opposite face by thermal evaporation. The fabricated device showed clear rectifying behavior, with reverse dark currents below 1 nA at 100 V bias for a 3 x 3 x 0.5 mm 3 device, representing a significant reduction compared to similar devices with Au contacts on both sides. Improved gamma-ray detection performance was also observed. Furthermore, the effects of CdTe substrate temperature during ITO deposition and post-deposition annealing on junction formation and detector performance, including dark current, energy resolution, and long-term stability, were systematically investigated.

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the characterization of conductive layers on CdTe semiconductor crystals fabricated via laser ablation. The layers were prepared at both ambient and elevated temperatures, with various ablation parameters evaluated to optimize their quality. Our analysis revealed the formation of conductive layers on the semiconductor surface, exhibiting high hole mobility. These layers were systematically characterized using a suite of electrical and optical techniques, including Hall effect measurements, photocurrent mapping, the Laser-induced Transient Current Technique (L-TCT), and stability tests focusing on time-dependent behavior.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 376Poster Number:RTSD-04-376] Contact Characterization of High-Flux Stable GaAs:Cr Detector (#3233)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Wang (Autores: K. Shi , B. Wang , H. Li , T. Zhong , Z. Shen , J. Kalliopuska , D. Nalyvaiko , V. Gnatyuk , X. Lai)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] ShanghaiTech University, School of Biomedical Engineering, pudong, China [2] Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare Advanced Tech-nology Research Institute Co., Ltd, pudong, China [3] Advafab OY, Espoo, Finland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Chromium-compensated gallium arsenide (GaAs:Cr) is a highly promising material for spectral X-ray photon counting detectors (PCDs), offering high electron mobility (∼4000 cm2/V · s), low K-shell fluorescence (9.2 keV and 10.5 keV), and ultra-high bulk resistivity (∼109 Ω · cm). A critical factor governing the high-flux stability of such PCDs is the metal-semiconductor contact. While conventional detectors often rely on Schottky contacts-which trap space charge and cause polarization under sustained irradiation-the ultra-high resistivity of GaAs:Cr enables barrier-free Ohmic contacts. This approach relies entirely on bulk resistance to limit dark current, eliminating interface charge accumulation and preserving a uniform electric field. In this work, we characterize the wide-bias (−1000 V to 1000 V) dark current-voltage (I-V ) behavior of pixelated GaAs:Cr detectors. The devices exhibit highly linear, symmetric responses with distinct Ohmic and space-charge-limited current (SCLC) regimes, confirming high-quality Ohmic contact formation. Furthermore, the extracted bulk resistivity and demonstrated pixel-level uniformity validate the contact integrity required for stable high-flux photon counting applications.
