sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 377Poster Number:RTSD-04-377] Validation of FAPbBr3 Perovskite Radiation Stability: Monte Carlo Simulation and Proton-Irradiation Experiment (#1624)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Z. Huang (Autores: Z. Huang , B. Song , Y. Chen , X. Pang , Y. Sang , J. Wu , H. Wu , Y. Ge)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen, China [2] Cancer Hospital Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, Shenzhen, Shenzhen, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract A Geant4-based Monte Carlo framework was developed to predict the proton-irradiation stability of FAPbBr3 perovskite. Beyond calculating non-ionizing energy loss (NIEL), the framework records layer-resolved energy deposition across a 2 mm crystal divided into 50 slices. For 70, 100, 150, and 200 MeV protons, the NIEL values are 2.04, 2.01, 1.38, and 1.55*10^-3 MeV cm^2 g^-1, confirming non-ionizing displacement-damage channels. The deposited-energy fractions in the incident-side 0.20 mm are 11.83%, 10.69%, 19.57%, and 14.90%, respectively, following the same order as the measured electrical response: 150 MeV > 200 MeV > 70 MeV > 100 MeV. This agreement indicates that near-surface energy deposition can effectively predict mobility-lifetime product variation and supports the framework as a screening tool for perovskite radiation stability.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 378Poster Number:RTSD-04-378] CZT Strip Detectors Characteristics After the Euro Material Ageing Mission (#2468)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Zappettini (Autores: M. Bettelli , N. Auricchio , E. Caroli , R. C. Silva , C. Ferrari , E. Ferrari , J. Maia , M. Vadrucci , E. Virgilli , A. Zappettini)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CNR, IMEM, Parma, Italy [2] INAF, OAS, Bologna, Italy [3] University of Coimbra, Department of Physics, Coimbra, Portugal [4] LIP, Coimbra, Portugal [5] ASI, Rome, Italy [6] University of Beira Interior, Physics Department, Covilha, Portugal
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The effect of the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) environment on future high energy instrument sensors is essential to optimize their performance, by minimizing orbital background noise. In the framework of the CNES-ESA European Material Ageing program (EMA), the ageing effects on critical components of a Laue lens telescope in the LEO space environment is investigated. Since more than a decade, the group has been developing CZT drift strip sensors to meet the stringent requirements of a Laue lens focal plane detector for high-energy photons. As part of the EMA proposal, two simplified samples of drift strip CZT detectors were exposed to outer space on the CNES Bartolomeo external platform of ISS for more than 12 months. The objective was to test the robustness and reliability of the surface passivation and metallization processes in the LEO space environment. The samples were taken down to earth on February 27. In this work, we report on the results of the simulations we carried out accounting for possible damages to the detector properties due to agents as oxygen and high energy ions. Also, preliminary measurements on the detectors come back from space will be shown.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 379Poster Number:RTSD-04-379] Development of a Compact CdTe-Based Gamma Spectroscopy System with Dual-Side Readout for High-Resolution Gamma Imaging (#1117)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Chang (Autores: S. Chang , S. Sato , Y. Mitsuya , H. Takahashi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] The University of Tokyo, School of Engineering, Tokyo, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We developed a compact CdTe-based gamma-ray spectroscopy system with a dual-side readout architecture for high-resolution gamma imaging. The system is designed for pixelated Schottky CdTe detector arrays. Cathode pixels at the same relative position across multiple detector chips are multiplexed, while the anode of each chip is read out independently. This configuration reduces the number of readout channels and system complexity while preserving energy information from the anode side and position information from the cathode side. The system integrates custom JFET-input charge-sensitive preamplifiers and a waveform-sampling data acquisition system based on AFE5801 chips, enabling measurement of pulse height, risetime, and waveform information. To evaluate the feasibility of the proposed method, spectral measurements were performed using a 2 × 1 CdTe detector array operated at +650 V with sealed ²²Na and ¹³⁷Cs sources. A 1 μs coincidence time window was applied to match the anode and cathode signals. Calibrated energy spectra were obtained from both sides. The anode signal showed slightly better energy resolution and was used as the primary signal for energy measurement, while the cathode signal can provide position information. After applying risetime selection, energy resolutions of 3.61% at 511 keV and 3.20% at 662 keV were achieved. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed dual-side merged readout architecture. A 5 × 5 CdTe detector array has also been assembled, and further verification experiments are in progress.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 380Poster Number:RTSD-04-380] An Event Reconstruction ASIC for 3D CdZnTe Gamma-Ray Detectors (#1375)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 F. Mohammed Rafee (Autores: F. Mohammed Rafee , D. Anderson , Y. Zhu , Z. He)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Michigan, Nuclear Engineering & Radiological Sciences, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States of America [2] H3D, Inc., Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional position-sensitive CdZnTe (3D-CZT) gamma-ray detector systems provide compact gamma-ray spectroscopy with 3D position sensing. Achieving high performance requires event-by-event energy and position reconstruction to compensate for charge loss, gain variation, and response nonlinearity. Such reconstruction calculations are typically performed on a powerful CPU. To reduce power consumption and minimize system footprint, we propose implementing the reconstruction in an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC). In this work, we focus on single-pixel event reconstruction, integrating depth and nonlinearity corrections along with a sub-pixel position calculation. This ASIC is implemented in TSMC 65 nm CMOS technology and is designed to interface with a DAQ-DSP back-end ASIC and four H3DD-UM front-end ASICs. Preliminary results demonstrate the feasibility of an event reconstruction ASIC with an area of 2.43 mm^2. This development represents a key step towards the development of more compact 3D-CZT systems.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 381Poster Number:RTSD-04-381] Spectroscopic Performance of SOI-CMOS Pixel Detector at Elevated Temperatures (#1803)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 H. Takamoto (Autores: H. Takamoto , A. Takeda , K. Mori , H. Suzuki , T. G. Tsuru)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Miyazaki, Engineering, Miyazaki, Japan [2] Kyoto University, Physics, Kyoto, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract XRPIX is a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) CMOS pixel detector developed for next-generation X-ray astronomical observations. An X-ray camera, SUIM (Soipix for observing Upper atmosphere as Iss experiment Mission), is our first space mission employing XRPIX and is planned for launch to the International Space Station (ISS) in 2026. Thermal analysis of the SUIM instrument indicates that the camera housing may reach temperatures as high as +60°C in orbit, making it essential to verify XRPIX performance under elevated temperature conditions. The primary concern under such conditions is the degradation of spectroscopic performance due to increased dark current. Spectroscopic measurements using 241 Am were conducted over a temperature range from −30°C to +70°C, with a periodic reset of 100 μs applied to suppress dark current accumulation during integration. Only minimal degradation was observed, confirming that the periodic reset scheme effectively maintains good spectroscopic performance even at +70°C. The gain decreases at a rate of −0.132 μV e −1 °C −1 , which can be corrected through gain calibration. These results demonstrate that XRPIX maintains sufficient spectroscopic performance at least up to +70°C, indicating that its performance is also adequate for use in the SUIM instrument.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 382Poster Number:RTSD-04-382] Development of Zero-Grid-Bias Operation in Coplanar Grid Type TlBr Detectors (#1807)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Tanaka (Autores: S. Tanaka , Y. Kawai , T. Teshima , K. Watanabe , M. Nogami , K. Hitomi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Kyushu University, Department of Applied Quantum Physic and Nuclear Engineering, Fukuoka, Japan [2] Tohoku University, Department of Quantum Science and Energy Engineering, Sendai, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract TlBr is a promising compound semiconductor material for gamma-ray detectors[1] because of its wide bandgap, high-Z constituents, and high density, which enable room-temperature operation and high detection efficiency. However, because the hole mobility in TlBr is significantly lower than the electron mobility, single-polarity charge sensing techniques are required to achieve high energy resolution. In this study, a zero-grid-bias operation in a coplanar-grid electrode structure for TlBr gamma-ray detectors was investigated. Unlike conventional coplanar-grid detectors, the proposed structure operates without a bias voltage between adjacent grid electrodes, which may reduce leakage current. A conventional comb-shaped electrode structure was evaluated experimentally and through simulations using a Cs-137 source. The simulation results reproduced the experimental pulse-height spectra well. In addition, pulse-height correction using the cathode-to-anode pulse-height ratio improved the energy resolution To further improve detector performance, the weighting-potential distribution inside the detector was analyzed, and a spiral-shaped electrode structure was proposed to suppress spatial nonuniformities in the weighting potential. Simulations indicated that the proposed spiral-shaped electrode structure suppressed spatial variations in the weighting potential between adjacent anodes, leading to improved energy resolution after correction. These results suggest that the proposed spiral-shaped zero-grid-bias coplanar-grid electrode structure is a promising approach for large active volume and high-resolution TlBr gamma-ray detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 383Poster Number:RTSD-04-383] A Monte-Carlo Simulation of Unipolar Charge-Sensing Amorphous Selenium X-ray Detector for Photon Counting Imaging (#2479)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Koc (Autores: Y. Mart , A. Koc , A. Camlica)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Middle East Technical University, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Ankara, Turkey [2] Xera Medical Systems and Technology, R&D, Ankara, Turkey [3] Chalmers University of Technology, Electrical Engineering, Goteborg, Sweden [4] Hacettepe University, Institute of Informatics, Ankara, Turkey [5] University of Waterloo, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Waterloo, Ontario, Canada
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the spectral performance of a unipolar charge-sensing amorphous selenium detector using Monte Carlo simulation and compares its response with that of a conventional amorphous selenium detector. The unipolar charge-sensing architecture mitigates the limitations associated with poor electron mobility and deep electron trapping in amorphous selenium by promoting hole-dominated signal formation. Both unipolar charge-sensing and conventional detector structures were simulated for a 20 μm pixel pitch under an average electric field of 8 V/μm. The simulated full-width at half maximum energy resolution was 8.02 keV for the unipolar charge-sensing detector, compared with 21.32 keV for the conventional detector. These results demonstrate that the unipolar charge-sensing architecture substantially improves the spectral performance of amorphous selenium detectors by suppressing depth-dependent signal variations and reducing sensitivity to electron trapping.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 384Poster Number:RTSD-04-384] Study of the spectroscopic performance of Timepix4 with highly ionizing particles (#2480)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 P. Smolyanskiy (Autores: P. Smolyanskiy , B. Bergmann , P. Burian , P. Broulim , R. E. Mihai)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Czech Technical University in Prague, Institute of Experimental and Applied Physics, Prague, Czech Republic [2] University of West Bohemia, Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Pilsen, Czech Republic [3] Horia Hulubei National Institute for Physics and Nuclear Engineering, Department for Nuclear Physics, Magurele, Romania
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We report on the characterization of the Timepix4 hybrid pixel detector with a Si sensor under exposure to heavily ionizing particles. The device was configured sequentially in three gain modes: logarithmic (log), high, and low. Previously developed methodology of pixel's energy calibration beyond calibration with X- and $\gamma$-rays was adopted and applied to Timepix4 data. It uses the protons with energies in the range from 500 -- 2000 keV. Saturation of the pixel's energy response was observed at 1057, 1244, and 2030~keV in the low, high, and log gain modes, respectively. In a laboratory experiment, the detector was irradiated with $\alpha$-particles from a $^{239}$Pu$^{241}$Am$^{244}$Cm source, even higher energy $\alpha$-particles were obtained from naturally occurring radon progeny decays recorded over several weeks of continuous operation. Both measurements yielded an energy resolution of about 2.5\%. The capability of Timepix4 for relativistic ion beam decomposition was investigated within fragment beams at the Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) at CERN. A spectrum stripping technique based on iterative Landau curve fitting was applied to the measured energy-loss spectra, enabling ion charge identification up to $Z$ = 10 at a track inclination of $\theta$ = 60 deg. with respect to the sensor normal.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 385Poster Number:RTSD-04-385] Investigation of Gain Instability of a 3-D CdZnTe Detector (#2768)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Granados (Autores: M. Granados , Y. Zhu , Z. He)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract CdZnTe (CZT) detectors require stable calibration parameters for optimal spectroscopic performance. However, certain pixels exhibit random gain variation during or between measurements, complicating calibration and degrading detector performance. Digital ASICs allow for readout of event waveforms in a CZT detector exhibiting gain instability. Th-228 and Cs-137 measurements were utilized to characterize the gain instabilities, revealing a decrease in the anode amplitudes proportional to the incident energy. Analysis of the neighbor pixel-anode waveforms reveal abnormally high tail amplitudes in the four side neighbors which exceed expectations based on the Shockley-Ramo theorem. The corner neighbors experience noticeable smaller increases in tail amplitudes. Sub-pixel position analysis demonstrates that the tail amplitude increase is not proportional to the neighbor signal amplitude. These findings suggest that the observed gain instability could be caused by issues with capacitance in the system rather than anomalous charge movement. Ongoing work aims to verify the cause of the shift and if the anode deficit can be entirely explained by the differences in the neighbor waveform signals.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 386Poster Number:RTSD-04-386] Bias Scan Analysis of Si-Timepix Detector with Various Sensor Thickness (#2847)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Sagatova (Autores: A. Sagatova , M. Balusik , K. Foss , B. Zatko , C. Granja , T. Slavicek , Z. Kohout)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Slovak University of Technology, Institute of Nuclear and Physical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia [2] Slovak Academy of Sciences, Institute of Electrical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia [3] Czech Technical University, Institute of Experimental and Applied Physics, Prague, Czech Republic
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In the present work, we study the MiniPIX Timepix hybrid pixel detectors with silicon sensors of two different thicknesses and their response to high energy protons. Thermally stabilized detectors measured protons of five energies, 400, 700, 1000, 1400 and 1800 keV in vacuum. During the measurements, a bias scan was performed to investigate the efficiency of collection of charge carriers generated by the protons. With increasing reverse bias, the signal from the detector grew until it saturated. The 300 um thick detector required an electric field generated by a reverse bias of 30 to 40 volts for effective charge collection. A detector with a thicker 500 um sensor required approximately 70 V bias for complete charge collection when registering 400 keV protons and a gradually higher bias of up to 100 V in the case of 1800 keV protons. The much larger bias for a complete collection of the charge generated by protons in a thick detector is in correlation with the theory, where the semiconductor depleted region thickness increases proportionally to the square root of applied reverse bias.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 387Poster Number:RTSD-04-387] Multidimensional Parameter-Space Analysis of Fast Neutron-Induced Tracks in Timepix Detectors (#2992)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Balusik (Autores: M. Balusik , C. Granja , A. Sagatova , K. Foss , T. Slavicek , B. Zatko)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, Slovak University of Technology, Institute of Nuclear and Physical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia [2] Czech Technical University, Institute of Experimental and Applied Physics, Prague, Czech Republic [3] Slovak Academy of Sciences, Institute of Electrical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The Timepix family of pixel detectors provides high spatial resolution together with per-pixel spectroscopic response, allowing event-by-event analysis of radiation interactions through deposited energy and cluster morphology. In fast neutron fields, the detector response is indirect and is produced mainly by secondary particles generated in the sensor and surrounding materials. This work focuses on fast-neutron-induced tracks measured with a Timepix3 detector equipped with a 300 µm silicon sensor at the Van de Graaff laboratory of IEAP CTU in Prague, using neutrons produced trough D-T reaction, in the range of approximately 15-17.5 MeV. The data were processed using TraXEngine [1] and further evaluated through selected spectral and morphological cluster parameters. The selected parameters were analyzed in two- and three-dimensional parameter spaces, where high-density regions corresponding to characteristic event groups were identified. Based on these regions, five parameter-based classes were defined: high-energy ion-like events, low-energy ion-like events, a transition region toward electron-like events, photon-like events, and electron-like events. The developed parameter-space analysis shows that combinations of spectral and morphological parameters can be used to separate components of a fast-neutron-induced mixed radiation field and can support future automated particle-recognition methods.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 388Poster Number:RTSD-04-388] A 512 × 256 a-IGZO Dual-Gate TFT 2T-APS Array for Low-Dose Direct-Conversion X-Ray Flat-Panel Detector (#2297)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Qi (Autores: Y. Qi , H. Xie , X. Pang , H. Wu , X. Liu , Y. Ge , K. Wang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Research Center for Advanced Detection Materials and Medical Imaging Devices, Shenzhen, China [2] Sun Yat-sen University, School of Electronics and Information Technology, Guangzhou, China [3] Shenzhen Chipwey Innovation Technologies Co., Ltd, Shenzhen, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Direct-conversion X-ray flat-panel detectors are attractive for high-resolution and low-dose imaging compared to indirect conversion. However, conventional passive pixel sensors (PPS) without in-pixel gain are commonly used in direct-conversion detectors, causing low signal-to-noise ratio under low-dose exposure. In this work, a compact two-transistor active pixel sensor (2T-APS) with in-pixel current amplification based on amorphous indium-gallium-zinc-oxide (a-IGZO) dual-gate TFTs is proposed for low-dose direct-conversion X-ray imaging. The proposed pixel employs two subthreshold-biased dual-gate TFTs to realize logarithmic-exponential signal processing, enabling electrical tuning of the operating point and sensitivity. A 512×256 2T-APS array was fabricated using an a-IGZO dual-gate TFT process with a pixel pitch of 75 μm×75 μm. Pixel-level characterization further demonstrated amplification of pA-level input currents, achieving a representative current gain over 10^3. The fabricated array was integrated with a perovskite layer to realize X-ray imaging. At the tube voltage of 50 kV, images acquired with tube currents from 0.5 mA to 2.0 mA clearly visualized the object outline. These results validate the feasibility of the proposed a-IGZO dual-gate 2T-APS pixel for low-dose, high-sensitivity direct-conversion X-ray flat-panel detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 389Poster Number:RTSD-04-389] Development of a Self-Triggering Pixelated TlBr Detector with Cherenkov Light Detection (#2504)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 T. Komaki (Autores: T. Komaki , H. Sekiguchi , M. Uenomachi , K. Hitomi , M. Nogami , A. Takeda , H. Toyokawa , K. Shimazoe)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] The University of Tokyo, Bioengineering/Graduate School of Engineering, Tokyo, Japan [2] Institute of Science Tokyo, Institute of Integrated Research, Tokyo, Japan [3] Tohoku University, Department of Quantum Science and Energy Engineering/Graduate School of Engineering, Sendai, Japan [4] University of Miyazaki, Faculty of Engineering, Miyazaki, Japan [5] Konan University, Faculty of Science and Engineering, Kobe, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Simultaneous multi-nuclide imaging is a key challenge in nuclear medicine, promising benefits such as improved diagnostic accuracy, reduced examination frequency, and elimination of physiological variations between scans. However, conventional imaging systems such as positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) are based on fundamentally different principles, making their integration into a single system technically difficult. To address this, we have proposed and developed a Compton-PET camera that enables simultaneous visualization of PET and SPECT nuclides using PET and Compton imaging, respectively. In our previous implementation, the system employed GAGG scintillators as absorbers, but their limited energy resolution (11-15% FWHM above 100 keV) degraded the Compton imaging performance. Thallium bromide (TlBr) semiconductor detectors have been shown to offer both high energy resolution, such as 2% FWHM at 662 keV, and high time resolution, including 511 ps via Cherenkov photon detection, making TlBr a promising sensor material for improving Compton-PET performance. Based on these advantages, we developed a new multi-pixel TlBr semiconductor detector by bonding a TlBr crystal to a self-triggering, energy-resolving pixel application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC). We plan to present the results of I-V characteristic measurements and evaluate detector performance through energy spectrum measurements and time resolution analysis using radionuclide sources.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 390Poster Number:RTSD-04-390] Readout Electronics of SPECTRE CZT detector (#2525)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. Cabiati (Autores: M. Greco , V. Monaco , F. M. Melendi , D. Cabiati)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] INFN, -Torino, Torino, Italy [2] University of Turin, Physics Dept., Torino, Italy [3] University of Ferrara, Physics Dept., Ferrara, Italy [4] INFN, -Ferrara, Ferrara, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The INFN SPECTRE (Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography Readout Electronics) project aims to design, assemble, and characterize a complete detection module based on CZT sensors for medical applications. As the demand for SPECT systems with higher spatial resolution, energy resolution, and sensitivity continues to grow, there is an increasing need to develop high-performance CZT detectors with small pixels and corresponding high-speed readout electronics [1,2]. For readout, SPECTRE uses electronics developed for a high-capacitance gas detector (CGEM@BESIII, IHEP, Beijing [3]): the TIGER (Torino Integrated GEM Electronics for Readout) ASIC for on-detector electronics and the off-detector FPGA-based GEMROC module for power and data processing [4]. TIGER is a mixed-signal chip with 64 channels on an area of 5 × 5 mm². Each channel has a complete readout chain with amplification, signal conditioning, and discrimination, as well as a data payload containing the time and charge information for each event. TIGER is versatile for the readout of radiation sensors up to 50 fC and for high rates up to 70 kHz. The TIGER/GEMROC readout circuit is compact, modular, scalable, and highly customizable. In typical CZT applications today, spectroscopic systems operate at rates of about 1 kcps/mm² because extracting energy information requires more processing time [5]. However, our system can acquire each sensor pixel at a rate of up to 70 kHz, or approximately 16 kcps/mm². In this presentation, we will cover all phases of the project to date, including CZT sensor and electronics simulation with the Allpix Squared package [6], based on Geant4, current-voltage characterization of the CZT sensors, system design and construction, assembly of four modules onto an adapter board, and initial system characterization using X-rays.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 391Poster Number:RTSD-04-391] Spectral Response and Counting Characteristics of a Peak-finding ASIC for GaAs:Cr Detectors (#2540)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 X. Lai (Autores: J. Bai , G. Yu , Y. Zhao , Y. Tong , H. Li , H. Ren , X. Lai)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] ShanghaiTech University, School of Biomedical Engineering, Shanghai, China [2] Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare Advanced Technology Research Institute Co., Ltd., Shanghai, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Photon-counting computed tomography requires readout ASICs with high count-rate capability and reliable spectral performance under clinical X-ray flux. In this work, a peak-finding ASIC for GaAs:Cr photon-counting detectors is presented. The prototype ASIC contains a 9 × 12 pixel array with a pixel pitch of 341 μm × 368 μm. Each pixel integrates a charge-sensitive preamplifier, shaper, peak-finding circuit, five energy bins, threshold DACs, and counters. The peak-finding circuit captures the amplitude of signal peaks, improving counting capability under high-flux conditions. Electrical measurements demonstrate reliable counting performance beyond 30 Mcps/pixel. After coupling with a GaAs:Cr sensor, X-ray measurements showed clear tungsten characteristic peaks, confirming the energy-discrimination capability of the detector module. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed ASIC for high-flux GaAs:Cr-based PCCT detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 392Poster Number:RTSD-04-392] Thickness-dependent front-end noise in CdTe Timepix3 detectors (#2649)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. S. Useche Parra (Autores: J. S. Useche Parra , G. Roque , M. Schütz , R. Ballabriga Sune , S. Procz , M. Fiederle)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Freiburg, Freiburg Material Research Center, Freiburg, Baden-Württemberg, Germany [2] CERN, EP, Geneva, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Photon-counting detectors (PCDs) with high-Z sensors are widely used for spectroscopic X-ray imaging in medical, security, and industrial applications. Hybrid PCDs can be coupled to different semiconductor sensors (Si, CdTe, GaAs), tailoring the assembly to the application. CdTe is the sensor of choice for energies above 50 keV, given its higher absorption efficiency compared to Si. The Timepix3 is a pixelated hybrid PCD that records each individual photon interaction in the sensor, providing the time-over-threshold (energy) and time-of-arrival of each event at fluxes up to 40 MhitsHits/cm 2 /s. The spectral resolution of CdTe-Timepix3 assemblies degrades with sensor thickness, and the relative weight of front-end electronic noise and sub-threshold charge-sharing losses has not yet been quantified at 55 µm pitch. An empirical equivalent-noise-charge (ENC) model exists for Si-Timepix3 but, to our knowledge, has not been reported for CdTe at this pitch. This work addresses this gap by measuring the front-end ENC of three CdTe-Timepix3 assemblies (1 mm, 3 mm, and 5 mm sensor thickness) from internal test-pulse scans, fitting an empirical ENC model with the detector capacitance estimated from per-pixel geometry, and decomposing the photopeak FWHM at the 241 Am (59.5 keV) line into Fano, front-end, and sub-threshold contributions. A Si-Timepix3 of the same ASIC family is included as a cross-check for the front-end term. The result is a quantitative basis for predicting CdTe-Timepix3 spectral performance as a function of sensor thickness on this ASIC.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 393Poster Number:RTSD-04-393] SiC Timepix3 detector response to fast neutrons: effect of varying sensor bias (#1226)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Foss (Autores: K. Foss , C. Granja , M. Balušík , T. Slavíček , B. Zaťko , A. Šagátová)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava, Bratislava, Slovakia [2] Institute of Electrical Engineering, Slovak Academy of Sciences, Bratislava, Slovakia [3] Institute of Experimental and Applied Physics, Czech Technical University in Prague, Prague, Czech Republic
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In semiconductor radiation detectors such as silicon (Si) and silicon carbide (SiC) the sensor bias determines the radiation sensitive volume. Varying the sensor applied bias can thus significantly change and even distort the detector response, sensitivity and spectral-tracking properties. These effects can be studied and described when the sensor is bump-bonded to the Timepix3 detector which provides particle counting response, high-granularity imaging detection and spectral-tracking ability to single particles. These properties make possible to analyze and resolve particle-type events which is useful for mixed-field decomposition. In this work we examine and experimentally investigate the response of the SiC Timepix3 detector to well-defined fast neutrons to quantify and analyze the changes induced by varying the sensor applied bias voltage. The main effects are further decreasing the detection efficiency, which is overall low (≤ 1%), and only partly reducing the spectral-tracking resolving power to particle-type discrimination.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 394Poster Number:RTSD-04-394] A neural network determining the gamma interaction position in pixelated CZT detectors (#2330)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. S. Anumah (Autores: A. S. Anumah , P. Dendooven , A. Hauptmann , M. Kalliokoski , M. Bezak)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Helsinki, Helsinki Institute of Physics, Helsinki, Finland [2] University of Oulu, Research Unit of Mathematical Sciences of University of Oulu, Finland, Oulu, Finland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This study presents an experimental and computational framework for gamma-ray imaging using a position-sensitive Cadmium Zinc Telluride (CZT) detector combined with deep learning-based reconstruction techniques. A GDS-100 CZT detector with an 11 × 11 pixelated anode matrix was irradiated using a tightly collimated 662 keV Cs-137 gamma-ray beam scanned across the detector surface with 1 mm step size. Detector waveforms were used to train a compact ResNet-based convolutional neural network capable of reconstructing higher-resolution spatial information by mapping 11 × 11 detector inputs to 22 × 22 outputs. Kernel density estimation (KDE) analysis of reconstructed events shows that the predicted interaction positions remain strongly localized around the true coordinates, demonstrating accurate spatial learning. Average spatial spreads of σx = 1.375 mm and σy = 1.398 mm, together with positional deviations below 1 mm, indicate stable and nearly symmetric localization performance. Although edge and corner regions exhibit slightly broader distributions due to detector-related physical effects, the reconstructed interaction densities remain well confined around the true positions. Overall, the results demonstrate that deep learning-based CZT signal analysis can significantly improve spatial reconstruction performance in semiconductor gamma-ray imaging systems.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 395Poster Number:RTSD-04-395] Robust and reliable radionuclide identification under realistic measurement conditions (#2743)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Zappettini (Autores: N. Sarzi Amadè , G. Li , M. Thompson , J. Alexander , M. Echlin , L. Li , N. Zambelli , V. Vicini , M. Bettelli , G. Bentoumi , A. Zappettini)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] due2lab, Reggio Emilia, Italy [2] Canadian Nuclear Laboratories, Chalk River Ontario, Canada [3] IMEM-CNR, Parma, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Reliable radioisotope identification with handheld instruments remains challenging due to limited detector resolution, shielding, low counting statistics, and variable background conditions. We present a convolutional neural network algorithm for automated multi‑isotope identification from gamma‑ray spectra acquired with low‑resolution detectors. The algorithm is trained using an optimized synthetic spectral library of 48 radionuclides and evaluated using measured data acquired under controlled shielding, signal‑to‑noise ratio, and count‑rate conditions. Results show near‑perfect identification accuracy for moderate to high signal‑to‑noise ratio regimes and for low to high statistics. At low signal‑to‑noise ratio the algorithm is still able to recognize some radionuclides with decent accuracy. These results demonstrate that the method provides a practical and scalable solution for real‑time isotope identification in nuclear security and radiation detection systems.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 396Poster Number:RTSD-04-396] In-situ high-resolution gamma spectroscopy for characterization of radiological environmental sites. (#2318)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Rossé (Autores: B. Rossé , L. Fevre , M. Allerme , P. Chotard)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CEA, DAM, DIF, F-91297 Arpajon, France
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In the context of in-situ radiological characterization of sites (natural or artificial radioactivity) and for the dismantling of nuclear installations, high-resolution gamma-ray spectrometry is a powerful tool to both identify and quantify gamma-emitters. This technique makes it possible to better define the state of radiologically polluted soils without having to collect samples. To perform mapping of large areas (a few hundred square meters) and to detect radiological hotspots, we first use a 2''x2'' NaI(Tl) scintillator probe (Mirion® SG2R) at 20 cm from the ground in pedestrian mode, called C.R.E.M.P ( C aractérisation R adiologique E n M ode P iéton, radiological characterization in pedestrian mode). Then, for each particular points, high-resolution gamma spectrometry is performed with an HPGe Ortec® DETECTIVE-X. To obtain a reliable transfer function, the absolute efficiency of the detectors must be known. We therefore used our radiological characterization platform located at CEA/DAM Ile de France. Thanks to these measurements, a geometric model of the HPGe detector was developed and optimized using the MCNP Monte Carlo simulation code taking into account real position and shape of the germanium crystal including mechanical supports and dead layers. To validate the model, experiments on radiologically marked standard soils were performed. Extrapolated data from MCNP simulations make it possible to obtain the transfer functions for each detected radionuclide. The whole method, measurements and simulations will be described.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 397Poster Number:RTSD-04-397] Gamma Spectroscopy Analysis and Benchmarking of Nuclear Fuel for Next Generation Reactor Designs (#3247)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. T. Giglio (Autores: D. T. Giglio , T. V. Holschuh , S. J. Thompson , J. D. Hix , D. L. Chichester , J. Sanders)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Idaho National Laboratory, Idaho Falls, Idaho, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper contains the findings associated with the collection of gamma spectroscopy of a variety of fuel types being utilized in the deployment of the next generation of nuclear reactors. Gamma spectroscopy of TRISO fuel types at HALEU levels of enrichment were collected and analyzed prior to installment in their respective reactor designs. Preliminary measurements of these fuels establish a strong baseline that serve as important experimental data points for simulation validation and monitoring fuel characteristics that are underexplored in next generation reactor designs such as burnup rates, and fuel stability (physical, chemical, performance). In addition, the established baseline also serves as an important benchmark for quality assurance and nuclear nonproliferation by providing reference spectrum for archiving purposes in a nuclear fuel landscape that is rapidly expanding. This ensures enrichment reporting is accurate in the event of fuel mixing/reprocessing prior to reactor loading.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 398Poster Number:RTSD-04-398] Comparison of the simulated response of the in-house DT hybrid pixel detector with synchrotron beam tests (#2098)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Leroy (Autores: M. Leroy , M. Dupont , E. Gaborieau-Borissenko , C. Morel , Y. Boursier)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Aix Marseille Univ., CNRS/IN2P3, CPPM, Marseille, France [2] Detection Technology Oyj., R&D, Moirans, France
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Simulation of Photon Counting Detectors (PCD) is essential to optimize detector design and to assess detector response for photon counting CT. In this work, synchrotron measurements performed with the new PCD tiles, developed by Detection Technology (DT) are compared to simulated data. The detector prototype is a pixelated array of CdTe and CZT pixel with 350 μm pixel pitch. Each pixel has 6 energy thresholds. Measurements were carried out at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF) using pencil beam scan to study charge-sharing and fluorescence escape. The experiment was reproduced in a simulation framework that encompasses physics interaction within the sensor, charge generation, drift, and diffusion and Coulomb repulsion. The comparison focuses on counts of distribution across pixel positions and single pixel spectral response. Results show a good agreement for central pixel irradiation, but discrepancies are observed near pixel boundaries. The assessment of the modeling for interpixel irradiation is currently under study.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 399Poster Number:RTSD-04-399] Characterization and Compensation of Radiation-Induced Leakage Current in CdTe/CZT Detectors Under High-flux X-ray Irradiation (#2377)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 X. Ran (Autores: X. Ran , Z. Deng , H. Luo , H. Dong)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Tsinghua University, Beijing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Radiatio-induced leakage current has been found in ohmic CdTe/CZT detectors under high-flux X-ray irradiation scenario such as photon-counting X-ray CT and new generation light sources. Slowly evolving radiation-induced leakage current that compromises signal stability. In this work, we experimentally characterize the dynamic behavior of this leakage current using step-irradiation and rapid-chopping measurements on a custom 32×32 pixel CdTe detector module. The results reveal a two-timescale response consisting of a fast photocurrent component and a slow, history-dependent leakage component that increases approximately exponentially during irradiation and decays over minutes after beam-off. This behavior is attributed to trap occupancy dynamics that modulate carrier injection at the contacts. A first-order exponential model is proposed to describe the temporal evolution, and a recursive deconvolution framework is explored for signal correction. However, observed nonlinearities and flux/history dependence indicate that a linear time-invariant (LTI) assumption is insufficient, suggesting the need for a more general nonlinear model. These findings provide insight into the instability mechanisms of Ohmic CdTe detectors and offer experimental support for the development of improved dynamic correction strategies for high-flux X-ray imaging applications.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 400Poster Number:RTSD-04-400] Compton Polarimetric Potential of a Low Power CdTe Timepix3 Frame Mode Detector (#2920)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. Rodrigues (Autores: G. Veyrac , R. M. Curado Da Silva , J. Maia , J. Campos , P. Carmo , G. Falcão , C. Francisco , M. Letra , F. Pinheiro , D. Rodrigues , J. Sousa , A. Trindade , C. Granja , M. Kasal , M. Konečný , J. Jakůbek , L. Marek)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] LIP - Laboratório de Instrumentação e Física Experimental de Partículas, Coimbra, Portugal [2] University of Coimbra, Department of Physics, Coimbra, Portugal [3] University of Beira Interior, Physics Department, Covilhã, Portugal [4] University of Coimbra, Department of Informatics Engineering, Coimbra, Portugal [5] University of Coimbra, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Coimbra, Portugal [6] University of Coimbra, Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory, Coimbra, Portugal [7] ADVACAM s.r.o., Prague, Czech Republic
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract CdTe Timepix3 based instruments are an excellent option to perform fine Compton gamma-ray polarimetry. Its high pixelization level (55×55 µm 2 ) allows to maximize instruments modulation factor and to deliver the higher polar angular resolution in the soft gamma-ray domain. This level of performance is especially important for future gamma-ray astrophysics' telescopes, since high-energy polarimetry is still a domain with a vast research potential. Timepix3 can be operated in two modes: frame mode and data-driven mode. In data-driven mode each interaction full detection data is available: pixel position (x and y), energy and time. In the frame mode only position (x and y) and energy are available for a given time interval, during which all interactions are integrated in a single frame. However, in this mode less intensive front-end electronics' processing capacity is required leading to substantial lower power consumption. This is an advantage that can be decisive for applications where high sensitive polarimetry must be performed in low electric power platforms, such as cubesat platforms. An experimental set of measurements with a CdTe Timepix3 operating in frame mode was performed at ESRF under a ~99% polarized 200 keV beam. A Q polarization modulation factor of 0.71 ± 0.014 was obtained, proving that under certain conditions and constraints, frame-mode polarimetry is not only a valid method but also a performant one.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 401Poster Number:RTSD-04-401] Imaging Performance Comparison of a GaAs Photon-Counting Detector and an Energy-Integrating Detector under Various Photon-Flux Conditions (#3232)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Wang (Autores: L. Yang , H. Li , D. Nalyvaiko , V. Gnatyuk , J. Kalliopuska , X. Ji , X. Lai , B. Wang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] ShanghaiTech University, School of Biomedical Engineering, Shanghai, China [2] Southeast University, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Nanjing, China [3] Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare Advanced Technology Research Institute Co.,Ltd., Shanghai, China [4] Advafab OY, Espoo, Finland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This work compares the imaging performance of a GaAs photon-counting detector (PCD) and an energy-integrating detector (EID) under various photon-flux conditions. The detectors were characterized using the modulation transfer function (MTF), noise power spectrum (NPS), and detective quantum efficiency (DQE), and were evaluated under similar effective spatial-resolution conditions. An NPS-based noise prediction model was then used to estimate the image standard deviation as a function of photon count. The results show that the GaAs PCD and the resolution-matched EID exhibit comparable frequency-domain performance and image quality under the reference photon-flux condition. At low photon flux, however, the PCD shows a markedly lower predicted noise level. Finally, phantom imaging experiments further confirm that the PCD provides lower background fluctuations and clearer structural visibility under low-flux conditions. These results demonstrate the noise advantage of GaAs photon-counting detectors for low-flux X-ray imaging.

sub_talks.title: [JS-03-01] Role of Al 2 O 3 passivation on high-resolution 4H-SiC radiation detectors (#1671)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. C. Mandal (Autores: K. C. Mandal , S. K. Chaudhuri , F. H. Ruddy)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of South Carolina, Electrical Engineering Department, Columbia, South Carolina, United States of America [2] Ruddy Consulting, Nuclear Detection and Imaging, Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Oxide passivation plays a critical role in stabilizing semiconductor radiation detectors by suppressing surface states and enabling low-leakage, high-resolution operation. In this work, Al 2 O 3 -passivated Ni/4H-SiC Schottky radiation detectors were fabricated on n-type epitaxial layers of varying thickness (20, 150, and 250 μm) using pulsed laser deposition without post-deposition annealing. All devices exhibit uniform rectification with Schottky barrier heights of ~1.3 eV, low interface trap density (~10⁹ cm⁻²eV⁻¹), and reverse leakage dominated by Poole-Frenkel transport. Capacitance-voltage measurements indicate a flat-band potential of ~2.3 V due to fixed oxide charge, while frequency dispersion confirms minimal contribution from slow interface states. Under 5.486 MeV α-particle irradiation, the detectors demonstrate efficient self-biased operation with energy resolution of 3.3% at 0 V, improving to ~0.5-0.6% at -40 V. A detailed comparison of two nominally identical 150 μm detectors reveals significant variation in charge collection efficiency (~0.99 vs ~0.6) and energy resolution despite similar electrical characteristics, indicating that bulk carrier trapping dominates performance variability. Deep-level transient spectroscopy identifies Z 1/2 centers as the primary recombination-active defects limiting resolution across all thicknesses. A broad high-energy feature is definitively resolved, for the first time in Al 2 O 3 -passivated 4H-SiC Schottky detectors, using isothermal transient spectroscopy into two distinct defect levels at E C -1.05 eV and E C -1.1 eV, attributed to oxide-related ON2a/b states. This work establishes a unified understanding of interface and bulk defect effects in SiC radiation detectors for optimizing high-resolution operation in harsh environments.

sub_talks.title: [JS-03-02] Vacuum-deposited metal halide perovskite film as a radiation scintillator (#2471)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Zahid (Autores: M. Zahid , A. Dickinson , J. Jayarathne , C. Crean , P. Sellin)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Surrey, School of Mathematics and Physics, Guildford, United Kingdom [2] University of Surrey, School of Mathematics and Physics, Guildford, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Metal halide perovskite (MHP) has been widely investigated as a radiation scintillator. Current solution-processing methods used to fabricate the MHP film suffer from toxic solvent issues and are limited in their ability to scale up for a large area detector. Single-source vapour deposition offers a solvent-free alternative that uses a single precursor, making it a promising technique for scalable film fabrication. In this study, (BA) 2 PbBr 4 films were fabricated using SSVD onto glass substrates under high vacuum. The films were subsequently characterised, and the X-ray scintillation performance was evaluated. The results revealed that SSVD produces a thick film with a mean thickness of 10.5 ± 4.0 um and has a polycrystalline grain distribution. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirmed that the SSVD method preserved the composition, as the Br/Pb ratio is consistent with the theoretical value 4 for (BA)₂PbBr₄. Photoluminescence spectroscopy revealed a narrow peak emission 423 nm with FWHM 13 nm in close agreement with reported values for solution-grown crystals, confirming that the optoelectronic structure is preserved after deposition. Under 50 kVp X-ray irradiation, the film exhibited a fast, stable, linear dose rate response yielding scintillation sensitivity of 2464 µC Gy⁻¹ cm⁻². These results demonstrate that SSVD is a viable, solvent-free method for fabricating MHP scintillator films with direct implications for scalable fabrication for next-generation medical imaging detectors.

sub_talks.title: [JS-03-03] FAST NEUTRON DETECTION USING A SINGLE-CRYSTAL DIAMOND DETECTOR (#2449)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Zaťko (Autores: B. Zaťko , M. Varga , A. Šagátová , E. Kováčová , T. Slavíček , R. Sýkora)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Slovak Academy of Sciences, Institute of Electrical Engineering, Bratislava, Slovakia [2] Slovak University of Technology, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, Bratislava, Slovakia [3] Czech Technical University in Prague, Institute of Experimental and Applied Physics, Prague, Czech Republic
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Diamond is a highly promising semiconductor material for ionizing radiation detection. Diamond-based detectors are excellent candidates for neutron detection due to interactions on relatively light carbon nuclei. Moreover, these detectors exhibit low sensitivity to X-ray and gamma radiation that often accompany neutron flux. Neutrons with energies below approximately 6 MeV are detected solely via elastic scattering on carbon nuclei within the diamond crystal. At higher energies, nuclear reactions occur, producing alpha particles, protons, and ions that can be detected by the detector. In this experiment, we use a single-crystal CVD diamond detector to detect fast neutrons with energies ranging from 300 keV to 18.5 MeV. A diamond detector has square contact dimensions of 3.6 × 3.6 mm 2 and a thickness of 0.5 mm. Testing the detector with an alpha-particle source showed a high-energy resolution of about 0.4% at 5.5 MeV. The detector was used to detect monoenergetic neutrons ranging from 250 keV to 911 keV, 3.5 MeV to 4.5 MeV, and 14.6 MeV to 18.5 MeV, generated by p-T, D-D, and D-T nuclear reactions at Van de Graaff accelerator, respectively. The single-crystal diamond detector showed good linearity and excellent detection properties. In the detected spectra, all main neutron-detector interactions were identified.

sub_talks.title: [JS-03-04] Improving the spectral resolution of photons in silicon Timepix3 by correcting for the cluster size and by lowering the Krummenacher current (#1416)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Jelinek (Autores: J. Jelinek , B. Bergmann)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Czech Technical University, Institute of Experimental and Applied Physics, Prague, Czech Republic [2] University of Geneva, Department of Particle and Nuclear Physics, Geneva, Genève, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We investigated ways to improve the spectral resolution of a Timepix3 hybrid pixel detector with a 1 mm thick silicon sensor for X-ray and soft gamma photons. A standard procedure is to calibrate the time-over-threshold (ToT) to deposited energy for each pixel, but even then, there remains room for improvement. The first improvement was lowering the Krummenacher current (Ikrum) to increase the ToT at even low-energy deposits to get a finer resolution. The second novel improvement was creating an additional calibration on cluster energies, taking into account the cluster size. It was observed that clusters of larger size feature a higher energy than smaller clusters created by the same photon source. The cluster energy could therefore be corrected based on its size, and we found that this correction is linear for each cluster size. Both the lowering of the Ikrum together with the cluster size correction decreased the full width at half maximum (FWHM) by 17-35 % compared to the initial settings in the energy range of 4-136 keV. The higher the photon energy, the larger the percentage decrease in FWHM. We intend to utilize the enhanced spectral resolution in Compton X-ray polarimetry. There, the coincident events of a Compton scattering followed by a photoabsorption are measured. The sum of the deposited energies in the two events gives the original energy of the photon. The FWHM of coincident pairs of clusters decreased by 22-44 % compared to the initial settings in the energy range of 43-136 keV.

sub_talks.title: [JS-03-05] Simulation-based inference for uncertainty-aware interaction reconstruction in 3D CZT drift strip detectors (#2532)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Valverde Mahou (Autores: A. Valverde Mahou , M. Kossakowski , I. Kuvvetli , S. Hauberg , G. Arvanitidis , C. A. Naesseth)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Technical University of Denmark, DTU Compute, Kgs. Lyngby, Denmark [2] Technical University of Denmark, DTU Space, Kgs. Lyngby, Denmark [3] University of Amsterdam, Informatics Institute, Amsterdam, Netherlands
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Accurate interaction position reconstruction in radiation detectors is often limited by the lack of tractable likelihood functions and the stochastic nature of particle transport and charge induction processes. In this work, we present a simulation-based inference framework for 3D Cadmium Zinc Telluride drift strip detectors (3D CZT DSD) that learns a probabilistic inverse mapping from Charge Induction Efficiency signals to interaction positions using Monte Carlo generated training data. We formulate the reconstruction problem as Neural Posterior Estimation and train a neural network to predict a Gaussian approximation of the posterior distribution over interaction positions. The model is optimized using negative log-likelihood, enabling simultaneous estimation of interaction positions and associated uncertainties in a single amortized inference step. Preliminary results on synthetic datasets show that the proposed method produces meaningful uncertainty estimates that provide insights into detector response variability compared to deterministic regression approaches.

sub_talks.title: [JS-03-06] One-Year Performance Analysis of the cadmium zinc TElluride Radiation Imager (TERI) in Orbit (#1229)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 N. Kirschner (Autores: N. Kirschner , D. Shy , M. Streicher , D. M. Groves , Z. He , J. Jaworski , W. Kaye , J. Mason , R. Parsons , F. Zhang , Y. Zhu , A. Thompson , C. C. Cheung , A. Hutcheson , M. Johnson-Rambert , N. Johnson , B. Phlips)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] National Research Council Research Associate resident, U.S. Naval Research Laboratory, Washington, United States of America [2] U.S. Naval Research Laboratory, Washington, United States of America [3] H3D, Inc., Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States of America [4] Technology Service Corporation, Arlington, Virginia, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The cadmium zinc TElluride Radiation Imager (TERI) was successfully launched to the International Space Station (ISS) on April 21, 2025 as a part of the Department of Defense's Space Test Program (STP-H10) mission. The primary mission of TERI is to space-qualify large-volume 4×4×1.5 cm 3 pixelated CdZnTe (CZT) detectors. The system is composed of four of these advanced detectors, each of which is 3D position sensitive, allowing for Compton event imaging. Here, we report on the one-year in-orbit performance results of TERI, including measurements of the background rate, which align with expected orbital variations. We analyze the 511 keV line and observe no significant degradation over nine months in orbit. Additionally, we observe multiple spectral lines, several of which are consistent with known activation lines.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 F. d'Almeida (Autores: F. d'Almeida , V. Bottau , C. Eleon , B. Pérot , C. Carasco , M. Abdelli , J. Lamblin , O. Litaize , A. Chalil)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract A system comprising sixteen polyvinyl toluene (PVT) scintillators is under development at the Nuclear Measurements Laboratory (CEA IRESNE) for the passive nondestructive assay of alpha-contaminated waste drums. Although PVT scintillators offer a low-cost alternative to 3 He counters, their sensitivity to gamma rays and scattering cross-talk restricts the use of traditional multiplicity equations for determining spontaneous fission rates. Machine learning methods provide a viable solution to this inverse problem but require extensive training datasets, necessitating a reliable, experimentally validated numerical model. Therefore, a novel calculation scheme utilizing the FIFRELIN and PHITS Monte Carlo codes is introduced. This framework generates and transports prompt fission particles, extracting raw time-of-flight and energy deposition data. The resulting files are subsequently processed using ROOT scripts to model the detectors' response. Specifically, the energy resolution function implemented in the simulation is derived from a 60 Co source measurement, utilizing parameters adjusted to align the simulated and experimental spectra. The full framework demonstrates good agreement with the measurement of 252 Cf doubles and triples counts, enabling the generation of training data for regression models capable of accurately predicting spontaneous fission rates across various measured mock drum configurations.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-09-02] Recent Advances in Developing Fluoride Eutectic Scintillators for Neutron Detection (#1651)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 C. L. Wang (Autores: C. L. Wang , X. Zhou)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Songshan Lake Materials Laboratory, Neutron Science-Imaging Science and Technology, Dongguan, China [2] Dongguan Institute of Materials Science and Technology, Division of Advanced Scientific Instruments and Equipment, Donguan, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The 6 Li-glass (GS20) Scintillator-based Anger cameras have been used for single-crystal neutron diffractometry. To expand their applications for more neutron-scattering instruments and Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) with a neutron flux~10 9 n/s/cm 2 , there are urgent needs to improve the neutron detection efficiency, light yield, and neutron-gamma discrimination ratio (NGD ratio, or efficiency ratio), and to reduce the light decay lifetime of the neutron scintillator. We have developed Eu 2+ :CaF 2 / 6 LiF eutectic scintillators to potentially replace the GS20 in neutron Anger cameras. In this work, we show our further endeavors in i). enhancing light yield of the eutectics in casting method; ii). improving transparency and uniformity of the eutectics in oriented growth; iii). reducing the light decay lifetime to about 4 ns via Pr 3+ doping; iv). the enhancement in the NGD ratio using an optimized multi-layer graph filter under a self-supervised learning framework. Therefore, future Eu:CaF 2 / 6 LiF eutectic neutron scintillators are expected to find wider applications not only in neutron scattering and BNCT, but also in nuclear power plants and homeland security.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-09-03] 3D Boron-Coated Straw Detector Array for Tomographic Multiplicity Counting (#1768)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Fang (Autores: M. Fang , D. Breitenmoser , S. Clarke , S. Pozzi , S. Thompson , D. Chichester , A. Di Fulvio)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Department of Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering, Urbana, Illinois, United States of America [2] University of Michigan, Department of Nuclear Engineering & Radiological Sciences, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States of America [3] Idaho National Laboratory, Radiochemistry and Nuclear Measurements Department, Idaho Falls, Idaho, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Accurate assessment of plutonium content during pyroprocessing is needed to enhance the proliferation resistance. Matrix isotopic heterogeneity, source non-uniformity, and high gamma-ray emission rate prevent the application of traditional non-destructive assay (NDA) systems and methods. We aim to develop a novel NDA system that can withstand pyroprocessing harsh environments and have consistent sensitivity and accuracy despite different fuel form factors. The proposed NDA system encompasses two system modules, a boron-coated-straw (BCS) multiplicity module and a 3D boron-coated-straw detector array (3D-BCSDA) tomography module. The multiplicity module performs multiplicity counting and provides assay observables, whereas the tomographic module reduces systematic biases by enabling geometry-aware corrections. In this work, we report the development of the multiplicity module and the 3D-BCSDA tomography module. The multiplicity module consists of six 64-straw BCS panels, with a measured neutron detection efficiency of 12.4% and die-away time of 42 μs. The tomography module is a moderated array incorporating thirty one-meter-long boron-coated straws with double-sided readout. Time delay lines and charge sharing have been implemented to enable 3D localization of the neutron interaction event. We will begin experimental testing with laboratory sources at UIUC and plutonium sources at INL to assess the system's accuracy in real-world conditions, supporting the integration of tomographic imaging with neutron multiplicity counting for bulk plutonium assay.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-09-04] An Imaging and Spectroscopy Detector for High-Energy and High-Rate Gamma-Ray Measurements (#2645)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Urban (Autores: K. Urban , M. Piroddi , C. Riboldi , A. Forgione , L. Santini , F. Garzetti , G. Borghi , M. Carminati , E. Bellotti , D. Bortot , D. Mazzucconi , C. Fiorini)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Politecnico di Milano, Department of Electronics, Information and Bioengineering (DEIB), Milan, Italy [2] National Institute for Nuclear Physics (INFN), Milan Section, Milan, Italy [3] Politecnico di Milano, Department of Energy (DENG), Milan, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The REALPATH detector and readout platform is a pixilated scintillation detector developed for prompt gamma imaging in proton therapy. Prompt gamma imaging aims to provide online verification of proton range via the position-sensitive detection of prompt gamma rays emitted during proton treatment. Due to the high fluence of modern medical proton accelerators, the detector is designed to cope with rates of up to 1 Mcps per pixel across 512 pixels. At the same time, good spectroscopic performance at high energies in the range of 3 MeV to 6 MeV is beneficial for neutron background rejection and prompt-gamma emission analysis. To address these requirements, each LYSO pixel features an independent SiPM readout, implemented with the custom SITH (spectroscopy imaging timing hadrontherapy) ASIC. In this work, we present the experimental characterization of the first 64-channel detector module. Using a 137 Cs source, we measured an average resolution of 8.5% at 662 keV for all pixels at low rates. The high source activity allowed us to characterize the detector up to 1.9 Mcps input count rate per channel. The high-energy performance was tested with a 241 Am-Be source that provides gamma rays of 4.44 MeV. By applying a light-sharing correction and combining data from coincident events across multiple pixels, we achieved an energy resolution of 4.8% at the 4.44 MeV full-energy peak. With these characteristics, the detector may also be suited for applications beyond prompt gamma imaging that require position-resolved high-rate gamma spectroscopy.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-09-05] Ratiometric Alpha-Particle and Gamma-Ray Imaging with a Ligand-Stabilized CsPbBr 3 Perovskite-Nanoparticle Coating on a 4.8-Megapixel Stacked CMOS Sensor (#2798)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 V. Gruev (Autores: H. Chang , S. Mandot , S. Zhu , M. Fang , A. Di Fulvio , S. Nie , L.-J. Meng , V. Gruev)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Champaign, Illinois, United States of America [2] University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Department of Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering, Champaign, Illinois, United States of America [3] University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Department of Bioengineering, Champaign, Illinois, United States of America [4] University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Beckman Institute for Advance Science and Technology, Champaign, Illinois, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Conventional alpha/gamma instruments often use bulk scintillators coupled to photomultiplier or silicon-photomultiplier pulse processing, or hybrid pixel detectors optimized for timing or deposited-energy readout; compact megapixel imaging with ratiometric particle-type contrast remains less developed. A monolithic alternative is demonstrated by spin-coating a 10-µm film of ligand-stabilized CsPbBr 3 perovskite nanoparticles (PNCs) onto a vertically stacked 4.8-megapixel complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor containing three photodiodes per pixel. Gamma-ray interactions in the PNC layer generate green scintillation photons that are registered differentially by the top, middle, and bottom photodiodes, whereas alpha particles deposit energy primarily in the top photodiode layer. Comparing these spatially registered photodiode responses with cluster amplitude and event footprint yields ratiometric single-frame alpha/gamma signatures without an external scintillator/photomultiplier timing chain. Radiation-induced events were extracted from full-frame readout as temporally nonpersistent, 8-connected pixel clusters. Relative to the uncoated sensor, the coated detector increased gamma-candidate event yield by 10 3 -10 4 in Am-241, Co-57, and Ac-225 measurements. Gamma-candidate clusters exhibited median signal-to-noise ratios of 10.9-11.0 and a median footprint of one pixel. In unfiltered Ac-225 free-path measurements, the coated sensor preserved the direct alpha-particle response while adding gamma sensitivity. These results establish a spin-coated PNC/three-photodiode stacked CMOS architecture for compact, spatially resolved, ratiometric alpha/gamma imaging.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-09-06] Evolution of ZnS:Ag/ 6 LiF wavelength shifting fibre detectors from flat to tilted geometry (#2905)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 G. Mauri (Autores: G. Mauri , J. G. Sykora , S. E. Mann , E. M. Schooneveld , N. J. Rhodes)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] STFC, ISIS, Harwell Campus, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Scintillator-based neutron detectors have been developed at ISIS for over three decades, with ongoing research and development focused on enhancing performance and meeting increasingly demanding instrument requirements. The Endeavour programme places new demands on detector technology, particularly in achieving large-area coverage, high spatial resolution, and high counting-rate capability. Conventional WLSF detectors are built from stacked flat scintillator screens interleaved with fibre planes. Achieving high neutron efficiency (~80% at 1.8 Å) requires four scintillator layers and two fibre planes. This work presents a novel approach to the design and manufacture of ZnS:Ag/⁶LiF wavelength-shifting fibre (WLSF) detectors, with the potential to significantly improve both performance and cost-efficiency for next-generation systems. This concept instead exploits the increase in neutron path length by tilting the scintillator relative to the incident beam. A V-shaped strip geometry is introduced, where the angle can be tuned to control detection efficiency and fibre spacing. This design also provides optical isolation between strips, enabling parallel signal processing for neutron event identification, which significantly reduces the detector dead time.A first linear position-sensitive detector prototype was developed featuring four regions with varying fibre pitches and tilt angles. This was followed by a 2D position-sensitive detector based on the same principle. The designs and performance results from tests on ISIS instruments are presented, along with a discussion of simplified manufacturing and reduced costs. Overall, these advancements enhance detector capability and support the continued evolution of the ISIS science programme, enabling future instrument upgrades.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 G. De Geronimo (Autores: G. De Geronimo , W. H. Baumgartner , S. Chakrabarti , W. Hodge , N. Poudyal , P. S. Ray , J. Roberts , C. A. Wilson-Hodge , E. A. Wulf)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] DG Circuits, Syosset, New York, United States of America [2] Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, New York, United States of America [3] U.S. Naval Research Laboratory, Washington, United States of America [4] University of Alabama in Huntsville, Huntsville, Alabama, United States of America [5] University of California San Diego, San Diego, California, United States of America [6] NASA Marshall Space Flight Center, Huntsville, Alabama, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We present NSX1, a very-low-power 64-channel front-end ASIC developed for large-area broadband-energy X-ray Silicon Drift Detectors (SDD) for space applications. Fabricated in 180 nm CMOS, it integrates dual-gain charge amplification, shaping, discrimination, peak detection, analog multiplexing, and 12-bit analog-to-digital conversion. The ASIC offers extensive programmability, including high-resolution mode, various discrimination modes, neighbor-channel/chip processing, peak processing modes, and power-down options. At less than 600 µW per channel and ∼110 fF input capacitance (SDD anode + wirebond), it achieves an Equivalent Noise Charge (ENC) below 7 e⁻ (< 6 e⁻ in high-resolution mode), meeting or exceeding STROBE-X requirements.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 U. Trunk (Autores: U. Trunk , A. Klujev , S. Lange , A. Marras , D. Pennicard , C. B. Wunderer , H. Krueger , S. Spannagel , T. Vanat , H. Graafsma)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] DESY - Deutsches Elektronensynchrotron, Photon Science - Detector Systems Group, Hamburg, Hamburg, Germany [2] DESY - Deutsches Elektronensynchrotron, CFEL, Hamburg, Hamburg, Germany [3] Universität Bonn, Physikalisches Institut, Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [4] Mid-Sweden University, Sundsvall, Sweden
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The Co ntinuous R eadout D igitizing I mager A rray (CoRDIA) is an X-ray hybrid pixel detector currently being developed for scientific experiments exploiting the performance of 4 th generation light sources, in particular that of PETRA IV, but also CW free electron lasers (FELs). Operating on the charge-integrating principle, it adopts the dynamic gain switching architecture and circuit topology of the AGIPD detector at the European XFEL to combine single photon sensitivity with a large dynamic range. Implementing the readout ASIC in a 65 nm CMOS technology enables a small pixel size of 110 × 110 µm 2 . To ensure up to 150 kframes/s dead time free operation, images are stored by a sample and hold (S&H) circuit, before digitisation by an 11 bit SAR ADC serving blocks of 16 pixels each. Data from 128 ADCs (2 kpixels) is driven off-chip by a 5.12 Gbit/s wire transmitter (GWT). In spring of 2026 we completed the design of the '20 k' prototype CoRDIA 0.5, which combines the full signal chain consisting of 1232 4 × 4 pixel blocks (tested on CoRDIA 0.2) with 14 GWTs (tested on Timepix4 and CoRDIA 0.3). This chip also contains a programmable sequencer, controlling the ADC and readout operation. This sequencer is based on an SRAM memory and thus much more flexible than counter-based solutions as implemented e.g. on the AGIPD chip. In addition to wirebond pads through silicon via (TSV) landing pads are evenly distributed across the whole chip area enabling 'local powering' for future gapless detectors. We will present the design of CoRDIA 0.5 with emphasis on the implementation of the readout sequencer, and new characterisation results.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Macchiarulo (Autores: L. Macchiarulo , I. Mostafanezhad , E. Forsythe , G. Uehara , S. Mazza , J. Ott , C. Chock)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In this article we describe the design of the LGAD Integrated Digitizer (LID) - a readout Integrated circuit that is meant for tight coupling with dense LGAD arrays. The circuit is a multi-channel device that performs internal pre-amplification and self-triggered high rate digitization (10 Gsps) and digital processing. The RoIC is an evolution of previous HPSoC chips[1][2][3], and it features variants of the front end Transimpedance amplifier (TIA) that are capable of handling the higher capacitance of strip detectors. The paper will detail the design and performance of the TIAs, the planned integration with sensors, and the definition and hardware implementation of algorithms using waveforms from multiple channels to extract accurate position and timing information. Simulation results in the presence of noise show that the system is capable of fine location to within 10 percent of the sensor pitch and up to 9 ps of timing resolution in the best case.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 C. Bakalis (Autores: H. Kim , L. Rota , A. Pena-Perez , C. Bakalis , L. Fanals-i-Batllori , D. Alnajjar , G. Liu , X. Defay , D. Doering , A. Gupta , A. Habib , M. P. Hammer , P.-C. Huang , C. Kenny , H. Hernandez , B. Markovic , F. Mele , H. Shi , R. Herbst , P. King , A. Dragone)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, TID/ID/IC, Menlo Park, California, United States of America [2] Argonne National Laboratory, Lemont, Illinois, United States of America [3] CentraleSupélec, Université Paris-Saclay, Gif-sur-Yvette, France [4] European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN), Geneva, Switzerland [5] Politecnico di Milano, Milan, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We present the design progress and early test results of SparkPix-S, a charge-integrating readout application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed for next-generation X-ray cameras operating at the 1 MHz frame rate of LCLS-II. The SparkPix-S detector is being developed for X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy (XPCS) and Speckle Visibility Spectroscopy (XSVS) experiments, where the inherent sparsity of the data - with average frame occupancies well below 1 % - enables a fundamentally different readout approach compared to conventional full-frame readout ASIC architectures. The pixel front-end architecture combines a charge-integrating front-end, coupled to an in-pixel discriminator to control the sparse readout architecture. 1 MHz operation is achieved through the combination of per-pixel asynchronous sparse readout logic, high-speed CML serial links, and a novel frame-work for sparse readouts named Pix2PGP. The first full-reticle (312 × 384 pixels) prototype has been fabricated in 130 nm CMOS technology. Electrical characterization of the front-end confirms noise performance below 60 electrons r.m.s., enabling single-photon sensitivity for tender X-ray energies. We report on the chip architecture, preliminary measurement results with a silicon sensor bump-bonded to the ASIC, and first results from the sample X-ray source testing with Cd-109 and Am-241, demonstrating the viability of the sparsified readout concept for MHz-rate photon science at free-electron laser facilities.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Ratti (Autores: L. Ratti , S. Bottinelli , T. M. Floris , T. Hemperek , P. Lazzaroni , M. Manghisoni , V. Re , C. Vacchi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Pavia, Pavia, Italy [2] University of Bergamo, Dalmine, Italy [3] DECTRIS AG Ltd., Baden- Daettwil, Switzerland [4] INFN - Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Pavia, Dalmine, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract A 10-bit single-slope analog-to-digital converter has been developed in a 110 nm CMOS technology for amplitude measurements in large-area pixel detectors for X-ray imaging. The converter generates the linear ramp and the timestamp in the chip periphery and distributes them to the 256x256 pixels in the chip core for comparison with the local amplitude sample. This approach reduces power dissipation in the chip core and achieves an optimal trade-off between IR-drop effects and front-end noise performance, while preserving the integrity of the analog sample at the pixel level. Although the current detector design targets frame rates in the tens-of-kHz range, the possibility of scaling to higher rates is explored through the implementation of a compression feature that accounts for Poisson noise in the photon signal.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Pacher (Autores: L. Pacher , A. Lai)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Istituto Nazionale Fisica Nucleare, Cagliari, Cagliari, Italy [2] University of Turin and INFN Torino, Torino, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The IGNITE project is developing advanced technical solutions in 28-nm CMOS technology for next-generation collider tracking systems, targeting time resolutions below 40 ps RMS while preserving the key constraints of current inner trackers, namely small pixel dimensions (~50 μm pitch) and low power density (1-2 W/cm.). This contribution presents characterization results for the Ignite64 prototype ASIC, featuring a 64x64-pixel matrix with 55 μm pitch and one TDC per pixel. The chip has been conceived as a test platform for advanced silicon sensor technologies, including 3D sensors, TI-LGADs, and i-LGADs. The Ignite64 adopts a modular architecture that is directly scalable to the final IgnitER ASIC, currently close to submission. The prototype implements and validates dedicated solutions for accurate power delivery and low-jitter clock distribution, both essential for achieving uniform timing performance across large pixel matrices. Several alternative Analog Front-End architectures have also been integrated and experimentally evaluated to optimize the trade-off among timing performance, power consumption, and Total Ionizing Dose tolerance. At an input charge of 1 fC and a power consumption of 10 μW per pixel, the measured timing resolution is approximately 20 ps RMS at zero input capacitance, remaining around 35 ps RMS at a typical pixel capacitance of 100 fF. Performance uniformity across the full matrix is well controlled, with an RMS spread of about 5 ps in the distribution of pixel time resolutions, demonstrating the effectiveness of the adopted architectural and powering strategies. Comprehensive laboratory characterization results are presented for operation both with and without connected sensors. Measurements include tests performed using the integrated pulsing system, radioactive sources, and a dedicated infrared laser setup capable of accurately reproducing the charge deposition profile generated by charged particles in silicon sensors.
