sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 130Poster Number:NSS-13-130] A Fully FPGA-Based 3D (x-y-t) Imager with 24 μm Spatial Resolution for Cross Delay-Line Detectors (#1821)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 N. Lusardi (Autores: F. Garzetti , N. Lusardi , A. Costa , E. Ronconi , G. Fiumicelli , A. Geraci , M. Cautero , M. Colja , S. Carrato , L. Stebel , R. Sergo , G. Cautero)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Politecnico di Milano, Dipartimento di Elettronica, Informazione e Bioingegneria, Milano, Italy [2] INFN, Milano, Milano, Italy [3] University of Trieste, Department of Physics, Trieste, Italy [4] Elettra Sincrotrone, Trieste, Trieste, Italy [5] University of Trieste, DIA, Trieste, Italy [6] INFN, Trieste, Trieste, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Advanced X-ray sources such as synchrotrons and Free Electron Lasers (FELs) enable ultrafast time-resolved experiments, requiring acquisition systems with event-by-event timing and spatial resolution. Cross Delay-Line (CDL) detectors are well suited for simultaneous time-space encoding via time-to-space conversion. Standard high-performance architectures rely on Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC)-based Time-to-Digital Converters (TDCs) or Time-to-Amplitude Converters (TACs), followed by Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) processing, but lack reconfigurability. We present a high-performance, fully FPGA-based reconfigurable acquisition system implementing both the TDC and real-time 3D (x, y, t) reconstruction in programmable logic, eliminating ASIC dependence while maintaining state-of-the-art performance and enabling full adaptability to experimental conditions. The system employs a two-FPGA architecture, with a 8-channel TDC and a dedicated reconstruction unit. The TDC achieves 12 ps rms timing precision, 9.6 ns dead time, and 4 ps integral non-linearity, corresponding to 24 and 27 μm spatial resolution on the CDL for the x and the y coordinates, respectively. This approach enables scalable, high-throughput, fully digital, and reconfigurable time-resolved imaging with spatial and temporal resolution comparable to state-of-the-art ASIC-based solutions.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 132Poster Number:NSS-13-132] High-performance preamplifier for spectroscopy systems based on High-Purity Germanium detectors (#1999)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 F. Ojeda (Autores: F. Ojeda , B. Nelson)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] AMETEK ORTEC, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Preamplifiers play a primary role in the resolution, linearity, and sensitivity of ionizing radiation spectrometers, converting the small charges collected by photo detectors into usable voltage signals that are further amplified, digitized, and processed to obtain the intended spectra. Additionally, the accuracy and thermal stability of such charge-to-voltage conversion must be assured to keep a constant performance over time and across different detectors, wiring configurations, and radiation scenarios. This article presents electronic simulations and the first laboratory results showing recent improvements in a new preamplifier designed for High-Purity Germanium spectroscopy systems, in terms of dynamic response, noise, linearity, thermal stability, symmetry, tolerance to reactive loads, piling-up, saturation recovery, and power consumption. The impact of these improvements is also discussed.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 134Poster Number:NSS-13-134] MAPSSIC: Toward a Wireless Implantable Positron Probe for Molecular Neuroimaging of Awake and Freely Moving Rats (#2143)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Dupont (Autores: M. Dupont , S. El katera , F. Agnese , L. Ammour , J. Baudot , S. Bouvard , F. Gensolen , M. Kachel , J. Laurence , P. Pangaud , T. Weicherding , L. Zimmer , P. Lanièce , M.A. Verdier , C. Morel)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Aix-Marseille Univ, CNRS/IN2P3, CPPM, Marseille, France [2] Centre de Radiothérapie St. Louis, Toulon, France [3] Université Paris Cité, CNRS/IN2P3, IJCLab, Orsay, France [4] Université Paris Saclay, CNRS/IN2P3, IJCLab, Orsay, France [5] Université de Strasbourg,, CNRS, IPHC UMR 7178, Strasbourg, France [6] Nantes Université, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France [7] Universitée Lyon 1, CERMEP, CNRS, INSERM, HCL, Lyon, France
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Correlating molecular neuroimaging with behavior in preclinical models requires acquisitions in awake and freely moving animals, whereas most current positron emission tomography procedures are still performed under anesthesia. The MAPSSIC project addresses this limitation with an implantable intracerebral probe based on monolithic active pixel sensors (MAPS) for direct positron detection in targeted brain structures of awake, freely moving rats, thereby avoiding the pharmacological bias of anesthesia. Following sensor characterization and simulation studies previously reported, this contribution presents the transition to a fully wireless system. The acquisition chain combines four IMIC2 sensor chips, a STM32L4 microcontroller, 1 Gbit on-board flash memory, and a bidirectional 2.4 GHz radio link to a Raspberry Pi ground station. The complete software stack is implemented in Rust with the Embassy asynchronous framework, providing memory safety and concurrent peripheral management without dynamic allocation. Planned validation with 18 F, 11 C phantoms, and anesthetized implanted rats will mark the shift from sensor feasibility to system-level wireless validation.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 136Poster Number:NSS-13-136] Single-Shot Precision Decomposition of a 64-Channel FPGA TDC for TOF-PET (#2381)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 G. Sportelli (Autores: G. Sportelli , M. Morrocchi , N. Belcari)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Pisa, Department of Physics "E. Fermi", Pisa, Italy [2] INFN, Sezione di Pisa, Pisa, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We report a channel-level characterization of a calibrated 64-channel FPGA Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) for fast-timing TOF-PET, with explicit decomposition of the single-shot precision (SSP) into quantization and jitter contributions. The TDC is implemented on an Altera Cyclone 10 GX device and operates with a 256-tap, 64-bin tapped-delay-line (TDL) at ~400 MHz, calibrated offline via code-density histograms. Two implementation strategies are compared: the default arithmetic carry-chain inference, and a placement-aware variant in which the TDLs are constrained to regular structures. Across all 64 channels, controlled placement reduces the ultra-bin width from 160 ± 76 ps to 101 ± 12 ps, the equivalent LSB (LSBeq) from 83 ± 32 ps to 63 ± 4 ps, and the quantization noise σ Q from 24.5 ± 7.3 ps rms to 18.1 ± 0.8 ps rms. The placement-constrained implementation also substantially improves channel-to-channel uniformity. The constrained routing increases σ jitter which makes jitter the dominant SSP contribution once σ Q is reduced. A system-level projection onto previously characterized UTOFPET monolithic modules indicates that the TDC accounts for 59% of the measured CRT² in a 12 mm LYSO/256-channel module (CRT ≈ 150 ps FWHM), but only ~8% in 16-20 mm BGO/64-channel modules (CRT ≈ 400 ps FWHM). This identifies σ jitter as the dominant architectural ceiling and motivates wave-union/multi-TDC averaging or finer-node FPGAs for full LYSO exploitation.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 138Poster Number:NSS-13-138] Education kit for radiation measurements (#2477)
sub_talks.speaker: M. Nomachi
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] The University of Osaka, RCNP, Ibaraki/Osaka, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract We have been organizing schools on radiation measurements for students from ASEAN countries. Hands-on experience with radiation measurements is very important, and we prepare radiation measurement systems for practical exercises. To host as many students as possible, we considered organizing the schools in ASEAN countries. However, the shipping cost of the equipment was extremely high. As a result, we could not conduct hands-on exercises on radiation measurement. Driven by recent large-scale experiments, electronics for radiation measurements have become compact, highly integrated, and low-cost. This development now makes it possible to carry equipment to schools. Today, compact detector systems are available at affordable prices, making it much easier to conduct practical radiation measurement exercises in schools. However, modern compact electronics have introduced a new problem: they are too small to probe easily with an oscilloscope. In modern electronics, waveform processing is increasingly performed digitally. Nevertheless, we believe that analogue processing remains important and highly educational for students. This motivated us to develop electronics specifically for educational purposes. We have developed an "education kit" for radiation measurement education. By plugging in a SiPM and a small scintillator crystal module, the board functions as a complete radiation measurement system. An on-board FPGA interfaces with a PC through a USB connection. The board is the size of a Raspberry Pi board. Optionally, it can be plugged onto a Raspberry Pi. Although the board is compact, it provides sufficient space for probing signals. The design of the board will be released as open-source hardware. Students can modify the design and develop their own versions of the board. The "education kit" will serve as an entry point to radiation measurement electronics.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 140Poster Number:NSS-13-140] Preliminary Test Results on Latest Version of FESA Readout ASIC for TOF-PET Detectors (#2565)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Yang (Autores: Y. Yang , Y. Wang , X. Xu , X. Zhang , H. Huang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Science and Technology of China, Department of Modern Physics, Hefei, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The latest version of the low-power 64-channel Front-End readout chip for SiPM Array (FESA4.0) with the preliminary test results is presented in this paper. Using a row-column summing readout method, FESA compresses the 64 input signals into 16 output digital pulses, which then is digitized by the followed field programmable gate array (FPGA). In the pathway of each summing output, there are two threshold current comparators used for signal pickup, one with a low threshold for signal timing and the other with a high threshold for signal validation. Since the signal amplitude is converted into the pulse time-width via the linear discharge method, both the signals timing and amplitude can be measured by the time-to-digital converter (TDC) in the FPGA. The new version of FESA incorporates a time-over-threshold (TOT) measurement capability, which allows to identify the signals originating from different scintillators. The chip offers prominent advantages of simple architecture, low power consumption, and high performance. Through electronics tests, FESA4.0 has a measurement linearity of 99. 1% with a dynamic range of 140. The intrinsic time measurement precision is measured better than 30 ps. Combined with a TOF-PET detector with an 8×8 LYSO crystal coupled to an 8x8 SiPM, the energy resolution and time coincidence resolution are measured as 279 ps and 12.4% respectively. These test results show that FESA4.0 is very promising for the construction of highly integrated TOF-PET scanners.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 142Poster Number:NSS-13-142] SEU Evaluation of an Atom Switch-based FPGA for Slow-Control Systems (#2501)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Ueno (Autores: K. Ueno , N. Taniguchi , T. Sakamoto , M. Miyamura)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] The University of Osaka, Department of Physics, Osaka, Japan [2] KEK, Institute of Particle and Nuclear Studies, Tsukuba, Japan [3] NanoBridge Semiconductor, Inc., Tsukuba, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Atom Switch-based FPGAs (AS-FPGAs) are being developed as next-generation FPGAs with expected high radiation tolerance. Their application to various radiation environments is anticipated, and we are also investigating their potential use in detector electronics for future high-energy physics experiments. In this study, neutron irradiation tests were performed to evaluate the Single Event Upset (SEU) tolerance of digital resources implemented in a 65 nm AS-FPGA. A prototype slow-control board equipped with the AS-FPGA was developed and used for the irradiation test. Two independent block RAM (BRAM) blocks and D-type flip-flop (DFF) blocks were implemented in the FPGA for SEU evaluation, and data mismatches detected during irradiation were counted as SEU events. Neutron irradiation tests were carried out using the tandem accelerator at Kobe University. The neutron fluence reached 1.2 × 10 11 n/cm 2 . No SEUs were observed in the DFF blocks, while approximately 10 SEUs were detected in the BRAM blocks. The preliminary SEU cross section for the BRAMs was estimated to be on the order of 10 −9 cm 2 /Mbit. In parallel with the irradiation studies, stable acquisition of temperature and pressure data from a commercial environmental sensor connected to the prototype slow-control board was successfully demonstrated during neutron irradiation, indicating the applicability of the AS-FPGA to detector slow-control systems in radiation environments.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 144Poster Number:NSS-13-144] Validation and Integration of the COMET Phase-I Trigger System (#2756)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 C. Yamada (Autores: C. Yamada , Y. Fujii , Y. Igarashi , M. Lee , H. Miyai , M. Miyataki , Y. Nakazawa , K. Oishi , S. Ueda , K. Ueno)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] The University of Osaka, physics, Osaka, Japan [2] Imperial College London, physics, London, United Kingdom [3] High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK), Tsukuba, Japan [4] Sungkyunkwan University, physics, Suwon, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The COMET Phase-I experiment at J-PARC searches for muon-to-electron conversion in muonic atoms, which is a charged-lepton-flavor-violating process. The signal electron is monoenergetic, and its momentum is reconstructed using hit information from the Cylindrical Drift Chamber (CDC) and timing information from the Cylindrical Trigger Hodoscope (CTH). The trigger system must provide high event-selection efficiency, be robust against radiation, return trigger decisions within 8.5 μs, and operate stably. To achieve high event-selection efficiency, a multi-stage hardware trigger system was previously developed in which the CDC and CTH trigger candidates are processed in parallel and required to be in coincidence. However, FPGA reconfiguration in the CDC trigger path could change the communication latency, shifting 10 MHz CDC hit frames and degrading the time consistency required for online track finding. This work reports the development and validation of fixed-latency CDC trigger firmware using a setup with one board of each type. Repeated communication-link reset tests show that the latency is fixed with path-to-path variations less than 1 ns. The total latency is 3.5-3.6 μs, satisfying the requirement with sufficient margin, and input-pulse tests demonstrate 100% trigger response efficiency. These results establish a basis for ongoing full-board CDC validation and CDC-CTH trigger-system integration toward Phase-I data-taking.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 146Poster Number:NSS-13-146] Evaluation of a Charge Sharing Compensation with Synchrotron Radiation (#2795)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 P. G. Maj (Autores: P. G. Maj , D. S. Gorni , G. W. Deptuch , D. P. Siddons , A. Rumaiz)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Brookhaven National Laboratory, Instrumentation Department, Upton, New York, United States of America [2] Brookhaven National Laboratory, NSLSII, Upton, New York, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Charge-sharing compensation results obtained with the 3FI ASIC bump-bonded to a pixelated silicon sensor and tested on an NSLS-II synchrotron beamline are presented. The 3FI is a 32×32-pixel readout ASIC fabricated in 65 nm CMOS for Full-Field Fluorescence spectral X-ray Imaging, with 100 μm pixel pitch and event-driven analog output. Building on previously reported functionality and noise performance, this work focuses on the charge-sharing regime. A micrometer-diameter pinhole beam was stepped across pixel boundaries, and event-by-event charge data were recorded at each position. When the beam is directed precisely between two pixels, raw individual-pixel spectra exhibit split-charge events with degraded energy resolution. Offline charge summation of coincident neighboring pixels restores the full photon energy, recovering spectral integrity at the cost of a √2 noise increase. Furthermore, since the shared event is independently sampled by both neighbors, averaging the two reconstructed values cancels the noise penalty entirely, making the detector effectively insensitive to charge sharing across the inter-pixel region. The correction is validated against single-pixel hits recorded away from pixel boundaries, demonstrating full spectral restoration.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 148Poster Number:NSS-13-148] A High-Precision and Wide-Dynamic Range Energy Acquisition Method based on MVT with Pulse-Shape for Elemental Logging (#2841)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 H. Liu (Autores: H. Liu , J. Yu , Q. Xie)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Science and Technology of China, Department of Electronic Engineering and Information Science, Hefei, China [2] Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Department of Biomedical Engineering, Wuhan, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract As unconventional oil and gas exploration extends toward deep and ultra-deep wells, downhole nuclear logging systems are required to operate under high-temperature, high count-rate, and high energy-precision conditions over a wide dynamic range, which are difficult to simultaneously achieve using conventional pulse sampling methods. The multi-voltage threshold (MVT) technique provides inherent advantages under these constraints; however, conventional power-exponential pulse models exhibit limited robustness to waveform variations among detectors of different types and sizes, resulting in degraded pulse reconstruction accuracy and energy linearity. To address this issue, an energy-linearity optimization method is proposed for MVT-based neutron elemental logging instruments. A dedicated front-end signal conditioning and pulse-shaping circuit was developed to regulate the detector pulse shape for improved matching with the power-exponential model, thereby enhancing fitting accuracy. This approach effectively reduces reconstruction error and improves spectral performance across a wide energy range. Experimental results demonstrate that the coefficient of determination (R 2 ) was significantly improved from 0.1380 to 0.9851. The energy resolution was enhanced from 10.5% to 6.2%, closely approaching the oscilloscope-based result of 6.0% with a deviation of only 0.2%. In addition, the proposed method demonstrated good compatibility with detectors of different types and sizes, indicating strong potential for applications in ultra-deep (∼10,000 m) and extreme downhole environments.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 150Poster Number:NSS-13-150] Realistic Detector Response Model for COMET Phase-I Cylindrical Drift Chamber (#2941)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Sun (Autores: S. Sun , M. Aoki , A. Jansen , M. Miyataki , Y. Nakatsugawa , Y. Uchida , K. Ueno , C. Wu , T. Xing , C. Yamada , Y. Yuan , Y. Zhang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] The University of Osaka, Department of Physics, Toyonaka, Japan [2] Dresden University of Technology, Department of Physics, Dresden, Saxony, Germany [3] Wakayama Medical University, School of Medicine, Wakayama, Japan [4] Imperial College London, Department of Physics, London, United Kingdom [5] Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China [6] Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Milan, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The COMET (COherent Muon to Electron Transition) Phase-I experiment at J-PARC searches for coherent muon-to-electron conversion in aluminum with a single-event sensitivity of 3 x 10^-15. A key detector challenge is the high instantaneous beam rate, which produces background hits in the Cylindrical Drift Chamber (CDC). In particular, low-energy protons can generate large ionization signals that drive the readout electronics into nonlinear regions, producing waveform saturation and pileups. These effects may reduce hit efficiency by masking later signal or background hits and therefore must be modeled realistically in performance studies. We developed a detector response model for the CDC that combines Geant4-based ionization with the Photon Absorption Ionization (PAI) model, Garfield++-based drift time calculation, and an electronics response emulation based on measured response functions. The model explicitly includes nonlinear saturation effects in the circuit and was validated using cosmic-ray test data. The measured-response model reproduces the main features of the data more accurately than a simple linear-response model. The remaining discrepancy corresponds to a limited uncertainty in the pileup-effect evaluation, providing a realistic basis for COMET Phase-I reconstruction and performance studies.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 152Poster Number:NSS-13-152] Improving UAV-Based Radiation Monitoring in Mountainous Forests Using ANN with Spectral Information (#1212)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Suzuki (Autores: K. Suzuki , M. Sasaki , A. Miyahara , Y. Morishita , H. Funaki)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Japan Atomic Energy Agency, Collaborative Laboratories for Advanced Decommissioning Science, Fukushima, Japan [2] Hirosaki University, Graduate School of Health Sciences, Aomori, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely used to estimate ambient dose equivalent rates in mountainous forests. However, improving estimation accuracy remains challenging due to complex terrain and forest structure. In this study, an artificial neural network (ANN) model was constructed using UAV measurement data, and its applicability to estimating ambient dose equivalent rates at 1 m above ground level in mountainous forests was evaluated. In addition, the effect of explicitly incorporating direct and scattered radiation components on estimation accuracy was examined. These results show that the proposed ANN-based approach incorporating physically informed spectral information reduces root mean square error by 23% relative to the conventional Flat Source Model in mountainous forests, with explicit separation of radiation components further improving both estimation accuracy and physical interpretability.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 154Poster Number:NSS-13-154] Figure-Grounded Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Radiation Equipment Manual Question-Answering (#1505)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Kim (Autores: M. Kim , J. Kwon , J. Park , S. Lee , B. Park)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, Applied Artificial Intelligence Section, Daejeon, Republic of Korea [2] Korea Institute of Nuclear Safety, Radiation Regulation Division, Daejeon, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Radiation equipment manuals are multimodal documents in which textual content and safety-related visual materials jointly carry critical information. Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods are predominantly text-centric and either fail to reflect visual information or include figures unrelated to the answer. This paper proposes a figure-grounded multimodal RAG pipeline that delivers an answer together with its supporting figures. The proposed method comprises figure-to-section alignment via a document map, hybrid sparse-dense retrieval, and answer generation accompanied by relevant figures. To evaluate multimodal performance, we construct an answer-grounded ground-truth figure set and define Figure Precision@k and Figure Recall@k as evaluation metrics. On a benchmark of ten radiation-equipment manuals (800 questions), the proposed method improves Figure Precision@5 from 0.06 to 0.30 and Figure Recall@5 from 0.15 to 0.61 over an image-embedding baseline, with textual answer quality comparable to a long-context text-RAG baseline in BERTScore-F1 and slightly lower in ROUGE-L.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 156Poster Number:NSS-13-156] Physics Enhanced Machine Learning for Thermoluminescence Glow Curve Deconvolution (#1623)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Tomaszewski (Autores: L. Tomaszewski , C. Shenton-Taylor)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Surrey, Department of Physics, Guildford, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Thermoluminescence dosimetry (TLD) relies on accurate glow curve deconvolution to characterise trapping parameters, yet conventional methods are computationally intensive and rely on expert-defined initial parameters. This study explores a machine learning (ML) framework to automate glow curve analysis while preserving interpretability and decreasing user input. A hybrid CNN-GRU model was developed and trained on 658 experimental glow curves from silica glass beads and 10,000 synthetic mathematical glow curves derived from kinetic order equations. The model demonstrates the ability to reconstruct glow curves and infer peak structures without explicit user-defined initialisation, achieving an average figure of merit (FOM) of 8.3% on unseen experimental data. Notably, the ML approach consistently identifies the primary glow peak at the same temperature positions as conventional deconvolution methods, indicating that prominent physical features are reliably captured. Although traditional deconvolution techniques yield lower FOM values (~1%), they require optimisation and expert guidance. However, the ML model provides rapid, repeatable predictions and scales efficiently to large datasets. The results suggest that ML is not a replacement for conventional approaches but a complementary tool, in which ML predicts the initial parameters rather than a user. This work highlights the potential for hybrid ML-physics strategies to advance TL analysis. UK Ministry of Defence © Crown Owned Copyright 2026/AWE

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 158Poster Number:NSS-13-158] A High-Fidelity Robotics Simulation Framework for Autonomous Radiation Source Search (#2144)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. M. Drouet (Autores: L. M. Drouet , K. Knecht , J. Sparger , M. Willis , P. Sobel , N. Prins , J. Karcz)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Tennessee, Department of Nuclear Engineering, Knoxville, Tennessee, United States of America [2] Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Radiological source search requires timely threat assessment to ensure the security of the public. Existing methods rely on personnel to conduct radiation surveys with mobile detector systems, potentially exposing them to hazardous environments. Recent advancements in physical AI have presented the opportunity to improve radiological source search with robotics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Prior work at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) has developed a radiation search platform that equips the Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped with a radiation imager, LiDAR, IMU, camera, and onboard computer for real-time 3D radiation imaging during autonomous navigation of complex environments. However, the development and field testing of autonomous robotic platforms are resource intensive and operationally constrained, motivating a simulation framework to refine autonomy algorithms and evaluate search performance across complex environments that would otherwise be infeasible to access. Building on the physical system, this work presents a high-fidelity simulation framework for developing and testing autonomous radiation search workflows in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. The framework centers on a model of the Spot quadruped equipped with simulated contextual sensors, including 3D LiDAR, RGB, and depth cameras, and exposes velocity-command control through a ROS 2 bridge. The current implementation provides end-to-end integration of sensor streaming, command interfaces, and a Python-based autonomy pipeline. Preliminary mapping outputs are presented as qualitative system-integration results and sandbox visualizations to support future autonomy and radiation-modeling studies.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 160Poster Number:NSS-13-160] Robust Dual-Target Radioisotope Quantification Under Increasing Unseen Contaminant Complexity (#2217)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Kim (Autores: C. Kim , Y. Kim , G. Kim , D.Y. Oh)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic of Korea [2] Korea University, Department of Bioengineering, Seoul, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Gamma-ray spectroscopy is a fundamental technique for radioisotope identification and quantification across safety-critical applications, where deep learning models have recently emerged as a data-driven alternative to traditional library-dependent methods. However, most existing deep learning approaches operate under a closed-set assumption that all isotopes during deployment are present in the training set; field deployments frequently violate this assumption, and the introduction of unknown isotopes leads to silent degradation. Recent OOD-detection studies have been reported, but they treat OOD spectra as anomalies to be flagged rather than quantified, and systematic evaluation under increasing unseen contaminant complexity remains lacking. This study proposes a denoising autoencoder (DAE) framework that reconstructs the clean target spectrum (¹³⁷Cs, ¹³³Ba) from contaminated measurements while simultaneously estimating target fractions through a dual-head architecture. Using Ce:GPS scintillator pulse data under a leave-one-out unknown noise (LOO-UN) protocol, the DAE achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.024 at 20% out-of-distribution (OOD) contamination in the two-unseen configuration, outperforming NNLS-known (0.038) and MLP (0.031), with near-constant accuracy as the unseen contaminant count increased from one to two (0.025 → 0.024).

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 162Poster Number:NSS-13-162] Recoil electron tracking in 3D CZT drift strip detectors: a feasibility study (#2296)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Kossakowski (Autores: M. Kossakowski , A. Valverde Mahou , S. Hauberg , I. Kuvvetli)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Technical University of Denmark, Space Research and Technology, Lyngby, Denmark [2] Technical University of Denmark, Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, Lyngby, Denmark
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Bridging the MeV gap remains difficult due to the interplay of competing photon interaction processes, leaving a persistent sensitivity gap in gamma-ray astronomy. Compton telescopes based on 3D CZT Drift Strip Detectors (DSD) are promising candidates for bridging this gap, offering room-temperature operation, high stopping power, excellent energy and position resolution. A key open question is whether recoil electron tracking, which significantly improves angular resolution and detector sensitivity is achievable from raw detector signals. We investigate this using a machine learning approach trained on forward simulations of the 3D CZT DSD response. Principal Component Analysis of simulated electron tracks confirms that track structure is encodable in a low-dimensional representation, and neural network training to regress the recoil direction directly from detector waveforms is ongoing.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 164Poster Number:NSS-13-164] Enhanced Spent Nuclear Fuel Characterization Using Sequential Detector Responses through Deep Learning (#2393)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 B. Kwon (Autores: B. Kwon , W. Hong , J. Kim , G. Kim)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Seoul National University, Nuclear Engineering, seoul, Republic of Korea [2] Seoul National University, Energy Systems Engineering, seoul, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of spent nuclear fuel (SNF) is essential for verifying operator-declared information in nuclear safeguards. Conventional nondestructive assay (NDA) approaches for such characterization based on gamma-ray spectroscopy typically rely on extracting specific photopeak information (ex. 662 keV peak of ¹³⁷Cs), which compresses high-dimensional detector responses into a limited number of variables and may lead to information loss. To address this limitation, we propose a deep learning-based SNF characterization approach that directly utilizes sequential detector-response data for advanced characterization performance. The training dataset was generated through integrated ORIGEN and MCNP simulations for 5000 realistic SNF conditions, covering variations in initial enrichment, burnup, and cooling time. The proposed C2C-GRU-v2 architecture was designed to process long sequential detector-response data by combining Coordinate-to-Context embedding and GRU-based recurrent sequence modeling, enabling both event-level contextual learning and sequence-level generalization. For comparison, a conventional spectrum-based regression method using ¹³⁷Cs peak counts was also implemented under identical conditions. The proposed approach demonstrated improved characterization performance compared with the conventional method, particularly for cooling time estimation, achieving Relative Root Mean Square Errors (RRMSE) of 0.157 for burnup and 0.0456 for cooling time prediction. These results demonstrate the feasibility of deep learning-based sequential detector-response analysis for advanced SNF characterization in nuclear safeguards applications.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 166Poster Number:NSS-13-166] Development of a PINN-Based Defect Verification Algorithm for CANDU Spent Nuclear Fuel Bundles (#2403)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Kang (Autores: J. Kang , Y.S. Chung , J. Ra , J.J. Ahn , Y.H. Chung)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Yonsei University, Department of Radiation Convergence Engineering, Wonju-si, Republic of Korea [2] Yonsei University, Division of Data Science, Wonju-si, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The 37-element CANDU (CANadian Deuterium Uranium) spent fuel bundles at the Wolsong heavy water reactor are stored vertically in 19 layers within a wet storage facility. The Improved Optical fiber-based VErification System (IOVES), comprising a scintillator, optical fiber, and photomultiplier tube, traverses vertically between bundles to measure radiation profiles. Operators manually count profile peaks to verify bundle integrity, but reliability degrades when peaks are indistinct. This study presents a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN)-based algorithm for automated defect verification of spent fuel bundles. The model learns physical characteristics of radiation profiles to generate predicted profiles, which are compared against measured profiles to localize defective bundles. A three-head output structure independently predicts the defect status per layer, the number of defective bundles per layer, and the left/right defect probability. The total loss, comprising the three head-specific losses and a mean squared error profile of prediction loss, was optimized using the Adam optimizer. The dataset comprised three scenarios (0, 1, and 2 defective bundles), with 200,000 samples each, totaling 600,000 samples, split 70%, 15%, and 15% for training, validation, and testing. Defect classification accuracy per layer reached 99.7%. 19-layer exact match accuracy was 97.2%, with 100% accuracy on defect-free arrays. This work demonstrates the feasibility of an automated verification system that overcomes operator-dependent inspection limitations. Future work will target improved left/right defect localization accuracy.

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This work introduces a neuromorphic in-pixel processing concept for next-generation high-flux radiation detectors. By leveraging event-driven principles inspired by Spiking Neural Networks, the proposed approach aims to move part of the signal interpretation directly into the pixel matrix, rather than relying solely on external readout and post-processing. This enables local extraction of photon timing, energy-related features, and mitigation of pile-up effects under extreme photon flux conditions. The concept builds on recent developments in hybrid pixel detectors and emerging intelligent in-pixel architectures, and extends them towards fully event driven detector operation. The proposed paradigm may open new directions for adaptive, low-latency radiation imaging at future synchrotron and XFEL facilities.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 170Poster Number:NSS-13-170] CVAE-Based Synthetic Thermoluminescence Silica Glass Jewellery Bead Glow Curve Generation (#2606)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Tomaszewski (Autores: L. Tomaszewski , C. Shenton-Taylor)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Surrey, Department of Physics, Guildford, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Micro silica glass jewellery beads have emerged as a viable material for thermoluminescence dosimetry (TLD), offering a low-cost and widely accessible option for personal dose assessment. Their linear glow curve responses, governed by irradiation, thermal conditions, and sample characteristics, exhibit unique spectral elements and structure variability. While machine learning (ML) methods have been successfully applied to dose estimation and irradiation analysis, can ML be used to elevate silica glass beads beyond just decorative jewellery? In this work, a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) is implemented to model and generate thermoluminescent glow curves from silica glass beads conditioned on experimental parameters. The model is trained on a dataset of experimentally acquired responses, augmented with Poisson noise to increase the dataset size and robustness. Conditioning variables include temperature profiles, irradiation and sample characteristics, enabling the model to learn relationships between physical conditions and the glow curve. Results show that the CVAE model can generate realistic glow curves that reflect the underlying conditioning variables. Generated predications maintain peak structure and overall shape, while also reproducing the expected linear relationship between total counts and absorbed dose. Model performance remains consistent when evaluated on previously unseen testing data with a mean figure of merit of 7.5%, although accuracy declines at low dose levels due to diminished signal intensity. The proposed approach demonstrates the potential of generative ML techniques for supporting dosimetry simulation, calibration, and data augmentation workflows for future research. sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 172Poster Number:NSS-13-172] Gamma-Ray Image Denoising and Source Enhancement Based on a Residual Convolutional Autoencoder (#2662)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Park (Autores: J. Park , Y. Park , I. Choi , H. Lee , K. Lee)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea University, Department of Bioengineering, Seoul, Republic of Korea [2] Korea University, Interdisciplinary program in precision public health, Seoul, Republic of Korea [3] ARALE Laboratory, Co., Ltd, Seoul, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract In radiation-guided cancer surgery, the amount of radioactive isotopes administered is limited, resulting in the acquisition of low-count, low-resolution gamma images that are further degraded by scattered radiation. In this study, a Residual Convolutional Autoencoder (Residual CAE) was developed to suppress background noise and enhance source-related signals in low-count gamma-ray images. The input images were zero-padded to and normalized by the image-wise maximum value. The Residual CAE was configured as an encoder-decoder network with a residual connection that adds the first shallow feature map to the final decoder feature map, thereby preserving source location and spatial details. In test results, the Residual CAE achieved an MSE of 0.0007, SSIM of 0.9682, peak bias of 0.2416 pixels, and FWHM of 0.0441 pixels. To enable direct deployment of the trained model on the gamma camera and the monitoring software the model was converted to the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) format, allowing its inference performance to be evaluated in an embedded environment. The entire deployment pipeline, including preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing, was implemented. The converted ONNX model produced outputs that were highly consistent with the trained model and demonstrated low-latency inference suitable for real-time gamma-ray image processing. After conversion to ONNX, the model maintained reliable inference performance, achieving a mean peak bias of 1.35 pixels, a minimum ∆ FWHM of −0.711 pixels, and 95.73% overall classification accuracy. These results demonstrate that the Residual CAE is effective for gamma-ray image denoising and source enhancement while preserving source localization and spatial resolution, supporting its feasibility for real-time deployment.

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a neural-network surrogate model for predicting Total Ionizing Dose (TID) induced degradation in a 180 nm bulk CMOS NMOS transistor. The proposed model uses only the gate length L, gate width W, W/L, total dose, and log(1+dose) as input features, where the layout parameters are extractable from a PDK netlist. The model predicts the dose-dependent changes in V th , I on , I off , g m , and SS. Using 180 nm NMOS data generated by a 3D drift-diffusion TCAD framework, the model is evaluated under three holdout conditions: 15 kGy(SiO 2 ) interpolation, 50 kGy(SiO 2 ) extrapolation, and a held-out geometry (L, W)=(240nm, 750nm). With 3-fold cross-validation along the dose axis and five random-seed repetitions, the worst-case absolute relative errors of V th , I on , g m , and SS are below 0.30% in the INTERP/EXTRAP conditions, while those of I off are 0.99-1.45% and 2.16-2.52%, respectively. In the held-out geometry condition, the worst-case errors of all five metrics remain within 2%, indicating that TCAD-level TID degradation trends can be approximated using layout and total dose variables.

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper describes a deep learning algorithm for the estimation of axial, transverse, and depth of interaction (DOI) positions of detected events in SPECT. The algorithm includes a method for automatic calibration of the gain factor mismatches between detectors. The training data is obtained by simulation. The model consists of three feed-forward networks, one for each parameter to estimate. The axial is a continuous estimate, while transverse and DOI and discrete. The axial estimate is passed as an additional parameter to the DOI estimate, which improves estimates near the detector edge. A single base model is trained with data from a reference detector that is taken to have perfect gains, then calibration learns factors relative to this detector. Log-gains are learned to smoothly enforce strict positivity, from which the gains can be easily recovered. The algorithm achieves an axial FWHM of 1.40 mm, transverse FWHM of 0.83 mm, and a DOI FWHM of 1.24 mm. The gain factor estimates, based on histogram data, are within 0.001%.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 178Poster Number:NSS-13-178] Deep learning for precise gamma-ray interaction in an hexagonal monolithic scintillation crystals for PET imaging (#2968)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Jiménez Algarra (Autores: L. Jiménez Algarra , D. Pérez-Benito , D. Izquierdo García , J. J. Vaquero López)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Universidad Carlos III, Departamento de Bioingeniería, Leganés, Spain [2] Instituto de Investigación Sanitaria Gregorio Marañón, Madrid, Spain
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The estimation of scintillation positioning with a high degree of precision in PET detectors is a crucial factor in determining the spatial resolution of the final image. Nevertheless, intra-crystal Compton scatter, optical diffusion, edge effects, and DOI ambiguity collectively limit the accuracy of first-interaction localization. Consequently, reducing this uncertainty will have a significant impact on the LOR definition and, in turn, will enhance the quality of the final PET image. Machine learning and deep learning methodologies have been shown to be particularly effective in this domain, resolving non-linear relationships between data and often outperforming other traditional approaches. In this study, we investigate various pipelines and deep learning techniques for enhancing gamma-positioning precision through the utilization of validated Monte Carlo simulations in a monolithic PET crystal with a specific hexagonal-shaped scintillation crystal. The validation of the selected models was done using experimental data specifically acquired for this study. The findings suggest that the most effective approach involves the utilization of a net trained with photoelectric and scatter events. The final FWHM mean in the corner and center are 1.2 mm and 1.7 mm for the simulated data respectively, while 1.74 and 2.63 mm, respectively for the validation. The bias achieved was 0.25 mm in the Z direction for the simulation.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 180Poster Number:NSS-13-180] Characterizing Neutron Detection Efficiency in Timepix3: A Bayesian-Optimized FLUKA Approach (#3239)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Mukhopadhyay (Autores: A. Mercado , S. Mukhopadhyay , M. West , P. Connolly , S. Dewji)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, Georgia, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Characterization of converter layer geometry is critical for determining the absolute detection efficiency of pixelated thermal neutron detectors. However, uncertainties in film deposition and source strength often lead to significant discrepancies between simulated models and actual experimental performance. This work addresses these challenges by implementing a Bayesian optimized FLUKA framework to determine the effective enriched Lithium-6 Fluoride converter thickness for an ADVACAM Timepix3 detector with a 1000 μm Silicon sensor. The FLUKA Monte Carlo model was benchmarked against experimental measurements using an Americium-Beryllium source with a nominal activity of 40 mCi and a documented tolerance of fifteen percent. The Bayesian optimizer successfully converged to an effective thickness of 5 μm after forty evaluations by minimizing the residuals between the nominal source activity and the simulation-implied activities. This methodology demonstrates a robust approach to resolving geometric uncertainties in hybrid semiconductor detectors where direct physical measurement of internal components is not feasible post-assembly. The resulting validated geometry provides a high-fidelity foundation for modeling future detection efficiency benchmarks across diverse neutron spectra. This work demonstrates a practical approach for integrating machine-learning optimization with Monte Carlo transport modeling to address geometric uncertainties in neutron detectors.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 182Poster Number:NSS-13-182] Background pattern recognition and its reconstruction during radiation shadowing by scanned vehicles in Radiation Portal Monitors. (#1109)
sub_talks.speaker: V. Kondrashov
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] GalaxRay LLC, radiation detectors, Mississauga, Ontario, Canada
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The author has presented the approach to ambient radiation background pattern recognition and reconstruction for plastic scintillator-based Radiation Portal Monitors during vehicle scanning in situations when the ambient background is depressed (shadowed) by a vehicle. The principle is based on a correlation-significance test derived from the paired Student's t-tests and Pearson correlation coefficients. The author establishes criteria to recognize background depression and radiation source presence in the occupancy spectrum. After determining the scale of depression for defined energy windows, the given approach presents the formalism to reconstruct the depressed background during the scan which is based on Aluminum variable thickness sheet as a vehicle equivalent model and the method for evaluating the signal-to-noise ratio to detect the radiation source under such scan conditions.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 184Poster Number:NSS-13-184] Effect of Source Intensity Imbalance on Two-Point Angular Resolution in Coded-Aperture Imaging (#1160)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Qiu (Autores: Y. Qiu , T. Dai , Q. Wei)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Science and Technology Beijing, School of Automation and Electrical Engineering, Beijing, China [2] China-Japan Friendship Hospital, Department of Radiation Oncology, Beijing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Far-field angular resolution of coded-aperture gamma-ray imagers is often assessed by the smallest angular separation at which two point sources can still be distinguished, but the effect of unequal source activities on such measurements remains unclear. In this work, Monte Carlo simulations were performed to quantify how source-count imbalance influences two-point-source resolution tests in coded-aperture imaging. Images were reconstructed using the maximum-likelihood expectation-maximization algorithm, and reconstruction quality was evaluated using the valley-to-weak-peak ratio and localization bias. An appropriate stopping point was determined by jointly examining both metrics. Under ideal noise-free conditions, increasing source-count imbalance progressively degraded two-source discrimination. When the valid-count mismatch did not exceed 20%, acceptable discrimination was maintained near the nominal angular resolution limit, whereas larger mismatches caused a marked increase in localization bias. These results indicate that source-count imbalance can bias two-point-source resolution measurements and should be controlled in practical evaluations of coded-aperture systems.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 186Poster Number:NSS-13-186] X-Ray Measurement of Tubes Using Closed-Loop Residual-Driven Optimization Algorithm (#1269)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Sun (Autores: Y. Sun , T. Zeng , L. Wang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Tsinghua university, Bejing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The geometric cross-sectional parameters of circular tubes, such as cables and rubber hoses, including inner and outer diameters, wall thickness, and eccentricity, are key indicators of manufacturing quality. However, existing X-ray digital imaging-based inspection methods generally rely on locating edge transition points (ETPs) in attenuation profiles, which degrades the accuracy and reliability of parameter reconstruction. To address these limitations, this paper develops a closed-loop residual-driven optimization (CRO) algorithm. The residual at ETPs between the measured projection and the analytical projection of the parameterized contour model is used as the feedback signal, and the contour parameters are corrected through a sign-driven update rule. Monte Carlo (MC) simulation data as the measured data demonstrates that, for a detector pixel size of 0.04mm, introducing CRO reduces the MAE of contour parameters by 69.44%, with a maximum error of 0.03mm.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 188Poster Number:NSS-13-188] Verification of a Rapid Dose Assessment Program Against MCNP for Nuclear Power Plant Decommissioning (#1310)
sub_talks.speaker: C. Yoon
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea Hydro & Nuclear CO., LTD, Central Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of radiation exposure for workers during nuclear facility decommissioning is important for radiation protection and work planning. To support this, a previously developed dose assessment program based on the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) algorithm was verified in this study. The program inversely estimates source activity from known source positions and measured dose rates at selected locations, and then calculates worker exposure based on the estimated activity. To verify the performance of the program, its results were compared with those from MCNP, a widely used Monte Carlo radiation transport code. Three representative scenarios were considered: (1) multiple workers and multiple sources, (2) presence of thick shielding, and (3) changes in shielding and source location. For each scenario, dose rates were first calculated using MCNP and used as reference values, and the developed program predicted doses under the same conditions. In addition, the Average Fractional Error (AFE) was evaluated by comparing the measured dose rates with the dose rates recalculated at the same points using the estimated source activity. The results show that the prediction error is within 10% for most cases, while the shielding scenario shows a higher deviation, with a maximum error of 18.2%. The AFE results also support this trend, with a maximum value of 34% for the shielding case and less than 6% for the other scenarios, which are within the acceptable range based on the EPRI algorithm criterion. These results indicate that the program provides reliable results overall, while some deviation appears under strong shielding conditions. Since decommissioning environments change frequently, repeated MCNP simulations can be time-consuming. The developed program provides results within a few seconds, allowing quick estimation of worker dose under changing conditions and supporting practical work planning.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 190Poster Number:NSS-13-190] High-Reliability Tritium Monitoring Using Hardware Alpha Suppression and AI-Based Smoothing Filter (#1370)
sub_talks.speaker: S. Lee
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, Department of Radiation Safety Control, Daejeon, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Tritium monitoring in research reactors is essential for radiation safety because tritium is released as a low-energy beta emitter and is therefore difficult to measure accurately in real time. In particular, the reliability of tritium measurements can be degraded by two major factors: unavoidable statistical fluctuations in the ion chamber output and transient interference caused by radon and its alpha-emitting progeny. Radon-induced alpha events generate large ionization signals in the ion chamber, producing spike-like transients that can distort the measured current, while statistical fluctuations reduce the stability and precision of the monitoring data. To address these limitations, this study proposes a tritium monitoring system that combines a hardware-based alpha suppression function with an AI-based smoothing filter. The proposed monitor consists of two ion chambers, a pump, and a membrane separator, enabling gamma compensation and the exclusion of beta-emitting noble gases. The alpha suppression circuit detects and removes alpha-induced transients before they affect the measurement output. In addition, a piecewise learning-based smoothing filter is applied to reduce statistical fluctuations while preserving the response to actual changes in tritium concentration. The filter employs a two-stage framework consisting of change point detection and local regression, and is implemented using ONNX Runtime in a C#-based real-time monitoring system. Experimental results show that the proposed approach improves both measurement stability and responsiveness, demonstrating its applicability to reliable tritium monitoring in research reactor stack environments.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 192Poster Number:NSS-13-192] Automated Monte Carlo-Based Efficiency Transfer Integrated into HPGe Gamma Spectroscopy Workflows for High-Throughput Laboratories (#1579)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Behling (Autores: S. Behling , F. Diel , M. Breidenbach)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Ametek, Ortec, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, United States of America [2] AMETEK GmbH, Meerbusch, Duesseldorf, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany [3] AMETEK GmbH, InnoRIID, Duesseldorf, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract High-purity germanium (HPGe) detector systems are widely used for gamma spectroscopy; however, increasing throughput demands, expanding measurement configurations, and a declining base of expert users have made traditional efficiency calibration and transfer workflows increasingly impractical. Efficiency transfer between counting geometries has historically required manual configuration, custom made sources, and/or execution of Monte Carlo simulations by trained computational physicists, limiting scalability in routine laboratory environments. We present an approach that embeds Monte Carlo-based efficiency transfer directly within a commercial spectral analysis software stack, enabling automated operation without additional user intervention. At runtime, sample geometries-already specified by laboratory personnel using standard container templates such as Marinelli beakers-are used to drive a ray-tracing-based gamma transport simulation coupled to detector interaction and pulse-processing models. The approach operates over an energy range of 20 keV to 2.5 MeV and produces both full spectra and efficiency curves. Validation is performed through comparison of simulated spectra and efficiency curves against measured data and results from the Geant4 Monte Carlo toolkit. While not intended to match the full generality of Geant4, the proposed approach demonstrates comparable practical accuracy for routine laboratory configurations while significantly reducing user complexity. Additionally, seamless integration into existing workflows is demonstrated, enabling non-expert users to apply physics-based efficiency transfer without specialized training. This work provides a scalable solution for automated, high-throughput gamma spectroscopy, bridging the gap between rigorous Monte Carlo modeling and practical laboratory usability.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 196Poster Number:NSS-13-196] Quantitative Neutron Emission Tomography of Plutonium-Bearing Materials using a Boron-Coated Straw Detector Array (#2009)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 D. Breitenmoser (Autores: D. Breitenmoser , M. Fang , D. Chichester , S. Thompson , S. Clarke , A. Di Fulvio , S. Pozzi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Michigan, Department of Nuclear Engineering and Radiological Sciences, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States of America [2] University of Illinois, Department of Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering, Urbana-Champaign, Illinois, United States of America [3] Idaho National Laboratory, Radiochemistry and Nuclear Measurements Department, Idaho Falls, Idaho, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Neutron-based non-destructive assay (NDA) is a cornerstone of nuclear safeguards. Yet conventional techniques relying on integral counting suffer from significant biases if the spatial distribution and emission strength of neutron sources are unknown. This work presents a new, quantitative neutron emission tomography framework using a custom boron-coated straw detector array, enabling simultaneous localization and emission rate estimation of plutonium-bearing materials. Using high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and a custom iterative support-refined non-negative least squares algorithm, we demonstrate that centimeter-scale spatial resolution and percent-level accuracy in emission rate reconstruction can be achieved for realistic counting statistics. These results highlight the potential of neutron emission tomography as a next-generation NDA technique for advanced nuclear fuel cycles and reprocessing technologies.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 198Poster Number:NSS-13-198] Caesium 137 Radiation Transport Profile Modelling for Application to Physical and Simulation Environments (#2147)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 E. Leo (Autores: E. Leo , K. A.A. Gamage , O. R. Popoola)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Glasgow, James Watts School of Engineering, Glasgow, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Towards the assembly of a virtual component of a radiological monitoring digital twin, an analysis of Caesium 137's mixed field radiation transport is presented. Caesium 137 decays by both beta and gamma radiation which can allow for long range detection of radioactive leakage events. First, a preliminary screening of the source-to-sensor distances of electrons in air was undertaken using the NIST ESTAR dataset. Following this, a Geant4 study was developed to investigate the profile of Caesium 137 activity with respect to distance from a source and threshold variation. This study confirmed that detection efficiency diminished with increased sensor thresholds and confirmed that the change in activity with respect to distance closely follows Poisson statistics. This sets the ground for creating engineering surrogate models that could be employed for application to the radiation field models and the creation of a physical simulation for radiation. The work carried out enables the application of digital twin methodologies to facilitate semi-autonomous radiological monitoring in Nuclear Power Plant environments.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 200Poster Number:NSS-13-200] Bayesian Filtering Image Reconstruction for SourceLocalization and Tracking in Compton Imaging (#2167)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Leland (Autores: J. Leland , C. Tarpau , M. Fang , Y. Altmann , A. Di Fulvio)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Nuclear, Plasma, and Radiological Engineering, Urbana, Illinois, United States of America [2] University of Edinburgh, Maxwell Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Bayes Center, Edinburgh, United Kingdom [3] Heriot-Watt University, School of Engineering and Physical Sciences, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Stand-off detection of special nuclear materials (SNM) in safeguards and non-proliferation applications demands imaging systems capable of tracking sources across dynamic environments. In this work, we introduce a Bayesian-Filtering (BF) algorithm for simultaneous source localization and tracking where existing reconstruction methods, such as simple back-projection (SBP) and maximum likelihood expectation maximization (MLEM), are insufficient. We evaluate the BF algorithm using synthetic data generated with MCNPX-PoliMi for a simulated Compton imager consisting of a 4 x 7 array of LYSO scintillator crystals. Two independent sources are simulated, one sweeping in azimuth and one in elevation, each traveling from -90° to +90° at 1 m/s. The BF algorithm successfully tracked both sources across the full angular sweep, achieving mean angular errors of 6.4° and 6.03° for the azimuth and elevation cases, respectively. Additionally, preliminary results for multi-source tracking are successful with the algorithm tracking both sources up until their paths intersect which is a known challenge we are currently investigating.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 202Poster Number:NSS-13-202] An Iterative Based Gain Calibration Method for Multi-Channel Readout Scintillation Detectors (#2248)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Z. Yan (Autores: Z. Yan , Y. Zhao , Q. Wei)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Engineering Research Center of Industrial Spectrum Imaging and School of Automation and Electrical Engineering, Beijing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract To address the common issue of channel gain non-uniformity in multi-channel readout scintillation detectors, this paper proposes an iterative correction method based on raw event data.The proposed method requires no additional hardware support and directly calibrates the gain coefficients of each channel directly using event data acquired by the detector. Channel energy data are extracted for each event, and the total energy is computed to locate the photopeak position.An energy selection window is then applied to retain valid events, thereby suppressing the influence of scattered and noise events. On this basis, an iterative optimization process is employed to refine the gain coefficients of each channel, gradually converging the event energy distribution toward the photopeak. The correction effect is assessed by the energy resolution derived from the resulting energy spectrum. Experimental results show that the proposed method effectively compensates for channel response inconsistencies, significantly improves detector performance including energy resolution, and consequently enhances imaging quality and accuracy. The method is simple to implement and highly practical, and can be directly integrated into the data processing pipeline of existing detection systems.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Priyadarshi (Autores: A. Priyadarshi , A. K. Gourishetty , K. Madhan , V. Ranga)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the development of a compact Geant4-Python simulation-analysis tool for a reproducible gamma response scintillation detector. The tool couples a configurable Geant4 C++ backend with Python automation for macro generation, simulation execution, ROOT-file validation, deposited-energy spectrum generation, count extraction and summarisation in a table. Unlike a general-purpose detector framework, the present implementation is focused on the end-to-end workflow required for scintillation detector response studies using solid cylindrical, hollow cylindrical, and near-4π soccerball-style geometries. Simulations with Cs-137 for 10 8 events demonstrate the complete workflow, while higher-statistics validation runs on PARAMGanga (Super-Computer at IITR) indicate that the same structure can be extended to larger detector-response campaigns. The resulting tool reduces manual intervention, improves traceability, and provides a reusable starting point for systematic Geant4-based gamma-spectroscopy simulations.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 206Poster Number:NSS-13-206] Development and deployment of a compact beta/gamma spectrometry chain for autonomous ground vehicles in nuclear decommissioning (#2624)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 P.-L. Antonsanti (Autores: P.-L. Antonsanti , J. Venara , M. Cuozzo , T. Durand , J. Seyssaud , M. Pacini , E. Cantrel)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Université de Montpellier / CEA, DES/ISEC/DPME/SEIP/LNPA, Bagnols-sur-Cèze, France [2] Université de Montpellier / CEA, DES/ISEC/DPME, Bagnols-sur-Cèze, France [3] Sigma Ingegneria, Lucca, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The XS ABILITY project aims to deploy a swarm of autonomous unmanned ground/aerial vehicles equipped with advanced radiation detection technologies for Dismantling & Decommissioning operations. As part of this effort, we developed a compact beta/gamma spectrometry chain to monitor concrete surfaces potentially contaminated with ¹³⁷Cs or ⁹⁰Sr, the main fission products encountered in nuclear facilities. The detection system comprises a 4-mm-thick plastic scintillator coupled to a photomultiplier tube, optimized for ⁹⁰Sr/⁹⁰Y full beta energy deposition. Analog signal processing is performed using a wireless, portable multichannel analyzer (CAEN Gammastream), adapted to both payload constraints and real-time measurements. It is currently being integrated into the Sigma Rover for automated floor/wall measurements. Energy calibration and resolution were estimated in laboratory using standard sources (¹³⁷Cs, ²⁰⁷Bi, ²⁴¹Am), complemented by an uncertainty analysis addressing calibration parameters, measurement geometry, and background noise. A Monte Carlo model of the spectrometer was developed and validated against experimental data, facilitating simulations of configurations infeasible in laboratory settings. One of the target test cases of XS Ability being the CEA Marcoule G2 reactor currently undergoing dismantlement, a campaign of automated background noise measurements in the building is scheduled. The analysis of the spatial variability of the signal and the accessibility of the facility are key steps in the development of robust and automated scans. The measures will complement the uncertainty analysis, thus improving the contamination detection and reducing the false alarm and false negative rates. Ongoing work focuses on developing machine-learning-based algorithms for source identification (¹³⁷Cs, ⁹⁰Sr) and localization, targeting both surface and subsurface contamination.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 208Poster Number:NSS-13-208] Neutron and secondary photon dose mapping of deuterium-deuterium (D-D) and deuterium-tritium (D-T) neutron generators via PHITS simulations (#2970)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. G. Alipio (Autores: A. G. Alipio , C. L. Dulohan , B. Egwolf , A. Asuncion-Astronomo)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The Monte Carlo-based Particle Heavy Ion Transport Code System (PHITS) was used to model deuterium-deuterium (D-D) and deuterium-tritium (D-T) neutron generators for preliminary radiation safety assessment of the ongoing establishment of the Neutron Irradiation Facility (NIF) of the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (PNRI). Neutron and secondary photon dose distributions were obtained for fully shielded, partially shielded, and unshielded configurations. In both D-D and D-T cases, the counting room dose rates were acceptable with respect to occupational dose limits for a 500-hour annual operating time. However, additional shielding should be explored for the D-T setup to further reduce dose rates in the work area. The dose maps presented the significance of the configuration of moderating and shielding materials in minimizing radiological doses during operation. The findings of this work will serve as a reference for the safe and reliable installation of the country's first neutron generator laboratory.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 210Poster Number:NSS-13-210] Count-Level Effects on Radiomics Robustness and Harmonization in Total-Body PET Imaging (#3090)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. S. Azimi (Autores: M. S. Azimi , M. Cheraghi , H. Zaidi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Geneva University Hospital, Division of Nuclear Medicine & Molecular Imaging, Geneva, Genève, Switzerland [2] Obuda University, University Research and Innovation Cente, Budapest, Hungary [3] Shahid Beheshti University, Department of Nuclear Medicin, Tehran, Iran (Islamic Republic of)
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Radiomics analysis in total-body PET imaging is highly sensitive to acquisition variability, particularly count reduction, which directly affects noise characteristics and feature reliability. In this study, we investigate the impact of count reduction and multi-parametric harmonization on the robustness of multi-organ radiomics. A retrospective dataset of 550 patients from two centers was analyzed. Multiple count levels were generated from list-mode data, including standard and reduced counts (reduction factors up to 100). Multi-organ segmentation was performed automatically, and 107 IBSI-compliant radiomics features were extracted from SUV-normalized images. Feature harmonization was applied using ComBat under different configurations, including scanner, voxel size, radiopharmaceutical, and scatter correction. Reproducibility was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients across count levels and anatomical regions. Results show that radiomics stability is strongly dependent on both count level and feature type. Approximately 31% of features achieved good reproducibility (ICC ≥ 0.75) in at least one organ. Shape and first-order features remained relatively stable under moderate count reduction (CRF ≤ 20), while higher-order texture features exhibited substantial degradation at extreme count levels (CRF ≥ 50). Harmonization improved feature consistency, particularly for scanner- and resolution-related variations, but had limited impact under severe noise conditions. Taken together, the results indicate that preserving quantitative reliability in low-count PET requires careful consideration of both feature selection and acquisition variability. Rather than relying solely on harmonization, robust radiomics analysis should incorporate count-aware strategies, especially when extending to multi-center or ultra-low-count imaging scenarios.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 212Poster Number:NSS-13-212] A Geant4 add-on package to emulate surface electron response in Monte-Carlo simulation (#3237)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 G. Konstantinou (Autores: G. Konstantinou , S. El Akel , C. Baillif , N. Wyrsch)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] EPFL, PV Lab, Neuchatel, Neuchâtel, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract One of the most complex aspects of understanding and simulating accurately micro-channel plate structures is the accurate estimation of surface response of electron impacts, an integral part of the avalanche driven multiplication process that dictates gain and temporal charge profiles. Electron behavior is heavily affected by the surface quality, roughness, material thickness, deposition process and other details that are difficult to model. For this reason, a lot of groups rely on measurements, which are then introduced in different simulators, such as COMSOL Multiphysics, SimIon or others. Geant4 is the state-of-the-art community-based Monte-Carlo simulation software. Several new physics packages have been introduced over the years to simulate low-energy electron interactions; however, it is very difficult to emulate the entirety of optimizations that can lead to accurate simulation. For this reason we develop an package that allows accurate electron response on surfaces by allowing import of experimental data and is calibrated through an emulation run. The purpose is not to substitute the scatter/back-scatter mechanism that is native to Geant4, but allow light-weight and accurate surface responses to be integrated in full MCP simulations, including multichannel and broad range primary kinetic energies. The model is benchmarked against a fully developed COMSOL model and experimental gain results and tried in various primary scenarios, including direct alpha, beta, beta+ and gamma absorption.

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Traditional dual-energy X-ray cargo inspection systems are limited in thin-material discrimination and detail visibility because low- and high-energy information is mixed within broad bremsstrahlung spectra. This work presents a multi-energy imaging system based on a 6/3/0.3 MeV three-energy accelerator and dual-layer detectors, enabling acquisition of six effective energy channels in a single scan. Experimental results show that the 0.3 MeV channel significantly improves detail resolution, achieving a wire resolution of 0.9 mm. A random forest classifier achieves 92% overall accuracy for four representative materials over a mass-thickness range of 1-120 g/cm2, outperforming a conventional dual-energy configuration by approximately 28%. These results demonstrate that the proposed architecture is a promising solution for high-precision cargo and vehicle inspection.

sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 P. Jones (Autores: P. Jones , S. Hart , M. Johnson , O. Mahgoub , S. Meyer , L. Pellegri , M. Rahman , N. Stodart , G. Taylor , F. van Niekerk , C. van Tubbergh , A. Vanker , S. Woodborne , D. Wyngaard)

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract iThemba LABS has pioneered a mobile gamma-ray detection unit [1] which allows a user to operate in the field and chart the location, strength and energy of gamma radiation. The system incorporates a sensitive scintillation detector [2] typically used for accelerator-based spectroscopy at the SSC laboratory and was integrated into a backpack incorporating a fast 125 MHz digitiser for readout and a GPS enabled Raspberry Pi microprocessor system, allowing in situ measurements of radiation around the Cape Town site, with collected data streamed to the cloud and analysed offline. The Portable African Neutron-Gamma Laboratory for Innovative Nuclear Science (PANGoLINS) project [3] aims to investigate measurements of both gamma rays and neutrons which forms an important component part on site or in transit and the detection of both fissile material for the use in decarbonised energy sources or disposal thereof. A core component of the project is be to miniaturize the weight of the gamma-ray detection device and associated infrastructure so that it can be loaded on an uncrewed aerial vehicle to enable access to, and enhance performance of radiation monitoring measurements at remote sites leading to autonomous operations. PANGoLINS incorporates commercial detector assemblies of LaBr 3 (Ce), SrI 2 (Eu) and/or CLYC(Ce) for spectroscopy. In addition, the project encompasses the instrumentation of other scintillation detectors with silicon photomultiplier technologies. The coupling of these to readout devices such as high-density ADC readout are planned for applications for nuclear science, medical imaging or astronomy.

sub_talks.title: [Poster panel: 218Poster Number:NSS-13-218] Feasibility Study on Ghost Imaging-based Neutron Depth Profiling for 3D Lithium Distribution Mapping (#1125)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Kim (Autores: J. Kim , J. Kim)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute, DAEJEON, Republic of Korea
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the feasibility of three-dimensional lithium distribution mapping in solid-state electrolytes by integrating ghost imaging with neutron depth profiling. In the proposed system, a cold neutron beam is spatially modulated by a sequence of 32×32 Hadamard-patterned cadmium masks, and a single-pixel charged-particle detector records the energy spectrum for each pattern. Since each energy bin corresponds to a specific depth layer via the stopping power, reconstructing a lateral image independently for every energy bin and stacking them along the depth axis produces a complete three-dimensional lithium map without mechanical scanning. Monte Carlo simulations were performed with 1024 mask patterns and 5×10⁸ neutron histories per pattern. Images were reconstructed using an untrained neural network-based algorithm at sampling ratios of 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%. At 100% sampling, the peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index reached 7.5 dB and 0.577, respectively. Although these quantitative scores remain modest due to limited source statistics, the reconstructed images qualitatively resolve the target lithium-rich structures across all depth layers. Compared to conventional pinhole-scanning approaches that require exhaustive spatial sampling, the proposed method would achieve comparable image quality at 50% sampling, directly halving beam time and making three-dimensional characterization practically feasible.
