sub_talks.title: [NSS-17-01] A Configurable Dual-CDL Sigma-Delta Readout Circuit for Dual-Polarity and High-Precision Signal Detection in CsI: Tl SPECT (#2067)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 X. Zhang (Autores: X. Zhang , H. Sabet)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Harvard Medical School, Massachusetts General Hospital, Malden, Massachusetts, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Conventional readout electronics for silicon photomultiplier-coupled cesium iodide scintillation detectors are bulky, costly, and difficult to integrate into compact single-photon emission computed tomography systems. Prior sigma-delta modulation charge-to-digital converter implementations are limited to single-polarity operation or require firmware modification for polarity switching. We propose a configurable dual controlled discharging line sigma-delta readout circuit that simultaneously supports dual-polarity readout and high-precision single-polarity charge integration without firmware or hardware modification. The circuit employs a sigma-delta modulator directly integrating silicon photomultiplier charge, with two controlled discharging lines supporting dual-polarity mode for concurrent handling of both signal polarities, and single-polarity mode for fast baseline recovery and precise charge zeroing. Three CsI :Tl crystal configurations were evaluated against a commercial digitizer using Hamamatsu silicon photomultiplier arrays: a small unprocessed crystal with 22 Na and 137 Cs sources, a monolithic 50×50×8 mm³ crystal with 57 Co, and a laser-processed 25×25 pixel array under collimated and flood irradiation. On the small crystal, energy resolutions of 8.49% and 7.47% at 511 keV and 662 keV. On the monolithic crystal, the proposed circuit achieves 7.88% energy resolution at 122 keV versus 13.86% for the CAEN digitizer, a 1.76-fold improvement. On the laser-processed array, a 9% higher peak-to-valley ratio and superior energy resolution are obtained under collimated irradiation, with cleaner pixel separation under flood irradiation. The proposed dual- CDLs sigma-delta readout circuit outperforms commercial digitizers in energy resolution, event rate, and pixel separability across all configurations, offering a scalable, low-cost solution for next-generation SPECT systems.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-17-02] Design and Preliminary Characterization of a Waveform-Sampling ASIC-Based Readout System for the MASS-Cube CZT Detector (#2596)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 C. Li (Autores: C. Li , F. Sha , X. Zheng , M. Zeng)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Tsinghua University, Department of Engineering Physics, Beijing, China [2] Tsinghua University, Key Laboratory of Particle and Radiation Imaging, Ministry of Education, Beijing, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract MeV gamma-ray astronomy provides an important observational window for studying cosmic nucleosynthesis, compact objects and high-energy transients. The MeV Astrophysical Spectroscopic Surveyor (MASS) is a 3-D position-sensitive CdZnTe (CZT) detector concept proposed for MeV gamma-ray detection. Its pathfinder payload, MASS-Cube, has been launched on September 5, 2025. To further improve the event reconstruction capability of CZT detectors, this work presents a readout system based on a waveform-sampling ASIC for the future upgrades of MASS-Cube. Preliminary test results show that the readout system can reliably acquire signal waveforms from the CZT detector. With a 137 Cs source, FWHM energy resolutions of 1.33% for single-interaction events and 0.69% for single-pixel spectrum were achieved at 662 keV. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed readout chain and provide a foundation for future waveform-based 3-D position reconstruction and imaging optimization.

sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The MALTA2 depleted monolithic active pixel sensor, implemented in 180 nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor imaging technology, has demonstrated hit detection efficiencies of up to 98% after neutron irradiation to 3 × 10¹⁵ 1 MeV n_eq/cm². Measurements at higher fluence motivate further sensor-characterization and test-beam studies, including planned investigations of UHD-modified samples. This contribution presents a new asynchronous oversampling readout developed to support these measurements through more stable sampling of MALTA2 hit signals. The system provides the readout basis for ongoing studies at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron H6 beam line and future beam-test campaigns at KEK.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-17-04] A fully-programmable mixed-signal RISC-V SoC for direct readout of radiation sensors (#3010)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 V. Pagliarino (Autores: V. Pagliarino , L. Borge , A. Dolmeta , S. Durando , L. Giuffrida , E. Manfredi , M. Martina , G. Masera , M. Mignone , V. Piscopo , A. Rivetti , M. D. Da Rocha Rolo)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Politecnico di Torino, Dipartimento di Elettronica (DET), Torino, Italy [2] INFN, Sezione di Torino, Torino, Italy [3] Università degli Studi di Torino, Dipartimento di Fisica, Torino, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract A 6U CubeSat scheduled for launch in March 2027 will be equipped with a payload for in-orbit charged-particle spectroscopy, requiring on-board signal processing and feature extraction to comply with the narrow-band downlink. To satisfy these requirements, while testing and validating in a space environment a novel technology, an FPGA has been installed implementing the digital logic of the MAIA SoC. The solution is currently entering the testing phase. MAIA is a fully-programmable mixed-signal System-on-Chip for readout of particle detectors, targeting a 28 nm CMOS node. Each channel integrates selectable analog front-ends a 320 MSps 10-bit waveform sampling ADC, a programmable DSP for continuous-time signal conditioning, a feature extraction engine and four 1.28 Gbps data links. A global trigger unit with real-time pattern analysis capability is integrated as well. The system control is provided by a multi-core cv32e40p RISC-V CPU with radiation-tolerant lock-step operation support and DMA engine, implementing closed-loop real-time control of the signal processing parameters. A chiplet-compatible architecture enables cost-effective channel scaling and connection to external chips. The encapsulation of the UART and JTAG slow-control interfaces on a full-duplex 320 Mbps 8b10b-encoded data link allow remote control of the SoC when integrated in medium or large-scale experiments. This approach based on high-level of programmability of the signal processing chain can reduce the cost with the respect to producing dedicated front-end ASICs in 110/65 nm for different experiments. All the features of the digital logic of MAIA SoC will be implemented on the satellite FPGA, while the analog front-end and the ADCs will be replaced by the "MIZAR" chip. The payload will be characterized using a particle beam in the next months and the results will be presented at the conference, while the submission of the complete MAIA SoC to the foundry is planned for 2027.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-17-05] The MIZAR ASIC: from mixed-signal design to the PBR mission (#3041)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Di Salvo (Autores: A. Di Salvo , E. Trossarello , M. Bussi , F. Reynaud , M. Abrate , S. Durandetto , R. Wheadon , M. Mignone , A. Rivetti , S. Garbolino , M. E. Bertaina)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] National Institute for Nuclear Physics, Section of Torino, Torino, Italy [2] University of Torino, Department of Physics, Torino, Italy [3] Politecnico di Torino, Department of Electronics, Torino, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The POEMMA Balloon with Radio (PBR) is a NASA's mission to achieve the dual purpose of detecting Ultra-High Energy Cosmic Rays (UHECRs) and performing neutrino astronomy. Planned to operate at stratospheric altitudes, this mission is equipped with two payloads, fluorescence light and Cherenkov light detectors respectively. To detect the latter, a new ASIC was designed in a commercial 65 nm CMOS technology. The Multi-channel Integrated Zone-sampling Analogue-memory based Readout (MIZAR) chip is a 64-channel ASIC developed to read out the signals generated in a tile of Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs). A single channel is made of 256 cells based on analog memories and working at the sampling frequency of 100 MHz. Each cell allows the local digitization of the events using a configurable Wilkinson Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) in the range 8-12 bits. When an event of interest is detected, MIZAR sends out to an FPGA a 64-bit hitmap. This raw information in used as first-level trigger and if it is validated the event is digitized, then the data is serialized through a dedicated Low Voltage Differential Signaling (LVDS) line at 200 MHz in Double Data Rate (DDR). This work describes the scientific context of the PBR mission and the design stages of the MIZAR ASIC. The general results of the test campaign in laboratory are shown, then a focus on the performances in terms of single photo-electron sensitivity and linearity are presented.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-17-06] A Timepix4-based High-Speed Imaging System for Energy-Resolved Neutron Imaging at CSNS (#3077)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Y. Yuan (Autores: H. Liu , Q. Li , Y. Zhou , C. Zhang , H. Guo , W. Gong , Y. Yuan)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Chinese Academy of Sciences, Institute of High Energy Physics, Beijing, China [2] Spallation Neutron Source Science Center, Dongguan, China [3] University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China [4] University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu, China [5] Chinese Academy of Sciences, Purple Mountain Observatory, Nanjing, China [6] University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) is undergoing a beam power upgrade to 500 kW. This upgrade requires new detector readout systems for the Energy-Resolved Neutron Imaging (ERNI) instrument. We present CTPX1, a data-driven camera system based on the Timepix4 ASIC, designed to overcome the 80 Mhits/s bandwidth limit of legacy Timepix3 systems. The CTPX1 integrates a custom high-voltage bias supply with a noise floor below 1 mV, a thermoelectric cooling unit that maintains the sensor temperature within 0.1°C, and a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA-based readout system. The FPGA aggregates sixteen 5.12 Gbps serial links from the ASIC. The system provides a buffered mode for short data bursts up to 81.92 Gbps and a continuous streaming mode up to 64 Gbps via a QSFP+ interface. In high-flux X-ray tests, the system achieved a peak event rate of 1.17 Ghits/s without data loss. During neutron imaging tests at the CSNS BL-20 beamline, using a ⁶LiF/ZnS:Ag scintillator coupled with an image intensifier, the system obtained a spatial resolution of 55 µm. Furthermore, time-of-flight measurements on austenitic stainless steel successfully identified the Bragg edges corresponding to the expected fcc lattice planes. Quantitative energy calibration using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) also showed a highly linear ToT-to-energy relationship. These results indicate that the CTPX1 meets the high-throughput requirements for energy-resolved neutron imaging, making it a suitable candidate for the ERNI upgrade at CSNS-II. Future work will explore its application at high-flux synchrotron light sources, such as HEPS.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-18-01] Fast Neutron Spectrometer for Fusion Diagnostics (#3079)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 F. Retiere (Autores: K. Sharma , F. Retiere)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] a. TRIUMF, 4004 Wesbrook Mall, Vancouver, British Columbia V6T 2A3, Canada, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Advancements in Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) performance in recent years have demonstrated success across a broad range of fields, including particle and nuclear physics, Positron Emission Tomography, Light Detection and Ranging technology, Fusion diagnostics, among others. This work develops a time-of-flight (ToF)-based neutron spectrometer using SiPMs coupled to plastic scintillators as a plasma fusion diagnostic tool. A Deuterium-fueled plasma fusion emits 2.45MeV neutrons with an energy spectrum broadened by ion kinematics. The achievable neutron energy resolution of the spectrometer is correlated to the relative uncertainty on the inferred plasma ion temperature, a critical parameter for evaluating plasma performance and viability of the fusion approach. The target relative uncertainty on temperature is below 20%, therefore constraining the neutron interaction time and position resolution within the spectrometer. A two-layer (L1-L2) detector array is in development at TRIUMF. The detector coupled with fast data acquisition is expected to successfully detect neutrons at GHz rate. Timing-Position resolution of the chosen scintillators (Eljen L1: EJ232Q 0.5% Benzophenone doped; L2: EJ230) paired with Broadcom series AFBR-S4N SiPMs is presented as proof of concept in the neutron energy range of interest. A 511keV-gamma source is used to characterize the timing and position response of a single scintillator-SiPM assembly, incorporating the light yield differences between gamma and neutron interactions accounted for via Birks' law. Techniques and results demonstrating time resolution ranging 60 to 120ps with energy in Layer 1 and preliminary work on Layer 2 will be presented.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-18-02] Pixel Size-Induced Visibility Degradation and Its Mitigation for X-ray Dark-Field Baggage Scanners (#2055)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 Z. Wang (Autores: Z. Wang , P. Guo , J. Tian , L. Men , X. Li , C. Wu , X. Ran , Z. Deng , L. Zhang , Z. Wang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Tsinghua University, Department of Engineering Physics, Beijing, China [2] Science and Technology Research Center of China Customs, Beijing, China [3] Nuctech Company Limited, Beijing, China [4] Technical University of Denmark, Department of Physics, Kongens Lyngby, Denmark
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract X-ray dark-field (DF) imaging enables detection of low-Z scattering materials such as powdered explosives and narcotics, which are indistinguishable in conventional absorption imaging, making it a transformative technology for security screening. However, industrial baggage scanners face an inherent trade-off: high-throughput operation requires large-pixel detectors to capture sufficient photon flux at 160 kV operating voltages, but this causes severe Moiré fringe blurring that fundamentally limits DF sensitivity. In our previous work, we developed a 160 kV dark-field baggage scanner prototype, but found that the 2.7 mm × 3.0 mm large-pixel detectors we used only achieved a fringe visibility of ~7.3% under practical operating conditions, severely limiting DF sensitivity. To address this bottleneck, this study quantitatively investigates pixel size-induced visibility degradation through physics-informed simulations and experimental validation on a benchtop grating interferometry platform. Results confirm the visibility decay trend predicted by the sinc model, and show that a 0.5 mm small-pixel detector achieves ~30% improvement in DF sensitivity for high-energy X-ray dark-field baggage scanners. This work provides critical quantitative guidance for optimizing these systems to improve hazardous material detection.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-18-03] Three-Dimensional Isotopic Imaging via Portable Neutron Resonance Transmission Analysis (#2122)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 K. Sanchez (Autores: K. Sanchez , A. Danagoulian , N. Kowitt)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] MIT, NSE, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Nuclear material safeguards demand portable, isotope specific verification methods capable of operating across diverse deployment contexts. Neutron Resonance Transmission Analysis (NRTA) exploits isotope-specific resonances in neutron cross sections to provide definitive material identification, but portable implementations have been constrained to one-dimensional areal density measurements. Here we present a compact pixelated NRTA system that achieves three-dimensional isotopic imaging through a deuterium-tritium neutron generator, a multi-element GS20 $^6$Li scintillator array, and Algebraic Reconstruction Technique (ART) algorithms. Systematic benchmarking establishes operational limits: maximum target dimensions of 17.5 × 17.5 × 17.5 cm, stand-off distances up to 17.5 cm, spatial resolution of 2.5 cm, and complete three-dimensional reconstruction within four hours using eight measurement angles at 30 minutes per angle. Three-dimensional reconstruction of both homogeneous and non-homogeneous tungsten and silver targets is demonstrated experimentally. This system extends portable NRTA beyond one-dimensional assay, enabling field-deployable isotopic imaging previously available only at large centralized neutron facilities.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-18-04] Neutron diffraction-contrast tomography demonstration using event-based Timepix camera (#2157)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 A. Khaplanov (Autores: A. Khaplanov , K. An , S. Kabra , S. Qian , G. Nagy , C. Zhang)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Oak Ridge National Laboratory, NScD, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, United States of America
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Diffraction contrast tomography is used extensively on x-ray scattering instruments, however, its neutron counterpart has up till now been elusive, in part due to detector limitations. Scintillator-coupled Timepix detectors offer high spatial resolution, event-mode readout, and improved rate capability, making them attractive for neutron scattering and imaging applications. Here we evaluate a LumaCam detector equipped with a TPX3Cam and a ZnO:Zn:6LiF scintillator in a near-field diffraction setup. Scintillation light was focused in a lens onto a 25mm-diameter MCP-based image intensifier. Intensified light was refocused onto a 0.3mm-thick Si sensor with a thin window bonded to a Timepix3 ASIC. Hits were collected in and clusterie to increase position resolution beyond the native pixelation of the ASIC. The detector was placed 10 cm from the sample at 90 degrees to the beam and calibrated using a silicon powder sample. A refractory alloy sample with grains up to 1mm was measured over 180 degrees of rotation. Diffraction spots were assigned to reflections from several crystallographic orientations. By correlating angular separations and relative intensities, 75 grains were identified. Results demonstrate the feasibility of compact grain-resolved neutron diffraction using Timepix camera technology. Irregular spot shapes indicate sensitivity to grain morphology, however, resolution is smeared by beam divergence. Thus, to fully exploit available detector resolution, shorter sample-to-detector distances are currently being explored. Ongoing work combines near-field diffraction with simultaneous transmission imaging to achieve neutron diffraction contrast tomography by relating diffraction spots to grain locations.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-18-05] Associated-Particle Neutron Time-of-Flight Measurements of Curium-244 and Californium-252 (#2360)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Joyce (Autores: A. Parker , M. D. Aspinall , F. Cave , S. Croft , A. Grievson , B. Swinson , M. Joyce)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Lancaster University (Lancaster), School of Engineering, Lancaster, United Kingdom [2] Hybrid Instruments Ltd, Gillow Avenue, Lancaster, United Kingdom [3] Aspinall Instruments, Lancaster, United Kingdom [4] Alpha Safety PSC, Sante Fe, New Mexico, United States of America [5] Mirion Technologies UK Ltd, Warrington, United Kingdom
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract γ-triggered neutron time-of-flight technique was used to measure fast-neutron spectra from spontaneous fission sources using two EJ-309 liquid scintillator detectors operated in coincidence. Prompt γ-ray detection provided the timing reference for neutron energy reconstruction. Measurements were performed using bare 244 Cm and 252 Cf sources, together with a moderated 252 Cf configuration to investigate scattering effects. Time-of-flight spectra were reconstructed into neutron energy distributions with corrections for detector efficiency and the non-linear time-energy relationship, supported by GEANT4 detector-response simulations. The reconstructed spectra were fitted using Maxwellian and Watt functions. Extracted Maxwellian temperatures were 1.89 MeV for bare 252 Cf, 1.41-1.51 MeV for moderated 252 Cf, and 1.48 MeV for 244 Cm, demonstrating the expected spectral softening caused by moderation. Although systematic deviations from literature values were observed due to detector threshold and efficiency limitations, the method successfully resolved relative differences between source configurations. The results demonstrate the suitability of γ-triggered nToF spectrometry for comparative neutron spectral characterisation.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-18-06] Quantitative Contamination Mapping Using an Electron-Tracking Compton Camera for Nuclear Decommissioning (#1819)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 S. Sonoda (Autores: D. Satoh , A. Takada , Y. Koda , S. Sonoda , T. Tanimori)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Japan Atomic Energy Agency, Ibaraki, Japan [2] Kyoto University, Kyoto, Japan [3] ERRAI Corporation, Kyoto, Japan [4] Kitasato University, Kanagawa, Japan
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Quantitative evaluation of radioactive contamination is essential for nuclear decommissioning; however, conventional survey methods provide limited spatial information, and conventional Compton cameras lack quantitative imaging capability due to their non-unique source reconstruction, in which the source position spreads into a cone. In this work, we investigate the applicability of an Electron-Tracking Compton Camera (ETCC) [1] to quantitative gamma-ray imaging in a decommissioning environment. The ETCC consists of a gaseous Time Projection Chamber (TPC) as the scatterer and a pixel scintillator array as the absorber. By reconstructing recoil electron tracks in the TPC, the ETCC uniquely solves the Compton kinematics, enabling a one-to-one correspondence between the source direction and the reconstructed image, in contrast to conventional Compton cameras. Measurements were conducted at the Prototype Advanced Thermal Reactor "FUGEN," currently under decommissioning. A 60 Co hot spot with a dose rate of approximately 1 μSv/h was successfully identified and imaged, and the dose rate estimated from the ETCC data was consistent with that obtained from a survey meter. In addition, weak 60 Co contamination at approximately 0.08 μSv/h, close to the background level and below the sensitivity limit of conventional survey meters, was visualized through direction-resolved analysis. These results demonstrate that the ETCC enables quantitative and sensitive imaging of radioactive contamination and can complement conventional survey methods, with potential to improve the efficiency of contamination assessment and clearance verification in nuclear decommissioning.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-19-01] Status of the Phase-2 Upgrade of the CMS Outer Tracker (#1573)
sub_talks.speaker: M. Tytgat
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Inter-University Institute for High Energies, Brussels, Belgium
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The Silicon Tracker of the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) is the innermost sub-detector, measuring charged particles produced in high-energy collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), and is the world's largest silicon tracking system operational today. The High-Luminosity LHC (HL LHC) will increase luminosity by up to an order of magnitude, delivering 3000-4000 fb⁻¹ of data with up to 200 simultaneous interactions per bunch crossing. To cope with these extreme conditions, CMS will replace its entire tracking system during the Phase-2 Upgrade. The new tracker will feature enhanced radiation tolerance, finer granularity, and extended coverage, significantly improving tracking efficiency, vertex resolution, and momentum measurement. A key innovation is the inclusion of tracking information at the Level-1 trigger. This is enabled by pₜ-modules in the Outer Tracker, each consisting of two closely spaced sensors that correlate hits to identify high-pₜ track candidates in real time. The Outer Tracker will comprise over 13,000 such modules, produced worldwide, with a large-scale production underway since 2025. This contribution will detail the Outer Tracker design and the ongoing module production and integration efforts leading up to the installation and commissioning of the new tracker during the upcoming LHC Long Shutdown 3.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-19-02] Operation and Performance of the ATLAS Liquid Argon Calorimeter During LHC Run 3 (#2118)
sub_talks.speaker: N. Fritzsche
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CERN, Experimental Physics, Geneve, Genève, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The ATLAS Liquid Argon (LAr) calorimeter provides electromagnetic calorimetry for |η|<3.2 and hadronic and forward calorimetry up to |η|=4.9, playing a central role in the reconstruction and triggering of electrons, photons, jets, and missing transverse momentum at the Large Hadron Collider. During LHC Run 3, the detector operated under increased instantaneous luminosity and pileup conditions reaching up to approximately 65 interactions per bunch crossing. A major evolution during this period was the commissioning and operation of the Phase-I Digital Trigger readout system based on longitudinally segmented supercells and real-time FPGA processing. The upgraded trigger path provides finer granularity and improved trigger performance compared to the legacy trigger architecture. In addition, the Digital Trigger enables advanced online detector monitoring and demonstrates strong potential for luminosity measurements using statistical properties of digitized supercell signals. Run 3 data show stable detector operation, excellent trigger-readout agreement, and enhanced trigger efficiency for physics objects.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-19-03] Building the TRISTAN Phase-1 Detector: Characterization of 1000 SDD Pixels (#2158)
sub_talks.speaker: M. Carminati
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] INFN - Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Milano, Milano, Italy [2] Politecnico di Milano, Dipartimento di Elettronica, Informazione e Bioingegneria, Milano, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The TRISTAN detector, an array of 9 modules based on monolithic arrays of 166 Silicon Drift Detectors (SDD) pixels is being realized for high accuracy (1 ppm) beta spectroscopy. It will be installed in the KATRIN focal plane by the end of 2026 in order to extend the use of the KATRIN Tritium facility for searching the sterile neutrino in the keV mass range. Each detection module is 4-side buttable and has an area of 4 by 4 cm 2 . Here, the progress in detectors assembly is reported. Currently, more than 25 modules have been realized and tested, allowing to select the best 7 modules, out of the final set of 9. They are being characterized in a chamber replicating the operating conditions in terms of vacuum, electric and magnetic fields. Out of the final target value of 1494 pixels, currently a total of 981 pixels are operational, making this system the largest array of spectroscopic SDD detectors ever commissioned. The challenges of this phase are mostly related to production yield and reliability of the complex assembly phase. All pixels show an average FWHM energy resolution below 300 eV for electrons of 20 keV.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-19-04] Detector Performance Results on the MOSAIX Stitched Sensor Structures for ALICE ITS3 (#2617)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 L. Terlizzi (Autores: H. Hillemanns , L. Terlizzi)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CERN, Geneva, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The ALICE collaboration is currently developing a new vertex detector ("ITS3"), scheduled for installation in 2028 - 2029 during LHC long shutdown 3 to replace the three innermost layers (Inner Barrel) of the existing Inner Tracking System as from Run 4 onwards. ITS3 comprises the use of ultra-thin (down to 50 micrometers) silicon wafers and stitching technologies in 65nm CMOS imaging process , enabling the production of large area (9.8cm x 26.7cm) Monolithic Active Pixels Sensors sensors which will be bent to half-cylindrical shapes of 19, 25.2 and 31.5 mm bending radii for layer 0, 1 and 2 respectively, and supported by carbon foam structures. The very low power consumption of about 40mV/cm 2 allows for air cooling, and the bent shape allows for a minimum of mechanical support using carbon foam only. The very low material budget of less than 0.09% of a radiation length per layer ensures extremely good tracking and vertexing performance. Following an extensive R\&D program for the ITS3, large area stitched prototype structures (MOSAIX) with a final pixel pitch of 20.8µm x 22.8µm, matrix sizes and all other features have been produced and will be tested throughout this year before and after irradiation with TID and NIEL in order to validate the final design for production. In this contribution we present and discuss an overview of detection performance measurements in various test beams.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-19-05] The LHCb PicoCal: a New Radiation-hard ECAL with Picosecond Time Resolution (#2732)
sub_talks.speaker: E. Picatoste
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Universitat de Barcelona, Institute of Cosmos Science of the University of Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract The LHCb Upgrade II program aims to operate at an instantaneous luminosity of up to 1.0x10 34 cm −2 s −1 , during the High-Luminosity LHC Run 5, targeting an integrated dataset of 300 fb −1 . This ambitious goal requires a complete redesign of the electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL), leading to the development of the PicoCal detector. The upgrade addresses the challenges of extreme pile-up, high particle densities, and severe radiation levels-reaching up to 1 MGy in the innermost regions-by introducing enhanced transverse granularity and precision timing capabilities at the level of O(10) picoseconds. The PicoCal design combines different technologies optimized for distinct detector regions. The central, high-radiation zones will employ Spaghetti Calorimeter (SpaCal) modules, based on dense absorbers coupled with fast scintillating materials. The outer regions will be instrumented with upgraded Shashlik calorimeters with fast wavelength-shifting fibers to improve timing performance. Extensive R&D efforts have focused on scintillators, photodetectors, and front-end electronics, with several photomultiplier tube (PMT) candidates evaluated for their timing precision and radiation tolerance. Prototype modules of both SpaCal and Shashlik technologies have been successfully designed, constructed, and tested. Test beam campaigns demonstrate that the calorimeter achieves an energy resolution with a stochastic term of about 10% sampling contribution and 1% constant term, while timing resolutions better than 20 ps are achieved at high energies across different scintillator options. In parallel, the SPIDER ASIC prototype has been validated in beam tests, achieving timing performance comparable to standard digitizer-based readout systems. These results collectively demonstrate that the PicoCal concept meets the stringent performance requirements of LHCb Upgrade II, ensuring precise energy and time measurements under extreme HL-LHC conditions.

sub_talks.title: [NSS-19-06] digital SiPMs for future RICH detectors (#2857)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 P. Singh (Autores: P. Singh , R. Dolenec , C. Bruschini , E. Charbon)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] EPFL, STI IEM AQUA, Neuchatel, Neuchâtel, Switzerland [2] Jozef Stefan Institute, Experimental Particle Physics Department, Ljubljana, Slovenia
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Planned upgrades to Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) detectors in the LHCb, Belle II, and ALICE 3 high energy physics experiments require photodetectors capable of single-photon detection at high event rates and neutron fluences up to a few 10¹³ 1-MeV equivalent/cm². The spadRICH project develops a CMOS-based single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) array optimized for radiation hardness and cryogenic operation to meet these requirements. This paper presents a decision-maker (DM) circuit architecture for use in digital silicon photomultiplier (dSiPM) readout. The DM identifies the first-firing SPAD along with its address among competing channels and disables both the winning and losing SPADs immediately after the decision, thus suppressing subsequent avalanches. Combined with fast quenching, this reduces afterpulsing and lowers power consumption in multi-channel readout - critical for operation in high-radiation cryogenic environments. The DM can be cascaded into a binary tree topology to implement full dSiPM functionality. dSiPMs with varying aspect ratios and SPAD sizes are fabricated in the GlobalFoundries 55 nm BCDLite® process. In addition to dSiPMs, we have also implemented analog SiPMs (aSiPMs) to compare the advantage of its high fill factor with selective deactivation of SPADs and time-gating features of dSiPMs in high radiation environments.

sub_talks.title: [RTSD-08-01] The Timepix ASIC Family: Past, Present, and Future (#3005)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 R. Ballabriga (Autores: R. Ballabriga , X. Llopart , M. Campbell)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] CERN, Meyrin, Switzerland
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This summary reviews the evolution of the Timepix family of hybrid pixel detector readout ASICs, from Timepix in 2006 through to the recently released Timepix4 and the forthcoming Picopix demonstrator. The early versions had a regular matrix of 256x256 pixels. Each generation introduced an architectural innovation: per-pixel programmable Time-of-Arrival (ToA) or Time-over-Threshold (ToT) mode selection (Timepix, 250 nm MOS, 2006, Medipix2 Collaboration); data-driven triggerless readout with simultaneous time and energy measurement (ToA/ToT) and a 1.56 ns on-pixel TDC (Timepix3,130 nm CMOS, 2013, Medipix3 Collaboration); simultaneous ToA/ToT with logarithmic gain mode, improved energy resolution, and dead-time-free continuous read/write (Timepix2,130 nm CMOS, 2018, Medipix2 Collaboration); and 195 ps ToA binning over a four-side buttable 448x512 matrix using through-silicon via (TSV) technology (Timepix4, 65 nm CMOS, 2019, Medipix4 Collaboration). The forthcoming Picopix (28 nm CMOS, submission foreseen in 2026) targets ∼35 ps ToA binning with on-pixel clustering, on-chip time calibration, and packet sorting. Key quantitative parameters-timing resolution, hit rate, active area, power consumption, and readout bandwidth-are compared across all five generations. Representative applications and the knowledge-transfer impact of the Medipix Collaborations model are discussed.

sub_talks.title: [RTSD-08-02] Timepix4 based photon-counting detector for full-spectral X-ray micro computed tomography (#1355)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 P. Cardarelli (Autores: P. Cardarelli , N. V. Biesuz , F. Brun , V. Cavallini , P. Delogu , A. Feruglio , M. Fiorini , R. Longo , V. Mazzini , P. Oliva , V. Rosso , S. Velardita , L. Brombal)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] INFN, Ferrara Division, Ferrara, Italy [2] INFN, Trieste Division, Trieste, Italy [3] Università di Trieste, Dipartimento di Ingegneria e Architettura, Trieste, Italy [4] Università di Trieste, Dipartimento di Fisica, Trieste, Italy [5] Università di Ferrara, Dipartimento di Fisica e Scienze della Terra, Ferrara, Italy [6] Università di Pisa, Dipartimento di Fisica, Pisa, Italy [7] INFN, Pisa Division, Pisa, Italy
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Timepix4 is the latest generation of the readout ASIC developed by the Medipix4 Collaboration for hybrid pixel detector technology, featuring a 448 x 512 matrix with a 55 μm pitch. Operating in data-driven mode, it provides simultaneous Time of Arrival (ToA) and Time over Threshold (ToT) information for each hit. This allows for multi-pixel signal clustering to mitigate charge sharing and fluorescence escape, while calibrated ToT values provide per-pixel energy measurement. Such capabilities enable high-resolution X-ray spectral imaging, providing accurate energy deposition information for each detected event and greater post-processing flexibility compared to traditional threshold-based photon-counting systems. In this work, we present the first full-spectral micro-CT images acquired with a Timepix4-based detector operating in data-driven mode. The detector is equipped with a 1 mm-thick CdTe sensor, making it suitable for X-ray energies commonly used in biomedical applications. Tomographic scans were performed at the INFN PEPI laboratory using a microfocus X-ray tube (80 kV, 20 μA). The study evaluated a custom plastic phantom containing three distinct contrast agents: silver, iodine, and gadolinium. Projections were acquired over 360° with a reconstructed voxel size of 33 μm. The resulting 3D attenuation spectra were processed using a basis material decomposition algorithm, producing independent 3D density maps for each contrast agent. The results confirm the feasibility of full-spectral micro-CT imaging using the Timepix4 ASIC, demonstrating its ability to capture 3D attenuation spectra at high spatial resolution. While data rate management remains a challenge, the ability to resolve full attenuation spectra in 3D enables precise multi-material identification in a single scan. This capability offers significant potential for advanced applications in biomedical research and materials science.

sub_talks.title: [RTSD-08-03] Machine learning pipeline for spectral material identification with a CdTe-Timepix3 detector (#1932)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. S. Useche Parra (Autores: J. S. Useche Parra , M. Schütz , G. Roque , S. Procz , M. Fiederle)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] University of Freiburg, Freiburg Material Research Center, Freiburg, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract X-ray imaging systems are widely used in industries such as homeland security, non-destructive testing, archaeological research, and medicine, where accurate material identification is often essential. Examples include explosives screening in airport luggage, product quality testing on a production line, and content characterization in historical manuscripts. Photon-counting detectors provide high spatial and energy resolution, along with full spectroscopic information on a per-event basis, and are therefore well suited for machine learning (ML) approaches to material identification. One example of such a detector is the Timepix3, which records single events at fluxes up to 40 Mhits/cm 2 /s. Previous work, presented at this conference, demonstrated the feasibility of training an ML classifier (Gradient-Boosted Trees) on measured X-ray spectra acquired with a 12x1 Timepix3 (bump-bonded to 1 mm CdTe) detector and reported initial identification results on a multi-material phantom. This contribution extends that work, addressing two limitations of its results: the restricted size of the experimental material database and the lack of quantitative model diagnostics. The database is supplemented with simulated spectra (generated with the Allpix Squared framework) for materials that are difficult to obtain as pure reference samples, and the consistency between simulated and measured data is assessed. The extended database is then used to retrain the classifier, and standard ML diagnostics are reported to characterize model behavior. The performance of this approach will be compared to classical techniques such as base-material decomposition.

sub_talks.title: [RTSD-08-04] Full Scale Microstructural Imaging Based on Energy dispersive X-ray Diffraction using Timepix3/4 with CdTe Sensor (#2737)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 J. Jakubek (Autores: J. Jakubek , R. Nebel , J. Volny , D. Vavrik)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] ADVACAM s.r.o., Prague, Czech Republic [2] Institute of Theoretical and Applied Mechanics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, Czech Republic
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract This contribution extends the technique of the fast energy dispersive X-ray diffraction (XRD) in transmission mode for inspection of macroscopic objects, as described in our previous work [1], published recently by Nature Scientific Reports. This technique utilizes the event-based registration of diffracted X-ray photons with simultaneous timing and energy information as provided by Timepix3/4 detectors. It enables rapid diffraction measurements with a polychromatic X-ray source, eliminating the need for mechanical angular scanning while preserving spatially resolved structural information. Current XRD systems utilize relatively low-energy monochromatic X-ray beam (5-20 keV) which can only penetrate shallow layer close to the sample surface. Therefore, thick or dense parts cannot be analyzed through their entire volume using standard approaches. An alternative is the use of synchrotron sources, however, these are generally impractical for industrial applications. A hard polychromatic X-ray source (X-ray tube) in combination with spectrally sensitive imaging detector such as Timepix3 or Timepix4 equipped with high-Z sensor (CdTe or CZT) overcomes above listed limits. This work focuses on optimizing detector performance by suppressing unwanted effects such as internal X-ray fluorescence and charge-sharing. Both of these effects degrade energy resolution, which directly impacts the quality of recorded XRD data. It will be demonstrated that an optimized detector, together with an event-sorting algorithm, can provide high-quality XRD data within a fraction of a second. Such speed enables 2D scanning across the entire volume of the inspected sample. [1] Vavrik, D., Georgiev, V., Jakubek, J. et al. Transmission energy dispersive X-ray diffraction as a tool for the laboratory study of fast processes in metals. Sci Rep 15 , 31752 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-16314-9

sub_talks.title: [RTSD-08-05] Energy-resolved Grating-based Phase-contrast Imaging with Timepix4 (#2862)
sub_talks.speaker: 🎤 M. Schneider (Autores: M. Schneider , G. Anton , B. Bergmann , P. Burian , T. Čelko , P. Mánek , S. Pospíšil , C. Rauch , M. Rongen , P. Smolyanskiy , S. Funk)
sub_talks.affiliation: [1] Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, Erlangen Centre for Astroparticle Physics, Erlangen, Germany [2] Czech Technical University in Prague, Institute for Experimental and Applied Physics, Prague, Czech Republic
sub_talks.abstract: Abstract Grating-based phase-contrast imaging (gbPCI) is a powerful tool for non-destructive testing and material analysis. In conventional X-ray imaging, only the attenuation of the X-rays is measured, resulting in low contrast between structures with similar absorption characteristics. With gbPCI, it is possible to not only get information about the absorption, but also the phase-shift of X-rays when propagating through material. For non-destructive testing and material analysis, the dark-field image provides complementary information, since it is sensitive to structures below the resolution limit of the system, which is primarily given by the pixel sizes of the detector. The pixel pitch is typically 50 μm or higher. With the dark-field image, it is possible to see porous or fibrous structures and estimate their sizes. A photon-counting and energy-resolving Timepix4 detector is used in this work. By setting energy cuts, the sensitivity range can be maximized, allowing a more detailed structural analysis. Additionally, the quality of the imaging system can be improved by cutting unwanted energies. First test measurements with Timepix4 have shown the feasibility of phase-contrast imaging with this detector, by acquiring energy-resolved dark-field images of lycopodium spores and a piece of wood.
